summary: Checkpoints 1–2 (Claude Code cc-39fac3). NE.1 is source_decomposed (CFKSV §§2–3, Burns–Venjakob §2). NE.2 is partial after checkpoint 2: CFKSV §§3–4 — the localisation sequence, the boundary map, surjectivity of ∂_G, characteristic elements with their ambiguity, semilocality of Λ(G)_S and units surjecting onto K₁, and the commutative comparison. NE.0 is partial (Lazard's noetherian theorem, finite global dimension; uniform-group theory unowned). NE.3–NE.7 are not read. Checkpoint 3 (cc-39fac3) plans NE.3 from CFKSV §3: twists, the homomorphism Φ_ρ, evaluation at representations, Akashi series, the evaluation–Akashi diagram, the Euler characteristic formula (Theorem 3.6), Artin representations (Theorem 3.8), the Artin formalism (Theorem 3.10) and the X₁(11) example. Reduced norms and SK₁ remain. Checkpoint 4 (cc-39fac3) plans CFKSV §4's integrality conjecture 4.8 with Lemma 4.9 (NE.3) and §5: the dual Selmer module, Conjectures 5.1–5.2 and the 𝔐_H(G) criteria (NE.4), and Conjectures 5.7–5.8 with Corollaries 5.9–5.10 and the X₁(11) check (NE.5). Conjectures are stated as propositions, never assumed. Checkpoint 5 reads Kakde §§1–4: admissible extensions and μ = 0, the complex C(F_∞/F), SK₁ and K′₁, ∂ surjective with p-torsion, the totally real main conjecture, the abelian × prime-to-p case from Deligne–Ribet and Wiles, the Burns–Kato patching principle, and the reductions to dimension one, to ℚ_p-elementary groups, the l-elementary case and the reduction to Δ × pro-p. Checkpoint 6 (cc-39fac3) reads Kakde §5 and §6.1: Λ_𝒪(G) as a twisted group ring over Λ_𝒪(Z), the congruence groups Φ^G, the additive theorem R[Conj Ḡ]^τ ≅ ψ^G, the logarithm on relative K₁ and the integral logarithm, the relation between θ^G and β^G, Theorems 52–53 (K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) ≅ Φ^G), Corollary 90, and the reduction of the main conjecture to (ζ_P) ∈ Φ^G_S with M1–M2 proved. Checkpoint 7 (cc-39fac3) completes the Kakde route: Kakde §§6.2–6.13 — Deligne–Ribet approximations, the basic congruences via Hilbert Eisenstein series and the q-expansion principle, M4 through the enlarged extension, Theorem 94, and Theorem 11 (the main conjecture for totally real fields, p odd, μ = 0). Findings E5–E10. Checkpoint 8 (cc-39fac3) starts NE.7 from Burns–Venjakob §§2–4: the determinant functor and localized K₁ (NE.2), Bockstein maps, semisimplicity, leading terms and their characteristic-series and cyclotomic-derivative interpretations, generalized Euler characteristics, and the Fukaya–Kato zeta isomorphism as a proposition; finding E11. Checkpoint 9 (cc-39fac3) completes Burns–Venjakob in NE.7 (§5 Tate motives, §6 critical motives).

nodes.title: The lower p-series
nodes.statement: For a pro-p group G put P₁(G) = G and P_{i+1}(G) = the closure of P_i(G)^p [P_i(G), G], the subgroup generated by p-th powers of P_i(G) and commutators [P_i(G), G]. The P_i(G) are closed characteristic subgroups, decreasing, with ⋂_i P_i(G) = 1 for a finitely generated pro-p group G.
hypotheses: G a pro-p group (Tau Ceti's TauCeti.IsProP); closures are taken in G.
proofSteps: Define P_{i+1} as the topological closure of the subgroup generated by {x^p : x ∈ P_i} ∪ [P_i, G].
Characteristic: every continuous automorphism preserves p-th powers and commutators, hence each P_i.
Separation for finitely generated G: P_i(G) is open for all i and the P_i are cofinal among open normal subgroups (Ardakov–Brown §2.4, citing Dixon–du Sautoy–Mann–Segal §7.1).
acceptance: For G = ℤ_p^d: P_i(G) = p^{i−1}ℤ_p^d.
For p = 2 the powerful condition uses G⁴, not G²; keep the lower p-series itself unchanged.

uses.how: the index condition |P_i : P_{i+1}| = |G : P₂|.
the filtration defining the graded ring of Ω(G).

nodes.title: Uniform pro-p groups
nodes.statement: A pro-p group G is powerful if G/G^p is abelian (p odd), resp. G/G⁴ is abelian (p = 2), where G^p is the closed subgroup generated by p-th powers; G is uniform if it is powerful, finitely generated, and |G : P₂(G)| = |P_i(G) : P_{i+1}(G)| for all i ≥ 1. The dimension of a uniform G is d with |G : P₂(G)| = p^d; it is the minimal number of topological generators.
hypotheses: G pro-p, with its lower p-series.
proofSteps: Define powerful through the quotient by the closed subgroup generated by p-th powers (fourth powers at p = 2).
Define uniform as the conjunction of powerful, topologically finitely generated and the constant-index condition.
acceptance: ℤ_p^d is uniform of dimension d; the first congruence subgroup Γ₁(GL_d(ℤ_p)) (p odd) is uniform.
ℤ/p is powerful but not uniform (indices p, 1).

nodes.title: Compact p-adic analytic groups
nodes.statement: A compact p-adic analytic (compact p-adic Lie) group is a profinite group G that has an open normal subgroup U which is a uniform pro-p group. Equivalently (Lazard; Dixon–du Sautoy–Mann–Segal Corollary 8.34): G is profinite with an open pro-p subgroup of finite rank; or G is a p-adic analytic manifold group; or G is a closed subgroup of some GL_d(ℤ_p). The dimension of G is the dimension of any open uniform subgroup.
hypotheses: The group-theoretic characterisation is taken as the definition; the equivalence with analytic manifold groups is recorded as a gap (Lazard's theorem has no owner in the atlas).
proofSteps: Package: profinite (compact, Hausdorff, totally disconnected) topological group with ∃ U open normal, pro-p and uniform.

Closure properties used later: open subgroups, closed normal subgroups and quotients by closed normal subgroups of compact p-adic analytic groups are compact p-adic analytic (Ardakov–Brown §2.1, citing Dixon–du Sautoy–Mann–Segal).
acceptance: Finite groups, ℤ_p^d × (finite), GL_d(ℤ_p), SL_d(ℤ_p) and their congruence subgroups are examples.
Separate: 'no element of order p', 'torsion-free' and 'pro-p' are different hypotheses (ℤ_p × ℤ/ℓ for ℓ ≠ p has no element of order p but is not pro-p; ℤ_p ⋊ ℤ/p may have p-torsion).

sources.match: The characterisation used as the definition.

nodes.title: Completed group algebras are free over open subgroups
nodes.statement: Let G be profinite and H′ ≤ H closed subgroups with H′ open in H. Then Λ(H) is a free left (and right) Λ(H′)-module of rank [H : H′], with basis any set of right (resp. left) coset representatives; likewise Ω(H) over Ω(H′). If H′ is open normal in H, Λ(H) ≅ Λ(H′) ∗ (H/H′) is a crossed product. Consequently a Λ(H)-module is finitely generated over Λ(H) iff it is finitely generated over Λ(H′).
hypotheses: Λ(−) = ℤ_p⟦−⟧, Ω(−) = F_p⟦−⟧, the completed group algebras of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1.
proofSteps: Compute Λ(H) as lim ℤ_p[H/V] over open normal V ≤ H′ of H; at each level ℤ_p[H/V] is free over ℤ_p[H′/V] on coset representatives; the bases are compatible, so the limit is free on the same set.
Finite generation transfers because Λ(H) is finite free over Λ(H′).
acceptance: The basis is a set of coset representatives, independent of the level V.

sources.locator: Chap. II, (2.2.7), p. 62 (Numdam PDF; printed page = PDF page + 3)
sources.match: Lazard: coset representatives form a basis of Λ(G) over Λ(U).

nodes.title: Iwasawa algebras of pro-p groups are local
nodes.statement: For a pro-p group G, Λ(G) is a compact local ring whose maximal ideal is the kernel of Λ(G) → F_p (reduction of the augmentation), and its open ideals form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0; likewise Ω(G) with maximal ideal the augmentation ideal. For G compact p-adic analytic, Λ(G) and Ω(G) are semilocal, and local iff G is pro-p.
hypotheses: G pro-p for the first statement; compact p-adic analytic for the equivalence.
proofSteps: For G finite p-group, the augmentation ideal of F_p[G] is nilpotent, so 1 + (augmentation ideal) consists of units; pass to the limit: every element of Λ(G) with unit image in F_p is a unit (geometric series converge).
If G is not pro-p, some finite quotient G/U has order divisible by a prime ℓ ≠ p or is not a p-group, and F_p[G/U] has more than one simple module; Λ(G) is then not local.
Semilocal: Λ(G) is a crossed product of Λ(U) (U open normal pro-p) by a finite group, whose Jacobson radical contains that of Λ(U).
acceptance: CFKSV use this for J pro-p to apply Nakayama's lemma to Λ(J)-modules.
Test: Λ(ℤ/ℓ) = ℤ_p[ℤ/ℓ] for ℓ ≠ p splits as a product of local rings, not local.

sources.locator: §2, p. 166 (Numdam PDF of the published article; printed page = PDF page + 162)
sources.match: The maximal ideal as CFKSV use it.

nodes.title: The graded ring of Ω(G) for uniform G
nodes.statement: Let G be uniform of dimension d with topological generators a₁, …, a_d and b_i = a_i − 1 ∈ Ω(G). Every element of Ω(G) is uniquely a convergent series Σ_{α∈ℕ^d} c_α b^α (c_α ∈ F_p) (the PBW theorem), the Jacobson radical J is generated by b₁, …, b_d on either side, Ω(G) is complete for the J-adic filtration, and gr_J Ω(G) ≅ F_p[X₁, …, X_d]. The analogue for Λ(G) has gr ≅ F_p[X₀, X₁, …, X_d] (X₀ from p).
hypotheses: G uniform; the ordering of the b_i is fixed (Ω(G) is noncommutative).
proofSteps: The P_i(G) are cofinal with open normal subgroups and the powers of the augmentation ideal are cofinal with the ideals generated by the augmentation ideals of the P_i(G) (Ardakov–Brown Theorem 2.4), so Ω(G) is the J-adic completion of F_p[G].

Uniformity makes each P_i/P_{i+1} ≅ F_p^d with P_i generated by a_j^{p^{i−1}}; the monomials b^α with |α| weighted by the lower p-series give an F_p-basis of each filtration quotient (Dixon–du Sautoy–Mann–Segal Theorem 7.23).
Hence gr_J Ω(G) is generated by the classes of the b_i, which commute modulo higher filtration, and the PBW basis shows they are algebraically independent (Dixon–du Sautoy–Mann–Segal Theorem 7.24).
acceptance: Test on G = ℤ_p: Ω(ℤ_p) = F_p⟦b⟧ and gr = F_p[X].
The Lie bracket of b_i, b_j is in general an infinite series; only its leading term vanishes in gr.

nodes.title: Complete filtrations with noetherian graded ring
nodes.statement: Let R be a ring with an exhaustive separated filtration (F_iR)_{i∈ℤ} that is complete. If gr R is left (right) noetherian then R is left (right) noetherian; such a filtration is Zariskian, and R inherits from gr R being a domain, being prime and having finite global dimension.
hypotheses: Complete: Cauchy sequences for the filtration topology converge uniquely.
proofSteps: Given a left ideal I, the ideal gr I of gr R is finitely generated; lift homogeneous generators to x₁, …, x_n ∈ I.
Completeness and separation give I = Σ R x_i by successive approximation of any element of I (standard filtered Nakayama argument).
acceptance: State both sides; Iwasawa algebras are noncommutative.
Only noetherianity is needed for NE.1; the inherited homological properties are recorded for NE.2.

sources.match: Complete filtrations with noetherian gr are Zariskian.

nodes.title: Lazard's noetherian theorem
nodes.statement: For a compact p-adic analytic group G, Λ(G) = ℤ_p⟦G⟧ and Ω(G) = F_p⟦G⟧ are left and right noetherian complete semilocal rings; for G pro-p they are local (Lazard V.2.2.4). The same holds for O⟦G⟧ = O ⊗_{ℤ_p} Λ(G), O the integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p.
hypotheses: G compact p-adic analytic.
proofSteps: Choose an open normal uniform subgroup U; gr Ω(U) ≅ F_p[X₁, …, X_d] is noetherian (Hilbert), and the J-adic filtration is complete, so Ω(U) is noetherian by zariskian-noetherian; similarly Λ(U) with gr ≅ F_p[X₀, …, X_d].
Λ(G) is a finitely generated free module over Λ(U) on either side, so it is left and right noetherian.
O⟦G⟧ is finite free over Λ(G).
acceptance: CFKSV cite this as 'well known'; it is used for the ascending chain argument of Proposition 2.3.
Finite global dimension is not asserted when G has p-torsion.

sources.match: Lazard's theorem for pro-p analytic G.

nodes.title: Nakayama's lemma for compact modules over Λ(J)
nodes.statement: Let J be a pro-p group, 𝔪_J the maximal ideal of Λ(J), and M a compact (Hausdorff, linearly topologised) Λ(J)-module, for instance a quotient of a finitely generated Λ(G)-module for J ≤ G closed. Then M is finitely generated over Λ(J) iff M/𝔪_J M is finite iff the coinvariants M_J are a finitely generated ℤ_p-module; and M = 0 iff M/𝔪_J M = 0.
hypotheses: Compactness of M is essential (ℚ_p as a Λ(ℤ_p)-module with trivial action has M/𝔪M = 0).
proofSteps: Lazard II.2.2.2: every neighbourhood of 0 in Λ(J) contains 𝔪_J^n for large n, so for compact M the submodules 𝔪_J^n M shrink to 0.
If P is compact with 𝔪_J P = P then P = 𝔪_J^n P for all n, hence P = 0.
Lift generators of M/𝔪_J M to x₁, …, x_r; N = Σ Λ(J)x_i is compact, hence closed, and P = M/N satisfies 𝔪_J P = P.
M_J/p M_J = M/𝔪_J M because 𝔪_J is generated by p and the augmentation ideal.
acceptance: Record the compactness hypothesis explicitly in every application (CFKSV Lemma 2.1, Proposition 2.3).

sources.locator: §2, p. 166 (Numdam PDF of the published article; printed page = PDF page + 162)
sources.match: CFKSV's use of the lemma; the proof here follows from Lazard II.2.2.2.

nodes.title: Finite global dimension without p-torsion
nodes.statement: If the compact p-adic analytic group G of dimension d has no element of order p, then Λ(G) (and Λ_𝒪(G)) has finite global dimension d + 1 on either side; in particular every finitely generated Λ(G)-module has a finite resolution by finitely generated projective modules.
hypotheses: No element of order p is essential: ℤ_p[ℤ/p] has infinite global dimension.
proofSteps: cd_p(G) = d for G without p-torsion (Lazard V.2.2.3 for p-valued groups, Serre's theorem that cd_p is inherited by open subgroups when there is no p-torsion).

Brumer: for a pro-p (or virtually pro-p) group without p-torsion, gl.dim Λ(G) = cd_p(G) + 1 (minimal resolutions of ℤ_p over the local ring Λ(U), then Serre's theorem for the finite extension Λ(G) ⊃ Λ(U)).
acceptance: Brumer's paper (J. Algebra 1966) and Serre's cd theorem are not freely available; the node records the route through Lazard's minimal complexes (V.2.2.5), read on Numdam.

sources.locator: §3, p. 174 (Numdam PDF page 12; printed page = PDF page + 162)

nodes.title: The canonical Ore set S
nodes.statement: Let G be a compact p-adic analytic group with a closed normal subgroup H such that G/H ≅ ℤ_p. The canonical set is S = {f ∈ Λ(G) : Λ(G)/Λ(G)f is finitely generated as a left Λ(H)-module}. With O-coefficients, S_O is defined in the same way with Λ_O(G), Λ_O(H).
hypotheses: No hypothesis of 'no element of order p' is needed for S itself; CFKSV assume it only for later sections.
Abstractly: for a ring A that is a left B-module through left multiplication, S = {f : A/Af finitely generated over B}.
proofSteps: Define S by the finiteness condition on the cyclic module Λ(G)/Λ(G)f.
By iwasawa-free-over-open-subgroup, H may be replaced by any open subgroup of H in the definition.
acceptance: For H = 1, G = Γ ≅ ℤ_p: Λ(Γ)/Λ(Γ)f is finitely generated over ℤ_p iff f ≠ 0 and p ∤ f (Weierstrass), so S = Λ(Γ) ∖ pΛ(Γ).
Never replace S by the set of all nonzero divisors: localisation at all nonzero elements is neither defined in general nor equal to Λ(G)_S.

nodes.title: A central copy of ℤ_p in G/J
nodes.statement: Let H ◁ G closed with G/H ≅ ℤ_p and J ≤ H open, normal in G. Then G/J contains a subgroup Π ≅ ℤ_p that is open, central, and maps isomorphically onto an open subgroup of Γ = G/H; hence Ω(Π) ≅ F_p⟦T⟧ is a discrete valuation ring in the centre of Ω(G/J), and Λ(Π) ≅ ℤ_p⟦T⟧.
hypotheses: J open in H (so H/J is finite) and normal in G.
proofSteps: Lift a topological generator of Γ to γ ∈ G/J; then G/J = (H/J) ⋊ ⟨γ⟩̄ with ⟨γ⟩̄ ≅ ℤ_p.
⟨γ⟩̄ acts on the finite group H/J by conjugation through a finite quotient, so an open subgroup Π = ⟨γ^{p^k}⟩̄ acts trivially; Π commutes with H/J and with ⟨γ⟩̄, hence is central.
Ω(Π) ≅ F_p⟦T⟧ by the power-series coordinate of ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 9.
acceptance: Π is central in G/J, not in G.
Test: G = ℤ_p ⋊ ℤ_p acting by a unit u ≠ 1 with H = ℤ_p: Π = ⟨γ^{p^k}⟩ with u^{p^k} ≡ 1 mod |H/J|.

nodes.title: The algebra V(G/J)
nodes.statement: With Π as in central-zp-subgroup and R(Π) = Frac Ω(Π) ≅ F_p((T)), put V(G/J) = R(Π) ⊗_{Ω(Π)} Ω(G/J). It is a finite-dimensional algebra over the central field R(Π); Ω(G/J) → V(G/J) is injective; and for x ∈ Ω(G/J), right multiplication by x on V(G/J) is injective iff surjective iff x is a unit of V(G/J), and the same holds on the left.
hypotheses: Ω(G/J) is a finite free Ω(Π)-module (iwasawa-free-over-open-subgroup), of rank [G/J : Π].
proofSteps: V(G/J) = R(Π)^{[G/J:Π]} as an R(Π)-vector space; left and right multiplications are R(Π)-linear because R(Π) is central.
Linear algebra: an injective endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space is surjective.
If x z = 1 in V then z x = 1 (finite-dimensional algebra), which gives the left–right symmetry used in Lemma 2.2.
acceptance: V(G/J) is not a division ring in general (G/J may be nonabelian with zero divisors in Ω(G/J)).

uses.how: criterion (iii): injectivity of right multiplication.
the left–right symmetry z α_J(f) = 1 ⇔ α_J(f) z = 1.

nodes.title: Criteria for membership in S (left)
nodes.statement: Let J ≤ H be pro-p, open in H and normal in G, with φ_J : Λ(G) → Λ(G/J) and ψ_J : Λ(G) → Ω(G/J). For f ∈ Λ(G) the following are equivalent: (i) f ∈ S; (ii) Λ(G/J)/Λ(G/J)φ_J(f) is a finitely generated ℤ_p-module; (iii) Ω(G/J)/Ω(G/J)ψ_J(f) is finite; (iv) right multiplication by ψ_J(f) on Ω(G/J) is injective.
hypotheses: J pro-p, open in H, normal in G (such J exist and are cofinal).
proofSteps: For M = Λ(G)/Λ(G)f: M_J = Λ(G/J)/Λ(G/J)φ_J(f) and M/𝔪_J M = Ω(G/J)/Ω(G/J)ψ_J(f); (i) ⇔ (ii) ⇔ (iii) by compact-nakayama (with H replaced by J).
Ω(Π) is a DVR, so a finitely generated Ω(Π)-module is torsion iff finite; Ω(G/J)/Ω(G/J)ψ_J(f) is finite iff right multiplication by ψ_J(f) has finite kernel, iff it is injective on V(G/J).
Ω(G/J) has no nonzero finite submodule, so finite kernel means zero kernel.
acceptance: Test on H = 1, G = Γ, J = 1: (iii) says F_p⟦T⟧/(f̄) finite, i.e. f̄ ≠ 0.

nodes.title: Criteria for membership in S (right)
nodes.statement: With J as before, f ∈ S iff Λ(G)/fΛ(G) is finitely generated as a right Λ(H)-module, iff Λ(G/J)/φ_J(f)Λ(G/J) is a finitely generated ℤ_p-module, iff Ω(G/J)/ψ_J(f)Ω(G/J) is finite, iff left multiplication by ψ_J(f) on Ω(G/J) is injective. In particular S is the same set whether defined with left or right modules.
hypotheses: As in canonical-set-left-criteria.
proofSteps: f ∈ S iff α_J(f) = image of ψ_J(f) in V(G/J) has a left inverse, iff it has a right inverse (quotient-total-algebra), iff left multiplication by ψ_J(f) is injective.
Reverse the argument of canonical-set-left-criteria for right modules.
acceptance: This symmetry is what makes S both a left and a right Ore set.

nodes.title: S-torsion equals finite generation over Λ(H)
nodes.statement: A finitely generated left (or right) Λ(G)-module M is S-torsion (every x ∈ M is killed by some s ∈ S) iff M is finitely generated over Λ(H).
hypotheses: G compact p-adic analytic, H ◁ G closed, G/H ≅ ℤ_p.
proofSteps: S-torsion ⇒ finitely generated: M is a quotient of ⊕ Λ(G)/Λ(G)f_i with f_i ∈ S, each finitely generated over Λ(H).

Conversely fix x ∈ M, J and Π as above, τ ∈ Λ(G) lifting T; the Λ(J)-submodules U_n = Σ_{k≤n} Λ(J)τ^k x of the finitely generated Λ(J)-module M stabilise (Λ(J) noetherian), giving s_n = τ^n − a_{n−1}τ^{n−1} − … − a₀ with s_n x = 0.
ψ_J(s_n) is a nonzero element of Ω(Π) (its image mod the augmentation of J is T^n + …), so right multiplication by it is injective on Ω(G/J), and s_n ∈ S by canonical-set-left-criteria (iv).
acceptance: The abstract direction (S-torsion ⇒ finitely generated over B) holds for any pair (A, B); the converse is the group-theoretic input.

nodes.title: The canonical Ore set theorem
nodes.statement: S is multiplicatively closed, a left and right Ore set in Λ(G) (for s ∈ S, r ∈ Λ(G) there are t₁, t₂ ∈ S and w₁, w₂ with s w₁ = r t₁ and w₂ s = t₂ r), and consists of nonzero divisors. Hence Mathlib's OreSet structure exists on S, on either side.
hypotheses: G compact p-adic analytic, H ◁ G closed, G/H ≅ ℤ_p.
proofSteps: Multiplicative: 0 → Λs₂/Λs₁s₂ → Λ/Λs₁s₂ → Λ/Λs₂ → 0 with the first term a quotient of Λ/Λs₁.
Ore: Λ/Λf and Λ/fΛ are finitely generated over Λ(H), hence S-torsion (Proposition 2.3): s x ∈ Λf and x s′ ∈ fΛ.
Nonzero divisors: φ_J(f) is not a zero divisor in Λ(G/J) for every J (criteria (iv) of Lemmas 2.1 and 2.2 lifted from Ω to Λ), and Λ(G) = lim_J Λ(G/J).
Mathlib's OreSet needs the left Ore condition in the form t r = w s and right cancellation, which follows from S consisting of nonzero divisors.
acceptance: Ardakov–Brown generalise to arbitrary closed normal H; not planned here.
p ∉ S always: Λ(G)/pΛ(G) = Ω(G) is not finitely generated over Λ(H) because Γ = G/H is infinite; keep S and S* distinct.

sources.match: The Ore conditions in CFKSV's orientation.

nodes.title: Nilpotent kernels between finite levels
nodes.statement: For pro-p subgroups J ⊆ J′ of H, open in H and normal in G, the kernel K of Ω(G/J) → Ω(G/J′) is a nilpotent two-sided ideal: K = Ω(G/J) I_Δ with Δ = J′/J a finite p-group and I_Δ^n = 0.
hypotheses: J ⊆ J′ as stated.
proofSteps: K is generated by δ − 1 for δ ∈ Δ; Δ is normal so K = Ω(G/J) I_Δ = I_Δ Ω(G/J).
The augmentation ideal of F_p[Δ] is nilpotent for a finite p-group Δ, so K^n = Ω(G/J) I_Δ^n = 0.
acceptance: Test: G = Γ × ℤ/p, J = 1, J′ = ℤ/p: K = (σ − 1) with (σ − 1)^p = 0.

nodes.title: S as the elements regular modulo the prime radical
nodes.statement: Let 𝒩 be the preimage in Λ(G) of the prime radical of Ω(G/J) (independent of J by nilpotent-transition-kernel). Then S is the set of elements of Λ(G) that are regular (nonzero divisors) modulo 𝒩.
hypotheses: The prime radical of a noetherian ring is nilpotent and contains every nilpotent ideal.
proofSteps: Λ(G)/𝒩 = Ω(G/J)/𝒩(Ω(G/J)); f is regular modulo 𝒩 iff α_J(f) is a unit of V(G/J)/𝒩(V(G/J)).
Units modulo nilpotent ideals are units, so this holds iff ψ_J(f) is a nonzero divisor in Ω(G/J), iff f ∈ S by Lemmas 2.1(iv) and 2.2(iv).
acceptance: This characterisation (due to Schneider) shows S is intrinsic in Λ(G) and H.

nodes.title: The saturated Ore set S*
nodes.statement: S* = ⋃_{n≥0} p^n S. It is a multiplicatively closed left and right Ore set of nonzero divisors, and Λ(G)_{S*} = Λ(G)_S[1/p]. A finitely generated Λ(G)-module M is S*-torsion iff M/M(p) is finitely generated over Λ(H), where M(p) is the p-power torsion.
hypotheses: p is central in Λ(G).
proofSteps: p central and a nonzero divisor, so {p^n} is a central Ore set; products of Ore sets with a central Ore set are Ore.
Λ(G)_{S*} is the localisation of Λ(G)_S at p.
M/M(p) finitely generated over Λ(H) iff it is S-torsion (Proposition 2.3), iff M is S*-torsion.
acceptance: p ∉ S (Γ is infinite), so S* ≠ S.

nodes.title: The canonical localisation Λ(G)_S
nodes.statement: Λ(G)_S is Mathlib's Ore localisation of Λ(G) at the Ore set S (on the left; the right localisation is canonically isomorphic because S is two-sided Ore). The map Λ(G) → Λ(G)_S is injective, every s ∈ S becomes a unit, and any ring map Λ(G) → T inverting S factors uniquely through Λ(G)_S. Likewise Λ(G)_{S*}, O-coefficients included.

proofSteps: Instantiate OreLocalization with the OreSet structure of canonical-ore-theorem.
Injectivity: numeratorHom_inj, since S consists of (left) nonzero divisors.
Universal property: universalHom and universalHom_unique.
Left and right localisations agree: both satisfy the universal property for maps inverting S.
acceptance: Do not construct Λ(G)_S as a commutative fraction ring; Λ(G) is noncommutative.

nodes.title: Ore localisation is flat
nodes.statement: For a left Ore set S of a ring R, the localisation R_S = S⁻¹R is flat as a right R-module, R_S ⊗_R M ≅ S⁻¹M naturally, and the kernel of M → R_S ⊗_R M is the S-torsion submodule of M. Hence a complex C of R-modules has R_S ⊗_R C acyclic iff every H^i(C) is S-torsion.
hypotheses: S left Ore; for the last statement C is bounded above with flat or projective terms, or any complex since R_S is flat.
proofSteps: S⁻¹M (Mathlib's OreLocalization of a module) is exact in M: a fraction m/s vanishes iff t m = 0 for some t ∈ S.
The natural map R_S ⊗_R M → S⁻¹M is an isomorphism (both are left adjoint-like; check on free modules and use right exactness).
Exactness of S⁻¹(−) gives flatness and commutes with cohomology.
acceptance: CFKSV use exactness of localisation at S (p. 192).

nodes.title: The category 𝔐_H(G)
nodes.statement: 𝔐_H(G) is the full subcategory of finitely generated left Λ(G)-modules that are S*-torsion; equivalently those M with M/M(p) finitely generated over Λ(H). It is a Serre subcategory (closed under submodules, quotients and extensions). For H = 1, G = Γ it is the category of finitely generated torsion Λ(Γ)-modules.
hypotheses: G, H as in canonical-ore-set.
proofSteps: Closure under submodules uses that Λ(G) is noetherian (submodules of finitely generated modules are finitely generated); quotients and extensions are immediate from the torsion description.
For H = 1: S* = Λ(Γ) ∖ {0}, so S*-torsion means torsion.
acceptance: Test: Λ(G)/Λ(G)f for f ∈ S is in 𝔐_H(G); Λ(G) itself is not.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes acyclic after localisation
nodes.statement: For a left denominator (Ore) set S of a ring R, Σ_S is the full subcategory of the category C^p(R) of perfect complexes of R-modules consisting of the C with R_S ⊗_R C acyclic. Σ_S contains 0, is closed under quasi-isomorphism, shifts and extensions; by ore-localization-flat, C ∈ Σ_S iff every H^i(C) is S-torsion. For R = Λ(G) and S = S*, a module in 𝔐_H(G) of finite projective dimension, viewed as a complex, lies in Σ_{S*}.
hypotheses: C^p(R): bounded complexes of finitely generated projective R-modules, up to quasi-isomorphism (GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.4).
proofSteps: Define Σ_S by the acyclicity condition; check (i) 0 ∈ Σ_S, (ii) quasi-isomorphism invariance (R_S ⊗ − preserves quasi-isomorphisms of perfect complexes), (iii) shifts, (iv) extensions (long exact sequence after the exact functor R_S ⊗ −).
The cohomological description follows from flatness.
acceptance: Burns–Venjakob need a weaker condition (iv′) for subcategories not closed under extensions; Σ_S itself satisfies (iv).

nodes.title: K₀ is insensitive to complete ideals
nodes.statement: If I is a two-sided ideal of R and R is I-adically complete, then K₀(R) → K₀(R/I) is an isomorphism; in particular K₀(Λ(G)) ≅ K₀(Ω(G)) ≅ K₀(F_p[G/U]) ≅ K₀(F_p[G/U]/Jac) for U open normal pro-p.
hypotheses: I-adic completeness; idempotents lift modulo I.
proofSteps: Surjectivity: idempotent matrices lift modulo I (completeness).
Injectivity: a projective P with P/IP free is free (Nakayama for the complete ideal I ⊂ Jac(R)).
acceptance: Test: R = ℤ_p, I = pℤ_p: K₀(ℤ_p) = ℤ = K₀(F_p).

nodes.title: The localisation sequence for the canonical Ore set
nodes.statement: If G has no element of order p, there is an exact sequence K₁(Λ(G)) → K₁(Λ(G)_{S*}) →^{∂_G} K₀(𝔐_H(G)) → K₀(Λ(G)) → K₀(Λ(G)_{S*}) → 0, where K₀(𝔐_H(G)) is the Grothendieck group of the abelian category 𝔐_H(G); likewise for S in place of S* with the S-torsion category.
hypotheses: S* is an Ore set of nonzero divisors (NE.1); finite global dimension identifies K₀(Λ(G)) with G₀ and 𝔐_H(G) with the category of S*-torsion modules of finite projective dimension.
proofSteps: Quillen's localisation theorem for the Ore localisation Λ → Λ_{S*} (GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.5, support K-theory for A → S⁻¹A) with the category of finitely generated S*-torsion modules of projective dimension ≤ 1 (Swan, Grayson).
Finite global dimension: dévissage/resolution identifies that category's K₀ with K₀(𝔐_H(G)) (K.3).
acceptance: Keep the hypothesis 'no element of order p'; without it one works with perfect complexes (Σ_S*) instead of modules.

nodes.title: The boundary map ∂_G
nodes.statement: ∂_G : K₁(Λ(G)_{S*}) → K₀(𝔐_H(G)) is the connecting map of the localisation sequence, normalised so that for s ∈ S* (a nonzero divisor, unit in Λ(G)_{S*}), ∂_G([s]) = [Λ(G)/Λ(G)s] = [coker(x ↦ xs)]; it is a homomorphism, natural for the maps induced by G → G′ with H ↦ H′.
hypotheses: The sign convention is the one of CFKSV §4 (∂(f(a)) = [Coker α] for right multiplication α by a).
proofSteps: For a matrix A ∈ GL_n(Λ_{S*}) ∩ M_n(Λ) acting by right multiplication on Λⁿ, ∂_G[A] = [coker A] (Swan's description).
Every class of K₁(Λ_{S*}) is represented by such matrices up to units of Λ (clearing denominators).
acceptance: Fix the sign: ∂[s] = +[Λ/Λs]; the opposite convention changes characteristic elements to their inverses.

nodes.title: K₀(Λ(G)) injects into K₀ of a finite level
nodes.statement: For P an open normal pro-p subgroup of G, K₀(Λ(G)) → K₀(ℤ_p[G/P]) is injective.
hypotheses: P pro-p (Nakayama over Λ(P)).
proofSteps: Lift a ℤ_p[Δ]-isomorphism M/IM ⊕ ℤ_p[Δ]^r ≅ N/IN ⊕ ℤ_p[Δ]^r to β : M ⊕ Λ^r → N ⊕ Λ^r (M projective).
coker(β)_P = 0 gives coker β = 0 by Nakayama; H₁(P, N ⊕ Λ^r) = 0 gives ker(β)_P = 0, hence ker β = 0.
acceptance: P must be pro-p for Nakayama.

nodes.title: Detecting K₀(Λ(G)) by characters of a finite quotient
nodes.statement: With Δ = G/P and L ⊃ ℚ_p splitting ℚ̄_p[Δ], the composite λ : K₀(Λ(G)) → K₀(ℤ_p[Δ]) → K₀(ℚ_p[Δ]) → K₀(L[Δ]) ≅ ⊕_{ρ ∈ Irr(Δ)} K₀(L) ≅ ⊕_ρ ℤ is injective, and λ([M]) = ⊕_ρ j(τ[tw_ρ(M)]) with τ[U] = Σ_i (−1)^i [H_i(G, U)] for finitely generated M (finite global dimension).
hypotheses: Uses the Cartan–Brauer injectivity K₀(ℤ_p[Δ]) → K₀(ℚ_p[Δ]) and K₀(ℚ_p[Δ]) → K₀(L[Δ]) (Serre, Linear representations, 16 Theorem 34 Cor. 2 and 14.6; not freely available).
proofSteps: Compose the four maps; λ₁ is injective by k0-finite-level-injective, λ₂, λ₃ by the representation theory of finite groups, λ₄ is an isomorphism (Wedderburn and Morita).
Compute τ on modules through a finite projective resolution: τ[U] = Σ(−1)^i[Tor_i^{Λ(G)}(𝒪, U)] = Σ(−1)^i[H_i(G, U)], and similarly ε with Λ(Γ) and H_i(H, −).
acceptance: The Euler-characteristic formula needs finite global dimension (no element of order p).

nodes.title: H-homology of modules in 𝔐_H(G)
nodes.statement: For M ∈ 𝔐_H(G) the homology groups H_i(H, M) = Tor_i^{Λ(G)}(Λ(Γ), M) are finitely generated torsion Λ(Γ)-modules for all i ≥ 0, and vanish for i ≥ d if G has no element of order p.
hypotheses: cd_p(H) = d − 1 when H has no p-torsion.
proofSteps: Finite generation over Λ(Γ): Tor over Λ(G) of finitely generated modules.
M(p) is killed by p^t, so H_i(H, M(p)) is torsion; M_f = M/M(p) is finitely generated over Λ(H), so H_i(H, M_f) is a finitely generated ℤ_p-module, hence torsion over Λ(Γ); long exact sequence.
acceptance: Test: G = Γ, H = 1: H₀(1, M) = M is a torsion Λ(Γ)-module and higher homology vanishes.

nodes.title: Twisting preserves 𝔐_H(G)
nodes.statement: For a continuous ρ : G → GL_n(𝒪) and M ∈ 𝔐_H(G), the diagonal twist tw_ρ(M) = (M ⊗ 𝒪) ⊗_𝒪 𝒪ⁿ lies in 𝔐_H(G).
hypotheses: 𝒪 finite free over ℤ_p.
proofSteps: M ⊗ 𝒪 ∈ 𝔐_H(G); tw_ρ of the p-power torsion is killed by the same power of p.
tw_{ρ|H}(Λ(H)^m) is free of finite rank over Λ(H), so tw_ρ(M_f) is finitely generated over Λ(H).
acceptance: Needed to evaluate characteristic elements at twists (NE.3).

nodes.title: Surjectivity of ∂_G
nodes.statement: If G has no element of order p, then ∂_G : K₁(Λ(G)_{S*}) → K₀(𝔐_H(G)) is surjective; equivalently every M ∈ 𝔐_H(G) has [M] = 0 in K₀(Λ(G)).
hypotheses: No element of order p.
proofSteps: By exactness, surjectivity of ∂_G is equivalent to [M] ↦ 0 in K₀(Λ(G)).
For each ρ ∈ Irr(Δ): H_i(H, tw_ρ M) is Λ_𝒪(Γ)-torsion, so ε[tw_ρ M] = 0 in K₀(Λ_𝒪(Γ)) ≅ ℤ (rank), hence τ = 0.
λ[M] = ⊕ j(τ[tw_ρ M]) = 0 and λ is injective.
acceptance: For G = Γ this is the statement that finitely generated torsion Λ(Γ)-modules have zero class in K₀(Λ(Γ)) = ℤ.

nodes.title: Characteristic elements
nodes.statement: For M ∈ 𝔐_H(G) (G without element of order p), a characteristic element of M is any ξ_M ∈ K₁(Λ(G)_{S*}) with ∂_G(ξ_M) = [M]. Characteristic elements exist (boundary-surjective) and two of them differ by an element of the image of K₁(Λ(G)) → K₁(Λ(G)_{S*}).
hypotheses: A characteristic element is a lift of a class, not a canonical scalar; its ambiguity is exactly the image of K₁(Λ(G)).
proofSteps: Existence by surjectivity of ∂_G; ambiguity by exactness at K₁(Λ(G)_{S*}).
acceptance: Recover the characteristic power series up to Λ(Γ)^× for G = Γ (commutative-cyclic-comparison).

nodes.title: Λ(G)_S is semilocal, Λ(G)_{S*} need not be
nodes.statement: Λ(G)_S is a semilocal ring: for J ≤ H pro-p, open in H and normal in G, the image S_J of S consists of all nonzero divisors of Ω(G/J), Ω(G/J)_{S_J} is Artinian (= Ω(G/J) localised at the central Ω(Π) ∖ 0), and the kernel of Λ(G)_S → Ω(G/J)_S lies in the Jacobson radical. For G = ℤ_p² with H one factor, Λ(G)_{S*} = ℤ_p[[U, V]]_{(p,U)}[1/p] has infinitely many maximal ideals.
hypotheses: G, H as in NE.1.
proofSteps: Lemma 4.3: every s ∈ S_J is integral over the central Ω(Π) with nonzero constant term, so invertible after inverting Ω(Π) ∖ 0; Ω(G/J)_Σ is finite-dimensional over R(Π).
For x = s⁻¹θ with θ ∈ ker ψ_J, s − θ ∈ S, so 1 − x = s⁻¹(s − θ) is a unit: ker ⊂ Jac.
acceptance: Keep the non-semilocal example for S*.

nodes.title: Units surject onto K₁ of the localisations
nodes.statement: If G has no element of order p, the natural maps Λ(G)_S^× → K₁(Λ(G)_S) and Λ(G)_{S*}^× → K₁(Λ(G)_{S*}) are surjective. Hence characteristic elements can be represented by units of Λ(G)_{S*}.
hypotheses: Vaserstein: units of a semilocal ring surject onto K₁ (not freely available; cited).
proofSteps: Λ(G)_S is semilocal (Proposition 4.2): surjectivity for S by Vaserstein.

For S*: the localisation sequence K₁(Λ(G)_S) → K₁(Λ(G)_{S*}) → K₀(Ω′(G)) and the surjectivity of (Λ(G)[1/p])^× → K₀(Ω(G)) through the classes [P/pP] of direct summands (Lemmas 4.5–4.6: right multiplication by a = α(1) with α = p on P and 1 on P′, ∂(a) = [P/pP]).
acceptance: The second assertion uses the explicit boundary ∂(a) = [coker α], fixing the sign convention.

nodes.title: The commutative one-variable case
nodes.statement: For G = Γ ≅ ℤ_p and H = 1: S* = Λ(Γ) ∖ {0}, Λ(Γ)_{S*} = Q(Γ) is the fraction field, K₁(Q(Γ)) = Q(Γ)^×, K₀(𝔐_H(G)) is the Grothendieck group of finitely generated torsion Λ(Γ)-modules, and ∂ sends f/g to [Λ/f] − [Λ/g]. A characteristic element of a torsion module M is its characteristic power series char(M) (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4) up to Λ(Γ)^×.
hypotheses: Λ(Γ) ≅ ℤ_p[[T]] is a regular local ring of dimension 2; K₁(Λ(Γ)) = Λ(Γ)^×.
proofSteps: Q(Γ) is a field, so K₁ = units by the determinant.
For M ≅ ⊕Λ/(f_i) up to pseudo-isomorphism, [M] = Σ[Λ/f_i]: a pseudo-null (finite) module has class 0 in K₀(𝔐), e.g. 0 → Λ/p →^T Λ/p → F_p → 0 gives [F_p] = 0; then ∂(∏ f_i) = [M].
acceptance: The ambiguity K₁(Λ(Γ)) = Λ(Γ)^× is exactly 'up to units'.
Check a pseudo-null (finite) module: its characteristic element is a unit.

nodes.title: Twisting modules by a representation
nodes.statement: G is a compact p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H and G/H = Γ ≅ ℤ_p (topological generator fixed, Λ(Γ) = ℤ_p[[T]]), 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite extension L of ℚ_p, Λ_𝒪(Γ) = 𝒪[[T]] with fraction field Q_𝒪(Γ), and ρ : G → GL_n(𝒪) continuous. For a finitely generated Λ(G)-module M, tw_ρ(M) = M_𝒪 ⊗_𝒪 𝒪ⁿ with M_𝒪 = M ⊗_{ℤ_p} 𝒪 and the diagonal action σ(m ⊗ z) = σm ⊗ ρ(σ)z, extended to Λ(G) by compactness. tw_ρ is exact, tw_ρ(Λ_𝒪(G)^m) is free over Λ_𝒪(G), and if M ∈ 𝔐_H(G) then tw_ρ(M) ∈ 𝔐_H(G) (Lemma 3.2).
hypotheses: ρ continuous; G compact p-adic Lie.
proofSteps: Exactness: tensoring with the free 𝒪-module 𝒪ⁿ.
Freeness: Λ_𝒪(G) ⊗ 𝒪ⁿ with the diagonal action is isomorphic to Λ_𝒪(G)ⁿ with the left action (the untwisting g ⊗ z ↦ g ⊗ ρ(g)^{−1}z).
Lemma 3.2: tw_ρ(M_𝒪(p)) is killed by the same power of p, and a surjection Λ(H)^m ↠ M_𝒪/M_𝒪(p) gives a surjection from the free Λ(H)-module tw_{ρ|H}(Λ(H)^m).
acceptance: The action is diagonal, not ρ on the coefficients alone; tw is used with the contragredient ρ̂ in the Euler characteristic formula.

nodes.title: The ring homomorphism Φ_ρ : Λ(G) → M_n(Λ_𝒪(Γ))
nodes.statement: G is a compact p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H and G/H = Γ ≅ ℤ_p (topological generator fixed, Λ(Γ) = ℤ_p[[T]]), 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite extension L of ℚ_p, Λ_𝒪(Γ) = 𝒪[[T]] with fraction field Q_𝒪(Γ), and ρ : G → GL_n(𝒪) continuous. By continuity ρ gives ρ : Λ(G) → M_n(𝒪) (14). The continuous homomorphism G → (M_n(𝒪) ⊗_{ℤ_p} Λ(Γ))^×, σ ↦ ρ(σ) ⊗ σ̄ (σ̄ the image of σ in Γ) (16), extends to a ring homomorphism Φ_ρ : Λ(G) → M_n(Λ_𝒪(Γ)) (15), with Φ_ρ(p) = pI_n; composing with the augmentation Λ_𝒪(Γ) → 𝒪 gives (14).
proofSteps: M_n(𝒪) ⊗_{ℤ_p} Λ(Γ) = M_n(Λ_𝒪(Γ)) because 𝒪 is free of finite rank over ℤ_p.
The map on G is a continuous homomorphism into the units of a compact ring, so it extends to the completed group algebra (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1).
acceptance: Φ_ρ records the Γ-component σ̄ as well as ρ(σ); for H = 1 and ρ trivial it is the identity of Λ(Γ).

nodes.title: Φ_ρ extends to the localisation at S*
nodes.statement: (Lemma 3.3.) Φ_ρ extends to a ring homomorphism Φ_ρ : Λ(G)_{S*} → M_n(Q_𝒪(Γ)) (17): Φ_ρ(s) is invertible for every s ∈ S* = ∪_n pⁿS.
hypotheses: S the canonical Ore set of NE.1.
proofSteps: It suffices that the reduction Φ̃_ρ(s) ∈ M_n(k[[T]]) has nonzero determinant for s ∈ S.
Φ̃_ρ factors through δ : Ω(G/J) → M_n(k[[T]]) for a pro-p open J ⊆ H normal in G inside ker ρ̃ (GL_n(k) is finite).
A central Π ≅ ℤ_p of G/J inside ker ρ̃ has δ(Ω(Π)) ⊆ k[[T]]I_n, and Q(k[[T]]) is finite over R(Π); δ extends to R(Π) ⊗_{Ω(Π)} Ω(G/J), where ψ_J(s) is a unit (NE.1), so δ(ψ_J(s)) is invertible.
acceptance: The extension is to matrices over the fraction field Q_𝒪(Γ), not over Λ_𝒪(Γ): elements of S become invertible only after inverting nonzero power series.

nodes.title: Evaluation of K₁-elements at representations
nodes.statement: (17) induces Φ′_ρ : K₁(Λ(G)_{S*}) → K₁(M_n(Q_𝒪(Γ))) = Q_𝒪(Γ)^× (22) (Morita equivalence and the determinant of the field Q_𝒪(Γ)). Let φ : Λ_𝒪(Γ) → 𝒪 be the augmentation with kernel 𝔭, extended to φ : Λ_𝒪(Γ)_𝔭 → L. For ξ ∈ K₁(Λ(G)_{S*}), ξ(ρ) := φ(Φ′_ρ(ξ)) ∈ L if Φ′_ρ(ξ) ∈ Λ_𝒪(Γ)_𝔭, and ξ(ρ) := ∞ otherwise. On K₁(Λ(G)) this restricts to K₁(Λ(G)) → K₁(M_n(𝒪)) = 𝒪^× (21).
hypotheses: ρ : G → GL_n(𝒪) continuous (Artin or not).
proofSteps: Morita invariance K₁(M_n(A)) ≅ K₁(A) and K₁(F) = F^× for a field (determinant) come from GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.7.
Functoriality of K₁ along the ring maps (14) and (17), compatible with K₁(Λ(G)) → K₁(Λ(G)_{S*}).
acceptance: Keep the conventions: Φ′_ρ is a determinant of Φ_ρ, so for a group element g, [g](ρ) = det ρ(g) (not trace, not det ρ(g^{−1})); the value ∞ is part of the definition.
Only the value at the augmentation is taken: Φ′_ρ(ξ) ∈ Q_𝒪(Γ)^× carries more information than ξ(ρ).

nodes.title: Akashi series
nodes.statement: For M ∈ 𝔐_H(G) the H_i(H, M) are finitely generated torsion Λ(Γ)-modules, zero for i ≥ d if G has no element of order p (Lemma 3.1). With f_{i,M} a characteristic power series of H_i(H, M), Ak(M) = ∏_i f_{i,M}^{(−1)^i} mod Λ(Γ)^× (37) defines Ak : K₀(𝔐_H(G)) → Q(Γ)^×/Λ(Γ)^× (38); for an 𝒪-module M, Ak_𝒪(M) uses characteristic series over Λ_𝒪(Γ) (39), and the norm N : Λ_𝒪(Γ) → Λ(Γ) gives N(Ak_𝒪(M)) = Ak(M) (40).
hypotheses: G without elements of order p for the vanishing statement (cd_p H = d − 1).
proofSteps: H_i(H, M) = Tor_i^{Λ(G)}(Λ(Γ), M) is finitely generated over Λ(Γ); torsion because H_i(H, M(p)) is killed by a power of p and H_i(H, M/M(p)) is finitely generated over ℤ_p.
Additivity on short exact sequences from the long exact sequence of H-homology and multiplicativity of characteristic series.
(40): N(g_i) = f_i mod Λ(Γ)^× (Bourbaki, Commutative Algebra VII §4.8, Prop. 18; PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4).
acceptance: Ak is defined only modulo units; the Euler-characteristic formula uses its value at T = 0 up to p-adic units.

nodes.title: The evaluation–Akashi diagram
nodes.statement: (Lemma 3.7.) With Δ_ρ([M]) = Ak_𝒪(tw_{ρ̂}(M)) (41)–(42), where ρ̂(g) = ρ(g^{−1})^t is the contragredient, and ∂_Γ : Q_𝒪(Γ)^× → Q_𝒪(Γ)^×/Λ_𝒪(Γ)^×, the square ∂_Γ ∘ Φ′_ρ = Δ_ρ ∘ ∂_G (43) commutes.
hypotheses: G without elements of order p (so ∂_G is defined on modules).
proofSteps: Functoriality of the localisation sequence with Morita equivalence gives (47): ∂_1 ∘ v_1 ∘ u_1 = v_0 ∘ u_0 ∘ ∂_G.

For a finite projective resolution P_• of M, u_0([M]) = Σ(−1)^i[M_n(Λ_𝒪(Γ)) ⊗_{Λ(G)} P_i] (49); the row-vector Morita functor identifies (Rⁿ)^t ⊗_{M_n(R)} M_n(R) ⊗_{Λ(G)} P_i with Λ_𝒪(Γ) ⊗_{Λ_𝒪(G)} tw_{ρ̂}(P_i) (50), since the right action (τ ⊗ x^t)g = τḡ ⊗ x^tρ(g)^t is the left action through ρ̂.
tw_{ρ̂}(P_•) resolves tw_{ρ̂}(M), and Λ_𝒪(Γ) ⊗ − computes H_i(H, tw_{ρ̂}(M)), whose alternating class is Ak_𝒪.
acceptance: The contragredient ρ̂ appears on the module side: the evaluation at ρ corresponds to twisting by ρ̂.

nodes.title: Characteristic elements compute twisted Euler characteristics
nodes.statement: (Theorem 3.6.) Assume G has no element of order p. Let M ∈ 𝔐_H(G) with characteristic element ξ_M. For every continuous ρ : G → GL_n(𝒪) with χ(G, tw_{ρ̂}(M)) finite, ξ_M(ρ) ≠ 0, ∞ and χ(G, tw_{ρ̂}(M)) = |ξ_M(ρ)|_p^{−m_ρ}, where m_ρ = [L : ℚ_p] and |p|_p = 1/p.
hypotheses: G has no element of order p; χ(G, tw_{ρ̂}(M)) finite.
proofSteps: If χ(G, W) is finite (W = tw_{ρ̂}(M)), then φ(f_{i,W}) ≠ 0 for all i, φ(Ak(W)) ≠ 0, ∞ and χ(G, W) = |φ(Ak(W))|_p^{−1} (44) (Coates–Schneider–Sujatha, via Hochschild–Serre and χ(Γ, N) = |f_N(0)|_p^{−1}; requested from IntegralIwasawaTheory I.4).
By (40) and N ∘ φ = φ ∘ N, χ(G, W) = |φ(Ak_𝒪(W))|_p^{−m_ρ} (45).
Lemma 3.7 gives ∂_Γ(Φ′_ρ(ξ_M)) = Ak_𝒪(tw_{ρ̂}(M)) (46), and the value at T = 0 is ξ_M(ρ).
acceptance: The formula determines |ξ_M(ρ)|_p only; the unit part of ξ_M(ρ) is not an Euler-characteristic invariant.

nodes.title: Evaluation at Artin representations under a finiteness condition
nodes.statement: (Theorem 3.8, Lemma 3.9.) Assume G has no element of order p and let M ∈ 𝔐_H(G) satisfy H_i(H′, M) finite for all i ≥ 1 and all open H′ ⊆ H normal in G (51). Then for every Artin representation ρ (ker ρ open), Ak_𝒪(tw_ρ(M)) ∈ Λ_𝒪(Γ)[1/p] modulo units (52), ξ_M(ρ) ≠ ∞, and ξ_M(ρ) ≠ 0 iff χ(G, tw_{ρ̂}(M)) is finite.
hypotheses: G without elements of order p; (51).
proofSteps: With H′ = ker ρ ∩ H, W = tw_ρ(M) is M_𝒪ⁿ as an H′-module, so H_i(H′, W) is finite for i ≥ 1 (54); Hochschild–Serre for Δ = H/H′ shows H_i(H, W) is killed by a power of p for i ≥ 1, so g_{i,W} = π^{μ_i} (53).
Hence Ak_𝒪(W) = g_{0,W}∏π^{(−1)^iμ_i} (56), and φ(Ak_𝒪(W)) ≠ 0 iff φ(g_{0,W}) ≠ 0 iff χ(G, W) is finite.
Lemma 3.7 then gives Φ′_ρ(ξ_M) ∈ Λ_𝒪(Γ)_𝔭 and the finiteness criterion.
acceptance: Condition (51) is on all open normal H′ ⊆ H; it holds for M iff it holds for M(p) and M/M(p).

nodes.title: Artin formalism for G-Euler characteristics
nodes.statement: (Theorem 3.10.) Let G be a compact p-adic Lie group without elements of order p (no H needed), G′ ⊆ G open normal, Δ = G/G′, V the irreducible Q̄_p-representations of Δ, all realised over L with integers 𝒪. For finitely generated M, χ(G′, M) is finite iff χ(G, tw_ρ(M)) is finite for all ρ ∈ V, and then χ(G′, M)^{[L:ℚ_p]} = ∏_{ρ∈V} χ(G, tw_ρ(M))^{n_ρ} (58).
hypotheses: G without elements of order p.
proofSteps: 0 → 𝒪[Δ] → ⊕_ρ L_ρ^{n_ρ} → W → 0 with W finite (59); tensor with a projective resolution P_• of M_𝒪 (61).
K_i = W ⊗ C_i is finite and [C] = 0 in K₀(𝒪[Δ]) (injectivity into K₀(L[Δ])), so ∏♯H_i(K)^{(−1)^i} = θ([C]) = 1 (67)–(69).
acceptance: The exponent [L : ℚ_p] on the left accounts for the 𝒪-coefficients.

nodes.title: The GL₂ example: X₁(11) at p = 5
nodes.statement: (Proposition 3.11.) For E = X₁(11), p = 5, F_∞ = ℚ(E_{5^∞}), G = Gal(F_∞/ℚ), H = Gal(F_∞/ℚ^cyc), M = X(E/F_∞) ∈ 𝔐_H(G), and the degree-4 Artin representations ρ_i induced from nontrivial characters of Gal(F_i/ℚ(μ_5)) with F_1 = ℚ(E_5), F_2 = ℚ(E_{2,5}) (E_2 the conductor-11 curve with E_2(ℚ) = 0): χ(G, tw_{ρ_1}(M)) = 5³ and χ(G, tw_{ρ_2}(M)) = 5, so |ξ_{E,5}(ρ_1)|_5^{−1} = 5³ and |ξ_{E,5}(ρ_2)|_5^{−1} = 5 (ρ̂_i = ρ_i).
hypotheses: The arithmetic inputs χ(G_F, X) = 5⁴, χ(G_{F_1}, X) = 5¹⁶, χ(G_{F_2}, X) = 5⁸ ((78)–(80)) come from Coates–Howson's Euler characteristic formula (77) and Fisher's computations, cited by CFKSV; they are recorded as a gap.
proofSteps: Theorem 3.10 with G′ = G_F (Δ cyclic of order 4, four characters over ℚ_5) and G′ = G_{F_1} (Δ = Gal(F_1/ℚ) of order 20: the four characters and ρ_1) gives χ(G, tw_{ρ_1}X)⁴ = 5¹⁶/5⁴ = 5¹².
Likewise χ(G, tw_{ρ_2}X)⁴ = 5⁸/5⁴ = 5⁴.
Theorem 3.6 converts these into the absolute values of the evaluations.
acceptance: Checks the Frobenius/contragredient conventions: ρ_i are self-dual, so tw_{ρ̂_i} = tw_{ρ_i}.

nodes.title: The integrality conjecture for characteristic elements (Conjecture 4.8)
nodes.statement: Assume G has no element of order p. Put R₁ = Λ(G), R₂ = Λ(G)[1/p], R₃ = Λ(G)_{S*} (so R₁ ⊂ R₂ ⊂ R₃), A₁ = Λ_𝒪(Γ), A₂ = Λ_𝒪(Γ)[1/p], and α : R₃^× → K₁(R₃) the canonical map (surjective by NE.2/units-surject-k1). Let ℜ(G) be the continuous representations ρ of the form (11) (over the integers of finite extensions of ℚ_p) and 𝔄(G) ⊂ ℜ(G) the Artin ones. Conjecture 4.8 is the proposition that, for every ξ ∈ K₁(R₃), in each of four cases the assertions (a)–(d) are equivalent: Case 1: (a) ξ ∈ α(R₂ ∩ R₃^×), (b) ξ(ρ) ≠ ∞ for all ρ, (c) Φ′_ρ(ξ) ∈ A₂ for all ρ, (d) Φ′_ρ(ξ) ∈ A₂ for all Artin ρ; Case 2: α(R₁ ∩ R₃^×), ξ(ρ) finite and in 𝒪, Φ′_ρ(ξ) ∈ A₁; Case 3: α(R₂^×), ξ(ρ) ≠ 0, ∞, Φ′_ρ(ξ) ∈ A₂^×; Case 4: α(R₁^×), ξ(ρ) finite and in 𝒪^×, Φ′_ρ(ξ) ∈ A₁^×. (Lemma 4.9.) In each case (a) ⇒ (b), (b) ⇔ (c) and (c) ⇒ (d).
hypotheses: a conjecture: it is stated as a proposition, never assumed by a downstream theorem
CFKSV report it true for G = ℤ_p^d × Δ (Δ finite of order prime to p), proof omitted, and cite Kato [21] Proposition 8.19 as further evidence; neither is planned (recorded as remaining)
proofSteps: Lemma 4.9: (c) ⇒ (d) is trivial, (c) ⇒ (b) because ξ(ρ) is the image of Φ′_ρ(ξ) under augmentation; (a) ⇒ (b) since ξ = α(p^{−m}f) gives ξ(ρ) = p^{−mn} det ρ(f).

(b) ⇒ (c): the twisting identity Φ′_{ρη}(ξ) = Φ′_ρ(ξ)(η(γ)^{−1}(1 + T) − 1) (94) for continuous η : Γ → 𝒪^×, proved on characteristic elements (they generate K₁(R₃)) from (87) and Lemma 3.7; a pole of Φ′_ρ(ξ) at T = α in the maximal ideal would give ξ(ηρ) = ∞ for η(γ₀) = (1 + α)^{−1}.
acceptance: For G = ℤ_p (so H = 1) Case 2 says: a characteristic power series lies in ℤ_p[[T]] up to units exactly when it has no poles at the points of the open unit disc; check this on f = T/(T − p).

nodes.title: The dual Selmer module over the trivialising extension of E[p^∞]
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ be an elliptic curve and p ≥ 5 a prime of good ordinary reduction ('our hypotheses on p'), F_∞ = ℚ(E_{p^∞}) ⊇ ℚ(μ_{p^∞}) ⊇ ℚ^cyc (Weil pairing), G = Gal(F_∞/ℚ) (a closed subgroup of GL₂(ℤ_p), of dimension 4 without CM and 2 with CM, and with no element of order p), H = Gal(F_∞/ℚ^cyc), Γ = Gal(ℚ^cyc/ℚ). For an algebraic extension L/ℚ the Selmer group is 𝒮(E/L) = ker(H¹(L, E_{p^∞}) → Π_w H¹(L_w, E(L̄_w))) over the non-archimedean w, and X(E/L) = Hom(𝒮(E/L), ℚ_p/ℤ_p); for L Galois over F, X(E/L) is a finitely generated left Λ(Gal(L/F))-module. Also G_F = Gal(F_∞/F), H_F = Gal(F_∞/F^cyc) and Y(E/K) = X(E/K)/X(E/K)(p).
hypotheses: p ≥ 5 and good ordinary reduction; p ≥ 5 is what rules out p-torsion in G ⊂ GL₂(ℤ_p)
the module-level Selmer group of CFKSV; the equivariant Selmer complexes of Fukaya–Kato, Kakde and Ritter–Weiss that NE.4 also asks for are not planned here (remaining)
proofSteps: Definitions; finite generation of X(E/L) over Λ(Gal(L/F)) by compact Nakayama (NE.0/compact-nakayama) from the finiteness of X(E/F) ⊗ over the augmentation.
acceptance: Check that for L = F finite X(E/F) is the usual Pontryagin dual of the p-primary Selmer group, with ℤ_p-corank the Mordell–Weil rank plus the corank of Ш[p^∞].

nodes.title: Criteria for X(E/F_∞) ∈ 𝔐_H(G) (Lemmas 5.3–5.4, Corollary 5.5, Proposition 5.6)
nodes.statement: (Lemma 5.3.) If X(E/F_∞) ∈ 𝔐_H(G), then for each finite F ⊂ F_∞: (i) X(E/F^cyc) is Λ(Γ_F)-torsion; (ii) H_i(H_F, X(E/F_∞)) = 0 for i ≥ 1; (iii) H_i(H_F, Y(E/F_∞)) is finite for i = 1, 2 and zero for i > 2; and μ_{G_L}(X(E/F_∞)) = μ_{Γ_L}(X(E/L^cyc)) when G_L is pro-p. (Lemma 5.4.) If X(E/F^cyc) is Λ(Γ_F)-torsion for all finite F and some L has G_L pro-p, μ_{G_L}(X(E/F_∞)) = μ_{Γ_L}(X(E/L^cyc)) and H₁(H_L, Y(E/F_∞)) finite, then X(E/F_∞) ∈ 𝔐_H(G). (Corollary 5.5.) If E has CM, X(E/F_∞) ∈ 𝔐_H(G) iff μ_{Γ_L}(X(E/L^cyc)) = 0 for some L with G_L pro-p. (Proposition 5.6.) If some L ⊂ F_∞ with G_L pro-p carries an elliptic curve E′ isogenous to E over L with X(E′/L^cyc) finitely generated over ℤ_p, then X(E/F_∞) ∈ 𝔐_H(G). Example: the three conductor-11 curves E₀, E₁, E₂ at p = 5 with L = ℚ(μ₅) (G_L pro-5 and X(E₁/L^cyc) = 0) satisfy Conjecture 5.1.
hypotheses: the proofs use Coates–Howson-type results ([8], [9], [11] of CFKSV: the finiteness of H¹(H_F, E_{p^∞}), Proposition 2.13 and Lemma 2.5 of [9]), Venjakob's pseudo-null theory [26], Schneps' thesis [28] and the two-variable CM main conjecture [27]; none is planned here (gap)
the vanishing X(E₁/ℚ(μ₅)^cyc) = 0 is quoted from [16] (a gap)
proofSteps: Lemma 5.3: the restriction map r_F : X(E/F_∞)_{H_F} → X(E/F^cyc) has finite cokernel (dual to ker t_F ⊂ H¹(H_F, E_{p^∞}), finite), so Y(E/F^cyc) is finitely generated over ℤ_p and X(E/F^cyc) is Λ(Γ_F)-torsion; the rest from [9].
Lemma 5.4: H₀(H_L, Y(E/F_∞)) is Λ(Γ_L)-torsion, and formula (25) of [9] forces its μ-invariant to vanish; Nakayama over the pro-p H_L.
Corollary 5.5 from Lemmas 5.3–5.4 with Schneps and Venjakob; Proposition 5.6 by Nakayama from r_L and an isogeny f : E′ → E whose induced map X(E/F_∞) → X(E′/F_∞) has kernel killed by a power of p.
acceptance: Check that Proposition 5.6's example uses the same F_∞ for all three isogenous curves.

nodes.title: The conjectural GL₂ p-adic L-function ℒ_E (Conjecture 5.7)
nodes.statement: For an Artin representation ρ of G realised over K_ρ, L(E, ρ, s) = Π_q P_q(E, ρ, q^{−s})^{−1} with P_q(E, ρ, T) = det(1 − Frob_q^{−1}T | (H¹_l(E) ⊗ V_{ρ,λ})^{I_q}); Ω_±(E) are the periods of the Néron differential over the ±-eigenvectors of complex conjugation on H₁(E(ℂ), ℤ); d^±(ρ) are the ±-dimensions of ρ; L_R(E, ρ, s) omits the Euler factors at R = {p} ∪ {q : ord_q(j_E) < 0}; p^{f_ρ} is the p-part of the conductor of ρ; 1 − a_pX + pX² = (1 − uX)(1 − wX) with u ∈ ℤ_p^×; e_p(ρ) is the local ε-factor at p. Assume (103): L(E, ρ, 1)/(Ω_+^{d⁺(ρ)}Ω_−^{d⁻(ρ)}) ∈ ℚ̄ and the analytic continuation of L(E, ρ, s) to s = 1. Let K(F_∞) be the maximal abelian extension of ℚ in F_∞ unramified at p (a finite extension), A the integers of the completion of K(F_∞) at a prime above p, Λ_A(G) = Λ(G) ⊗_{ℤ_p} A and S(A)* the corresponding Ore set, with Λ_A(G)_{S(A)*} = Λ(G)_{S*} ⊗ A. Conjecture 5.7 (p ≥ 5, good ordinary reduction) is the proposition that there is ℒ_E ∈ K₁(Λ_A(G)_{S(A)*}) with ℒ_E(ρ) ≠ ∞ and ℒ_E(ρ) = L_R(E, ρ, 1)/(Ω_+^{d⁺(ρ)}Ω_−^{d⁻(ρ)}) · e_p(ρ) · P_p(ρ̂, u^{−1})/P_p(ρ, w^{−1}) · u^{−f_ρ} for all Artin ρ (107).
hypotheses: a conjecture; the period conjecture (103) and analytic continuation are assumptions of its formulation
the enlarged coefficient ring A comes from the Tamagawa number conjecture (Fukaya–Kato [17], Theorem 4.2.26); evaluation extends to K₁(Λ_A(G)_{S(A)*}) as in §3
proofSteps: Definitions; S(A) is a left and right Ore set by the arguments of §2 (NE.1/canonical-ore-theorem), and Λ_A(G) = Λ(G) ⊗ A since A is free of finite rank over ℤ_p.
acceptance: The abelian specialisation (ρ a Dirichlet character of Γ-type) must recover the Mazur–Swinnerton-Dyer p-adic L-function with the same normalisation, not merely one with the same ideal (the stage's acceptance).

nodes.title: The GL₂ main conjecture (Conjecture 5.8)
nodes.statement: Assume p ≥ 5, good ordinary reduction and X(E/F_∞) ∈ 𝔐_H(G), and let ξ_E be a characteristic element of X(E/F_∞) (NE.2/characteristic-element). Let i : K₁(Λ(G)_{S*}) → K₁(Λ_A(G)_{S(A)*}) be induced by the ring extension. Granted Conjecture 5.7, Conjecture 5.8 is the proposition that i(ξ_E) and ℒ_E have the same image in K₁(Λ_A(G)_{S(A)*})/(image of K₁(Λ_A(G))).
hypotheses: existence (5.7) and the equality (5.8) are separate propositions; a conjectural interpolation object discharges no downstream theorem (the stage's boundary)
for CM curves (G of dimension 2) CFKSV say 5.8 follows from the two-variable main conjecture of Rubin and Yager once X(E/F_∞) ∈ 𝔐_H(G) (Corollary 5.5); this is recorded, not planned
proofSteps: Definition; well defined since characteristic elements are unique up to the image of K₁(Λ(G)) (NE.2/characteristic-element).
acceptance: The ambiguity is exactly the image of K₁(Λ_A(G)); an equality in K₁(Λ_A(G)_{S(A)*}) itself is not asserted.

nodes.title: Consequences of the main conjecture (Corollaries 5.9–5.10)
nodes.statement: Assume Conjecture 5.8. (Corollary 5.9.) For each Artin representation ρ of G, χ(G, tw_ρ(X(E/F_∞))) is finite iff L(E, ρ̂, 1) ≠ 0. (Corollary 5.10.) If L(E, ρ̂, 1) ≠ 0 and m_ρ is the degree of the fraction field of 𝒪 over ℚ_p (ρ as in (12)), then χ(G, tw_ρ̂(X(E/F_∞))) is the m_ρ-th power of the inverse of the p-adic absolute value of the right-hand side of (107).
hypotheses: conditional on Conjecture 5.8 (hence on 5.1 and 5.7)
CFKSV note that Case 1 of Conjecture 4.8 would put ξ_E in the image of Λ(G)[1/p]^× ∩ Λ(G)_{S*}^×
proofSteps: Corollary 5.9: for X in 𝔐_H(G), Lemma 5.3 and Theorem 3.8 (NE.3/artin-evaluation-integral) give ξ_E(ρ) ≠ 0 iff χ(G, tw_ρ̂(X)) is finite; |η(ρ)|_p = 1 for η in the image of K₁(Λ_A(G)); and ℒ_E(ρ) ≠ 0 iff L(E, ρ, 1) ≠ 0.
Corollary 5.10 from (36) (NE.3/euler-characteristic-evaluation) and (107).
acceptance: The source proves Corollary 5.9 with ρ and ρ̂ interchanged relative to the statement; since L(E, ρ̂, 1) is the complex conjugate of L(E, ρ, 1) for Artin ρ, the two readings agree — check this in the formalisation.

nodes.title: The main conjecture for X₁(11) at p = 5: the data and the consistency check
nodes.statement: For E = X₁(11) and p = 5 (continuing NE.3/gl2-euler-example): K(F_∞) = ℚ(μ₁₁)⁺, 5 is inert in it, and A is the integers of the unramified extension of ℚ₅ of degree 5. For the two degree-4 Artin representations ρ₁, ρ₂: d⁺ = d⁻ = 2; f_{ρ₁} = 3, f_{ρ₂} = 5; P₅(ρ₁, X) = 1 − X, P₅(ρ₂, X) = 1; P₅(E, ρ₁, X) = 1 − X + 5X², P₅(E, ρ₂, X) = 1; P₁₁(E, ρ_i, X) = 1; |e₅(ρ₁)|₅ = 5^{−3/2}, |e₅(ρ₂)|₅ = 5^{−5/2}; 1 − a₅X + 5X² = 1 − X + 5X²; and L(E, ρ₁, 1)/(Ω₊Ω₋)² = −2²/(11²√5), L(E, ρ₂, 1)/(Ω₊Ω₋)² = −2⁶/(11²·5√5). Both L-values are nonzero, so with Proposition 3.11 Corollary 5.9 holds for ρ₁, ρ₂; the right-hand side of (107) has the 5-adic valuations predicted by (74), so Corollary 5.10 holds for them too.
hypotheses: the numerical data are quoted from Dokchitser–Dokchitser [15], not recomputed (a gap for formalisation)
this checks consistency, not the conjecture
proofSteps: Insert (108)–(115) into (107): u, w are the roots of Y² − Y + 5 with u ≡ 1, w ≡ 0 mod 5, so v₅(1 − u^{−1}) = v₅(w) = 1 and v₅(1 − w^{−1}) = −1.
ρ₁: v₅ = −1/2 (L-value) + 3/2 (e₅) + (1 − (−1)) (the P₅ ratio) = 3; ρ₂: v₅ = −3/2 + 5/2 + 0 = 1. These match Proposition 3.11's Euler characteristics 5³ and 5 (with m_ρ = 1, ρ_i realised over ℤ₅).
acceptance: The valuation sums −1/2 + 3/2 + 2 = 3 and −3/2 + 5/2 = 1 are checked in the Lean file.

nodes.title: Surjectivity of ∂ for every compact p-adic Lie group
nodes.statement: Let G be a compact p-adic Lie group with closed normal H and G/H ≅ ℤ_p, possibly with elements of order p. In the localisation sequence K₁(Λ(G)) → K₁(Λ(G)_S) → K₀(Λ(G), Λ(G)_S) → K₀(Λ(G)) → K₀(Λ(G)_S), the boundary map ∂ is surjective: the map η : K₀(Λ(G), Λ(G)_S) → K₀(Λ(G)) is zero.
hypotheses: No hypothesis on p-torsion in G (CFKSV assume none; see boundary-surjective).
proofSteps: Fix an open normal pro-p subgroup P with Δ = G/P, and λ : K₀(Λ(G)) → ∏_{ρ∈V(Δ)} K₀(L), the composite of K₀(Λ(G)) → K₀(ℤ_p[Δ]) → K₀(ℚ_p[Δ]) → K₀(L[Δ]) ≅ ∏ K₀(M_{n_ρ}(L)); each step is injective (k0-representation-injective).

An element of K₀(Λ(G), Λ(G)_S) is [(P, s^{−1}a, Q)] and η of it is [Q/a(P)] − [Q/Qs]; for M = Q/a(P) S-torsion, each twist tw_ρ(M) is S-torsion (twist-preserves-MHG), so H_i(H, tw_ρ(M)) is Λ_𝒪(Γ)-torsion and its class in K₀(Λ_𝒪(Γ)) vanishes.
Hence ε([tw_ρ(M)]) = Σ(−1)^i[H_i(H, tw_ρ M)] = 0, so τ = 0 on the twists, λ([M]) = 0 and [M] = 0.
acceptance: Covers groups with p-torsion, which Kakde's reductions need (finite quotients of order divisible by p).

nodes.title: SK₁ and the quotient K′₁ of Iwasawa algebras
nodes.statement: For a finite group P and 𝒪 the integers of a finite extension L/ℚ_p, SK₁(𝒪[P]) = ker(K₁(𝒪[P]) → K₁(L[P])). For a compact p-adic Lie group G, SK₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) := lim_U SK₁(𝒪[G/U]), and SK₁(Λ_𝒪(G)_S), SK₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S) are its images in K₁(Λ_𝒪(G)_S) and K₁ of the p-adic completion Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S. K′₁(R) := K₁(R)/SK₁(R) for R each of these rings. Then K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) ≅ lim_Δ K′₁(𝒪[Δ]) over the finite quotients Δ of G, and K′₁(Λ(G)) ≅ lim_{Ḡ} K′₁(Λ(Ḡ)) over the quotients Ḡ = G/U by open pro-p subgroups U ≤ H normal in G.
hypotheses: G compact p-adic Lie.
proofSteps: K₁(Λ(G)) ≅ lim_n K₁(Λ(G)/J^n) for the Jacobson radical J (Fukaya–Kato, Proposition 1.5.1; see the gap on Fukaya–Kato).
For the finite groups K₁(Λ(G)/J^n, I_{Δ,n}/J^n) the limits over Δ and n commute, and ⋂_n⋂_Δ I_{Δ,n} = 0, so K₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) ≅ lim_Δ K₁(𝒪[Δ]) (Lemma 19).
Each SK₁(𝒪[Δ]) is finite (Wall; see the gap on Oliver's book), so the quotients pass to the limit.
Corollary 20 by cofinality of the finite quotients.
acceptance: K′₁ is used because SK₁ is invisible to Artin evaluations; uniqueness in the main conjecture holds in K′₁.

nodes.title: Admissible p-adic Lie extensions and the hypothesis μ = 0
nodes.statement: Let F be a totally real number field and p odd. An admissible p-adic Lie extension F_∞/F is a Galois extension, unramified outside a finite set of primes, with F_∞ totally real, G = Gal(F_∞/F) a p-adic Lie group and F_cyc ⊆ F_∞; put H = Gal(F_∞/F_cyc), Γ = G/H, and fix a finite set Σ of finite primes containing those ramified in F_∞. F_∞/F satisfies μ = 0 if some open pro-p subgroup H′ ≤ H has Gal(M/F_∞^{H′}) finitely generated over ℤ_p, M the maximal abelian pro-p extension of F_∞^{H′} unramified outside Σ; equivalently, the Iwasawa μ-invariant of L(μ_p) vanishes for L with L_cyc = F_∞^{H′}. Equivalently (Lemma 9), X = Gal(M_∞/F_∞) is finitely generated over Λ(H), M_∞ the maximal abelian pro-p extension of F_∞ unramified outside Σ.
hypotheses: F totally real, p odd, Σ finite containing the ramified primes.
proofSteps: Lemma 9: for H′ pro-p, Λ(H′) is local, so by Nakayama X is finitely generated over Λ(H) iff X_{H′} is finitely generated over ℤ_p; the inflation–restriction sequence for Gal(F_Σ/F_∞) ⊆ Gal(F_Σ/F_∞^{H′}) with ℚ_p/ℤ_p coefficients (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2) and the cofiniteness of H^i(H′, ℚ_p/ℤ_p) compare X_{H′} with Gal(M/F_∞^{H′}).
acceptance: μ = 0 is a hypothesis, recorded separately; Ferrero–Washington proves it for abelian L/ℚ, and nothing more general is claimed.

nodes.title: The complex C(F_∞/F)
nodes.statement: For an admissible F_∞/F, C(F_∞/F) = RHom(RΓ_ét(Spec 𝒪_{F_∞}[1/Σ], ℚ_p/ℤ_p), ℚ_p/ℤ_p) ≅ RHom(RΓ(Gal(F_Σ/F_∞), ℚ_p/ℤ_p), ℚ_p/ℤ_p), with H^{−1} = Gal(M_∞/F_∞), H⁰ = ℤ_p and H^i = 0 otherwise. It is a perfect complex of Λ(G)-modules, Λ(Gal(K/F)) ⊗^L_{Λ(G)} C(F_∞/F) ≅ C(K/F) for F ⊆ K ⊆ F_∞, and, under μ = 0, it is S-torsion, so it has a class [C(F_∞/F)] ∈ K₀(Λ(G), Λ(G)_S).
hypotheses: F_∞/F admissible; μ = 0 for the class in relative K₀.
proofSteps: The étale–Galois comparison, since ℚ_p/ℤ_p is a colimit of finite p-groups.

Cohomology: H⁰ = ℤ_p is the dual of H⁰(Gal(F_Σ/F_∞), ℚ_p/ℤ_p); H^{−1} is the dual of Hom(Gal(F_Σ/F_∞), ℚ_p/ℤ_p) = Gal(M_∞/F_∞)^∨; H²(Gal(F_Σ/F_∞), ℚ_p/ℤ_p) = 0 for totally real F_∞ and odd p (weak Leopoldt along F_cyc and ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4's cohomological dimension).
Perfectness and base change (1) are Fukaya–Kato's (see the gap on Fukaya–Kato).

S-torsion: its cohomology is finitely generated over Λ(H) by admissible-extension's Lemma 9, so Λ(G)_S ⊗^L C is acyclic (NE.1/s-torsion-iff-finitely-generated); the class is in NE.1/torsion-perfect-complexes.
acceptance: When G has elements of order p, X itself need not have finite projective dimension; the complex, not the module, is what has a class.

sources.match: The complex, its cohomology, and Fukaya–Kato's results (i)–(ii).

nodes.title: The main conjecture for totally real fields
nodes.statement: For an admissible F_∞/F satisfying μ = 0, MC(F_∞/F) is the proposition: there is a unique ζ(F_∞/F) ∈ K′₁(Λ(G)_S) with ∂(ζ(F_∞/F)) = −[C(F_∞/F)] and ζ(F_∞/F)(ρκ_F^r) = L_Σ(ρ, 1 − r) for every Artin character ρ of G and every positive integer r divisible by [F_∞(μ_p) : F_∞], where κ_F is the p-adic cyclotomic character and L_Σ(ρ, 1 − r) the Klingen–Siegel value with the Euler factors at Σ removed.
hypotheses: μ = 0; p odd; F totally real. Kakde states it as Theorem 11 because he proves it (NE.6).
proofSteps: Definition; the evaluation is NE.3/artin-evaluation on K′₁ (k1-prime), ∂ is the boundary of the localisation sequence, surjective by boundary-surjective-p-torsion.
acceptance: Uniqueness is in K′₁; in K₁ it can fail (Kakde, Remark 12). The formulation in K₁ is equivalent because SK₁(Λ(G)_S) = ker ∂ ∩ ⋂_ρ ker(evaluation at ρ) (Burns, recorded, not planned).
Independence of Σ (Remark 14) is recorded as the test below, not proved here.

nodes.title: The main conjecture for abelian × prime-to-p Galois groups
nodes.statement: Let F_∞/F be admissible with μ = 0 and Gal(F_∞/F) = G × Δ, G abelian and Δ finite of order prime to p. Then MC(F_∞/F) holds, and K₁(Λ(G × Δ)) → K₁(Λ(G × Δ)_S) is injective. For G = H × Γ with H finite abelian, the Deligne–Ribet pseudomeasure ζ is a unit of Λ(G)_S (Lemma 15) with ∂ζ = −[C(F_∞/F)] (Theorem 16).
hypotheses: μ = 0; p odd; #Δ prime to p.
proofSteps: Lemma 15: Λ(G)_S ≅ ⊕_{ψ∈Ĥ′} Λ_{𝒪_ψ}(H_p × Γ)_S, each summand local; (ψ × 1)(ζ) ∉ π_ψΛ_{𝒪_ψ}(Γ)_S by μ = 0 and Wiles's theorem, so ζ is a unit.

Theorem 16: characterwise, ∂(ψ(ζ)) = −[C_ψ] is Wiles's main conjecture (IntegralIwasawaTheory I.5) for the Deligne–Ribet functions G_ψ (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3); θ₀ : K₀(Λ(G), Λ(G)_S) → ∏_ψ K₀(Λ_{𝒪_ψ}(Γ), Λ_{𝒪_ψ}(Γ)_S) is injective, because x = |H|^{−1}Σ_h h Σ_ψ x_ψ ψ(h^{−1}) shows the cokernel of θ injects into that of θ_S (snake lemma).

Lemma 17: for p ∤ #Δ, K₁(Λ(G × Δ)_S) ≅ ⊕_{χ∈R(Δ)} Λ_{𝒪_χ}(G)_S^×, and ζ = Σ e_χ L_p(χ), with L_p(χ) built from Deligne–Ribet functions by Brauer induction (Tau Ceti InductionRestriction Layer 6), is the zeta element.
Theorem 18: K₀(Λ(G × Δ), Λ(G × Δ)_S) ≅ ⊕_χ K₀(Λ_{𝒪_χ}(G), Λ_{𝒪_χ}(G)_S), and the same decomposition for K₁ gives injectivity.
acceptance: The analytic input (Deligne–Ribet) and the arithmetic input (Wiles) are imported, not reproved; μ = 0 is used for the unit property.

sources.match: Theorem 18 with Lemma 15, Theorem 16 and Lemma 17 (pp. 14–17).

nodes.title: The Burns–Kato patching principle
nodes.statement: Let 𝒞 be a family of pairs (U, V), U open in G and V closed normal in U with U/V admissible, and θ = (θ_{U,V}) : K′₁(Λ(G)) → ∏_𝒞 K′₁(Λ(U/V)), θ_S the same on the localisations, each θ_{U,V} the norm to U followed by the quotient map. Suppose θ is an isomorphism onto a subgroup Φ, θ_S lands in a subgroup Φ_S with Φ_S ∩ ∏ K′₁(Λ(U/V)) = Φ, MC holds for every F_∞^V/F_∞^U with (ζ_{U,V}) ∈ Φ_S, and every Artin character of G is a ℤ-combination of characters induced or inflated from the U/V. Then MC(F_∞/F) holds, and K′₁(Λ(G)) → K′₁(Λ(G)_S) is injective when each K′₁(Λ(U/V)) → K′₁(Λ(U/V)_S) is.
hypotheses: The hypotheses listed; μ = 0 for each subquotient.
proofSteps: Choose f ∈ K′₁(Λ(G)_S) with ∂f = −[C(F_∞/F)] (boundary-surjective-p-torsion); θ_S(f) has components f_{U,V} with ∂f_{U,V} = −[C(F_∞^V/F_∞^U)] by base change (totally-real-iwasawa-complex).
u_{U,V} = ζ_{U,V} f_{U,V}^{−1} has ∂ = 0, so lies in K′₁(Λ(U/V)); (u_{U,V}) ∈ Φ_S ∩ ∏ K′₁ = Φ, so u_{U,V} = θ(u)_{U,V} for a unique u, and ζ = uf.
∂ζ = −[C]; interpolation by writing ρ = Σ n_i Ind/Inf ρ_i and using the norm and inflation compatibilities of evaluation (Kakde §2.4 (i)–(iii)); uniqueness and injectivity by the same diagram.
acceptance: This is the argument Kakde repeats in Theorems 21, 27, 33 and 36; planning it once lets each reduction supply only the description of Φ.

sources.locator: §1, the observation of Burns and Kato, p. 3 (arXiv v3)
sources.match: The principle stated in the introduction and carried out in each reduction.

nodes.title: Burns's reduction to one-dimensional extensions
nodes.statement: Let F_∞/F be admissible with μ = 0. If MC holds for every F_∞^U/F with U ≤ H open pro-p and normal in G, and each K′₁(Λ(G/U)) injects into K′₁(Λ(G/U)_S), then MC(F_∞/F) holds.
hypotheses: μ = 0; the quotients G/U are one-dimensional.
proofSteps: k1-prime (Corollary 20): K′₁(Λ(G)) ≅ lim_U K′₁(Λ(G/U)).

Uniqueness makes (ζ_{G/U}) a compatible system; burns-kato-patching with 𝒞 = {(G, U)} and Φ the inverse limit; every Artin character of G factors through some G/U, and [F_∞(μ_p) : F_∞] = [F_∞^U(μ_p) : F_∞^U] as U is pro-p.
acceptance: The injectivity hypothesis on K′₁ is carried, not dropped.

nodes.title: Reduction to ℚ_p-elementary Galois groups
nodes.statement: Let F_∞/F be admissible, one-dimensional, with μ = 0. If MC holds, and K′₁(Λ(U)) → K′₁(Λ(U)_S) is injective, for every admissible subextension whose Galois group U is ℚ_p-elementary (U = P ⋊ Γ with a central open Γ^{p^r} and (P ⋊ Γ)/Γ^{p^r} an l-ℚ_p-elementary finite group C_n ⋊ P₁, the image of P₁ in (ℤ/n)^× lying in Gal(ℚ_p(μ_n)/ℚ_p)), then MC(F_∞/F) holds and K′₁(Λ(G)) injects into K′₁(Λ(G)_S).
hypotheses: G one-dimensional: G ≅ H ⋊ Γ with Γ^{p^e} central.
proofSteps: Dress–Wall induction: K′₁(𝒪[P]) ≅ lim_π K′₁(𝒪[π]) over the K-elementary subgroups π, with norms and conjugations (Oliver, Theorem 11.2; see the gap on Oliver's book).
Lemma 26: K′₁(Λ(G)) ≅ lim_P K′₁(Λ(U_P)) over the ℚ_p-elementary P ≤ G_n = G/Γ^{p^{e+n}}, U_P their preimages (k1-prime's Lemma 19 in the limit).

burns-kato-patching, with compatibility of (ζ_P) under conjugation and norms from uniqueness and the invariance of L_Σ under conjugation and induction; interpolation by Brauer's induction theorem (Tau Ceti InductionRestriction Layer 6), elementary subgroups being ℚ_p-elementary.
acceptance: Uses ℚ_p-elementary subgroups for the K₁ isomorphism, although Brauer induction needs only elementary ones.

sources.match: Theorem 27 with Definitions 23–24, Theorem 25 and Lemma 26 (pp. 20–23).

nodes.title: The l-ℚ_p-elementary case, l ≠ p
nodes.statement: If F_∞/F is admissible with μ = 0 and G = Gal(F_∞/F) is l-ℚ_p-elementary for a prime l ≠ p, then MC(F_∞/F) holds and K₁(Λ(G)) injects into K₁(Λ(G)_S). Here G ≅ Γ^{p^e} × Ḡ with Ḡ = C ⋊ P finite (Lemma 28); reducing to C a cyclic p-group and P of order prime to p, with C̄ = H⁰(P, C), P₁ = ker(P → Aut C) and G₁ = Γ × C × P₁, the map θ = (quotient, norm) : K₁(Λ(G)) → K₁(Λ(Γ × C̄ × P)) × K₁(Λ(G₁)) is an isomorphism onto Φ = {(x₀, x₁) : norm(x₀) = can(x₁), x₁ fixed by P} (Proposition 30).
proofSteps: Lemma 28: the minimal central Γ^{p^e} splits off.
If p ∤ #C, abelian-case applies. Otherwise SK₁(Λ(G)) = 1 (Oliver 12.7), and θ lands in Φ: conjugation by P preserves the norm's matrix class, and the norm square commutes.
Surjectivity: J = ker(K₁(Λ(G₁)) → K₁(Λ(Γ × C̄ × P₁))) is pro-p (Oliver 2.10; Fukaya–Kato 1.5.3), so n = (P : P₁)-th roots exist in J^P.

Injectivity: Lemma 31 (every irreducible representation is inflated from C̄ × P or induced from G₁) makes β dual to (χ, ρ) ↦ Inf χ + Ind ρ injective; Oliver–Taylor's logarithm has kernel μ_{p−1} × G^ab (Wall), which the first component detects.
Then burns-kato-patching with abelian-case for the two components.
acceptance: Oliver's and Wall's theorems are cited inputs (see the gap on Oliver's book).

sources.match: Theorem 33 with Lemmas 28, 31, Definition 29 and Proposition 30 (pp. 23–27).

nodes.title: Reduction of the p-ℚ_p-elementary case to Δ × pro-p
nodes.statement: Let F_∞/F be admissible with μ = 0 and G p-ℚ_p-elementary, G/Γ^{p^e} = C_n ⋊ H_p with p ∤ n, U the preimage of H_p, and for χ ∈ Ĉ_n let U_χ = ker(U → Gal(L_χ/ℚ_p)), L_χ = ℚ_p(χ). Then K′₁(Λ(G)) ≅ ⊕_{χ∈C} K′₁(Λ_{𝒪_χ}(U_χ))^{U/U_χ} (Proposition 35), and if MC holds for each F_∞^{C_χ}/F_∞^{C_n ⋊ U_χ} with K′₁(Λ_{𝒪_χ}(U_χ)) → K′₁(Λ_{𝒪_χ}(U_χ)_S) injective, then MC(F_∞/F) holds and K′₁(Λ(G)) injects into K′₁(Λ(G)_S). This reduces the main conjecture to G = Δ × G_p with Δ cyclic of order prime to p and G_p one-dimensional pro-p.
hypotheses: G p-ℚ_p-elementary; μ = 0.
proofSteps: Proposition 35 at finite level is Oliver's Proposition 11.6 and Theorem 12.3(4) (gap on Oliver's book); pass to the limit with k1-prime.
Gal(F_∞^{C_χ}/F_∞^{C_n ⋊ U_χ}) ≅ C_n/C_χ × U_χ, and [F_∞(μ_p) : F_∞] is unchanged.
burns-kato-patching; every irreducible ρ is Ind(χρ_χ) (Serre, Proposition 25), giving interpolation.
acceptance: The final reduction step; the pro-p one-dimensional case is Kakde §5–6 (next checkpoint).

nodes.title: The Iwasawa algebra of a one-dimensional pro-p group as a twisted group ring
nodes.statement: For a ring R and a 2-cocycle τ : P × P → R^×, the twisted group ring R[P]^τ is the free R-module on P with h̄·h̄′ = τ(h, h′)·(hh′)‾. In the standing setting, Λ_𝒪(G) = Λ_𝒪(Z)[Ḡ]^τ with τ(h₁γ^{a₁}, h₂γ^{a₂}) = γ^{[(a₁+a₂)/p^e]p^e} ∈ Λ_𝒪(Z)^× (0 ≤ a_i < p^e), which is independent of the generator γ, symmetric, and satisfies τ(g, g⁻¹) = 1 = τ(g, 1). For every P ≤ Ḡ, Λ_𝒪(U_P) ≅ Λ_𝒪(Z)[P]^τ and Λ̂_𝒪(U_P)_S ≅ Λ̂_𝒪(Z)_{(p)}[P]^τ (Lemma 45), and U_P is abelian when P is cyclic (Lemma 46). T = Λ_𝒪(Z) ∖ pΛ_𝒪(Z) is a multiplicatively closed left and right Ore subset of the canonical Ore set S, and Λ_𝒪(G)_T = Λ_𝒪(G)_S = Λ_𝒪(Z)_{(p)}[Ḡ]^τ (Lemma 37, Remark 38). For R = Λ_𝒪(Z) or Λ̂_𝒪(Z)_{(p)}, the map Σ r_g ḡ ↦ Σ r_g [g] is an isomorphism of R-modules R[Ḡ]^τ/[R[Ḡ]^τ, R[Ḡ]^τ] ≅ R[Conj Ḡ]^τ (Lemma 43), where [I₁, I₂] is the additive subgroup generated by the ab − ba (Definition 41).
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p, or a finite direct sum of such rings.
proofSteps: The presentation: Λ_𝒪(G) is free over Λ_𝒪(Z) on lifts of Ḡ, and the cocycle records the carry γ^{a₁}γ^{a₂} = γ^{(a₁+a₂) mod p^e}·γ^{[(a₁+a₂)/p^e]p^e}; symmetry and normalisation are direct from the formula.

Lemma 37: T is Ore because Z is central, and has no zero divisors because Λ_𝒪(Z) is a domain, so Λ_𝒪(G)_T ⊆ Λ_𝒪(G)_S. Q(Λ_𝒪(Z)) ⊗ Λ_𝒪(G) is artinian (Λ_𝒪(G) is free of finite rank), hence equals Q(Λ_𝒪(G)); if x = a/t ∈ Λ_𝒪(G)_S with t ∈ p^nΛ_𝒪(Z), then a = tx ∈ p^nΛ_𝒪(G)_S ∩ Λ_𝒪(G) = p^nΛ_𝒪(G), and dividing p^n out of a and t puts t in T.

Lemma 43: the map is surjective, and its kernel contains the commutators because τ is symmetric; conversely an element of the kernel is Σ_{x∈Ḡ/C_g} r_{xgx⁻¹}(xgx⁻¹ − g) = Σ r_{xgx⁻¹} τ(xg, x⁻¹)⁻¹(xg·x⁻¹ − x⁻¹·xg), a sum of commutators.
Lemma 45 by restricting the presentation to U_P; Lemma 46 because U_P/Z is cyclic and Z is central.
acceptance: For Ḡ = 1 (G = Z ≅ ℤ_p) the construction is Λ_𝒪(ℤ_p) itself, and Conj Ḡ is a point.
The twisted group ring is not in Mathlib; with τ ≡ 1 it must agree with MonoidAlgebra.

sources.locator: §5.1.2, p. 31, with Lemmas 37, 43, 45, 46 and Remark 38, pp. 31–33 (arXiv v3)
sources.match: §§5.1.1–5.1.4: the twisted group ring, the Ore set T (Lemma 37, Remark 38), Lemma 43 and Lemmas 45–46. The text layer drops the bar on G = G/Z.

nodes.title: The maps θ^G and the congruence subgroups Φ^G, Φ^G_S
nodes.statement: For P ≤ Ḡ, θ^G_P : K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) → K′₁(Λ_𝒪(U_P)) → K′₁(Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)) = Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^× is the norm followed by abelianisation (just the norm when P is cyclic), θ^G = (θ^G_P)_{P≤Ḡ}, and θ^G_S, θ̂^G are the same maps on K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)_S) and K′₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S). The data: ver^{P′}_P : U_{P′}^ab → U_P^ab the transfer and ϕ : U_P → U_{P^p} the transfer for cyclic P, both extended to Iwasawa algebras with Frobenius on 𝒪 (Notations 40); for [P′,P′] ≤ P ≤ P′, the trace tr^{P′}_P, norm nr^{P′}_P and projection π^{P′}_P into Λ_𝒪(U_P/[U_{P′},U_{P′}]) (Definition 48); T_{P,P′} the image of x ↦ Σ_{g∈P′/P} g̃xg̃⁻¹ on Λ_𝒪(U_P), T_P = T_{P,N_ḠP} (Definition 49); and α_P(x) = x^p/∏_{k=0}^{p−1}ω_P^k(x) for nontrivial cyclic P, where ω_P is a fixed character of order p and ω_P(g) acts by g ↦ ω_P(g)g, and α_P(x) = x^p otherwise (Definition 47). Φ^G is the subgroup of ∏_{P≤Ḡ} Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^× of tuples (x_P) with M1: nr^{P′}_P(x_{P′}) = π^{P′}_P(x_P) whenever [P′,P′] ≤ P ≤ P′; M2: (x_P) is fixed by conjugation by G; M3: ver^{P′}_P(x_{P′}) ≡ x_P mod T_{P,P′} when [P′ : P] = p; M4: α_P(x_P) ≡ ∏_{P′} ϕ(α_{P′}(x_{P′})) mod pT_P for nontrivial cyclic P, over the cyclic P′ ≠ P with P′^p = P, and x_{1}^p ≡ ϕ(x_{1})∏_{P′} ϕ(α_{P′}(x_{P′})) mod pT_{1} over the nontrivial cyclic P′ with P′^p = 1. Φ^G_S and Φ̂^G_S impose the same conditions in ∏Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^×_S and ∏Λ̂_𝒪(U_P^ab)_S^× (Definition 51). For [P′ : P] = p and ω a nontrivial character of P′/P, nr^{P′}_P(x) = ∏_k ω^k(x) and tr^{P′}_P(x) = Σ_k ω^k(x) (Lemma 50).
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p, or a finite direct sum of such rings.
For 𝒪 = 𝒪₁ ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ 𝒪_n the groups split as ⊕ Φ^G_{𝒪_i} (Remark 54), so 𝒪 is unramified in the proofs.
proofSteps: Lemma 50: in the basis 1, g, …, g^{p−1} of R[P′^ab]^τ over R[P/[P′,P′]]^τ, multiplication by x = Σ a_i g^i is the twisted circulant matrix with rows (a₀, …, a_{p−1}), (g^p a_{p−1}, a₀, …), …; the vectors (1, ω^k(g)g, …, ω^k(g^{p−1})g^{p−1}) are eigenvectors with eigenvalues ω^k(x), so the determinant and trace are the product and sum.
M4 is well posed: α_C(x) ≡ 1 mod p for nontrivial cyclic C (Remark 83), and T_P is an ideal of Λ_𝒪(U_P)^{W_ḠP}.
acceptance: The conditions are the multiplicative analogue of the pair condition of Proposition 30 (Remark 54); compare l-elementary-case.

nodes.title: The additive maps t^G_P, η_P, β^G and the group ψ^G_R
nodes.statement: Let R = Λ_𝒪(Z) or Λ̂_𝒪(Z)_{(p)}. For P ≤ Ḡ, t^G_P : R[Conj Ḡ]^τ → R[P^ab]^τ is t^G_P([g]) = Σ_{x∈C(Ḡ,P)} {x⁻¹gx : x⁻¹gx ∈ P} over left coset representatives, independent of their choice. For cyclic P, η_P : R[P]^τ → R[P]^τ is the R-linear map with η_P(h) = h for generators h of P and 0 otherwise, i.e. η_P(x) = x − (1/p)Σ_k ω_P^k(x). β^G_P = η_P ∘ t^G_P for cyclic P and t^G_P otherwise, and β^G_R = (β^G_P)_P (Definition 55). For cyclic P, T_{P,R} is the image of x ↦ Σ_{g∈W_ḠP} gxg⁻¹ on R[P]^τ, W_ḠP = N_ḠP/P (Definition 56). ψ^G_R ⊂ ∏_{P≤Ḡ} R[P^ab]^τ is the group of tuples (a_P) with A1: for [P′,P′] ≤ P ≤ P′ (and [P′,P′] ≠ P if P is nontrivial cyclic), tr^{P′}_P(a_{P′}) = π^{P′}_P(a_P) if P is not cyclic, η_P(tr^{P′}_P(a_{P′})) = π^{P′}_P(a_P) if P is cyclic and P′ is not, and tr^{P′}_P(a_{P′}) = 0 if P′ is cyclic; A2: (a_P)_{P∈C(Ḡ)} is invariant under conjugation by Ḡ; A3: a_P ∈ T_{P,R} for every cyclic P (Definition 57). δ = Σ_{P cyclic} δ_P : ∏_P R[P^ab]^τ → R[Conj Ḡ]^τ[1/p], δ_P(x) = [x]/[Ḡ : P], is a left inverse of β^G_R (Definition 61, Lemma 62), and β^G_R lands in ψ^G_R (Lemma 60).
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p, or a finite direct sum of such rings.
R[Conj Ḡ]^τ is only an R-module (Remark 42).
proofSteps: Lemma 60, A1: tr^{P′}_P ∘ t^G_{P′} = π^{P′}_P ∘ t^G_P, since both send [h] to [P′ : P]·h for h ∈ P and to 0 otherwise; apply η_P when P is cyclic; if P < P′ are both cyclic, β^G_{P′}([g]) involves only generators of P′, whose traces to P vanish.
Lemma 60, A2: transport coset representatives, t^G_{g₁Pg₁⁻¹}([g]) = g₁t^G_P([g])g₁⁻¹. A3: t^G_P = t^{N_ḠP}_P ∘ t^G_{N_ḠP}, and t^{N_ḠP}_P([g]) = Σ_{x∈W_ḠP} x⁻¹gx ∈ T_{P,R} for g ∈ P.
Lemma 62: for P = ⟨g⟩ and its conjugates P′, δ(β([g])) = ([Ḡ : P])⁻¹ Σ_{P′}[N_ḠP′ : P′][g] = [g].
acceptance: Checked on Ḡ = C_p below, where ψ^G_R ≅ R^p.
