nodes.title: Kakde's additive theorem
nodes.statement: β^G_R induces an isomorphism R[Conj Ḡ]^τ ≅ ψ^G_R (Theorem 58). Moreover id_{ℚ_p} ⊗ β^G_R : ℚ_p ⊗ R[Conj Ḡ]^τ → ∏_P ℚ_p ⊗ R[P^ab]^τ is injective with image the tuples satisfying A1 and A2, and if (id ⊗ β^G_R)(a) = (a_P) with a_P ∈ T_{P,R} for every cyclic P, then a ∈ R[Conj Ḡ]^τ and a_P ∈ R[P^ab]^τ for all P (Proposition 64).
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p, or a finite direct sum of such rings.
proofSteps: Lemma 63, cyclic components: δ_P(a_P) and δ_{P′}(a_{P′}) can cancel only for conjugate P, P′, where A2 makes them equal; so δ((a_P)) = 0 gives a_P = 0 for cyclic P (the coefficients are constant on N_ḠP-orbits by A2).

Lemma 63, noncyclic components: take P′ of least order with a_{P′} ≠ 0, h₀ in its support and a maximal P ∋ h̃₀ of index p. If P is cyclic, h̃₀ generates P (otherwise A1 for P^p ⋊ C_p ≤ P′, or for {1} ≤ P′ = P × C_p, contradicts minimality), and η_P(tr^{P′}_P(a_{P′})) ≠ 0 = π^{P′}_P(a_P) contradicts A1; if P is not cyclic, the coefficient p·a_{h₀} of tr^{P′}_P(a_{P′}) contradicts A1.
δ(ψ^G_R) ⊆ R[Conj Ḡ]^τ: by A3 write a_P = Σ_{x∈W_ḠP} xb_Px⁻¹; summing δ over the conjugates of P gives [Ḡ : P]δ_P(b_P) ∈ R[Conj Ḡ]^τ.
Theorem 58: δ ∘ β = id (Lemma 62) and β(R[Conj Ḡ]^τ) ⊆ ψ^G_R (Lemma 60); δ injective on ψ^G_R gives β ∘ δ = id there.
Proposition 64 from Theorem 58 after ⊗ℚ_p; A2 puts a_P in ℚ_p ⊗ T_{P,R}, and δ recovers a from the cyclic components.
acceptance: Artin's induction theorem would give injectivity after projecting to cyclic P (Remark 59); Kakde proves injectivity directly, so no request is needed.
The cyclic test of additive-map-beta (Ḡ = C_p) is an instance.

nodes.title: The p-adic logarithm on relative K₁ of Iwasawa algebras
nodes.statement: Let R = Λ̂_𝒪(Z)_{(p)} and J_R the Jacobson radical of the local ring R[Ḡ]^τ. Then J_R/pR[Ḡ]^τ is nilpotent (Lemma 65). For every ideal I ⊆ J_R, Log(1 + x) = Σ_{i≥1}(−1)^{i+1}x^i/i (x ∈ I) induces a unique homomorphism log_I : K₁(R[Ḡ]^τ, I) → (I/[R[Ḡ]^τ, I]) ⊗_{ℤ_p} ℚ_p; if I ⊆ ξR[Ḡ]^τ for a central ξ with ξ^p ∈ pξR[Ḡ]^τ, it lands in I/[R[Ḡ]^τ, I], and it is an isomorphism if moreover I^p ⊆ pIJ_R (Proposition 67). For Λ_𝒪(G), with G_n = G/Z^{p^n} and F = Frac 𝒪, the logarithms log : K₁(𝒪[G_n]) → F[Conj G_n] of Oliver kill torsion and pass to the limit, log : K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) → lim_n F[Conj G_n] = F⟦Z⟧[Conj Ḡ]^τ.
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p, or a finite direct sum of such rings.
G pro-p, so R[Ḡ]^τ is local.
proofSteps: Lemma 65: over k = 𝒪/p there is an exact sequence 0 → J_R/p → Q(k⟦G⟧) → Q(k⟦Γ⟧) → 0; the kernel N of k⟦G⟧ → k⟦Γ⟧ is k⟦G⟧I_H with I_H nilpotent (H is a finite p-group), and by Lemma 37 the denominators can be taken central.

Lemma 66 (Oliver's Lemma 2.7 for twisted Iwasawa algebras): R[Ḡ]^τ is J_R-adically complete, so Log converges on 1 + I into I[1/p] (into I under the ξ-hypothesis, since then I^n ⊆ nI); Log(uv) ≡ Log u + Log v modulo U(I) = Σ_{m≥0,n≥1}(1/(m+n))[I^m, I^n] by summing the coefficients of cyclically equivalent words; under I^p ⊆ pIJ_R, Exp converges and inverts Log, and Exp([R[Ḡ]^τ, I]) ⊆ E(R[Ḡ]^τ, I) by Vaserstein's identity Exp(rx)Exp(xr)⁻¹ ∈ E(R[Ḡ]^τ, I) and successive approximation through D_k = ⟨rx − xr : rx, xr ∈ IJ_R^k⟩.

Proposition 67 (Oliver's Theorem 2.8): apply Lemma 66 to M_n(I) ⊆ M_n(R[Ḡ]^τ), compose with the trace Tr_n, note L_n([r, u]) = Tr_n(rLog(u)r⁻¹) − Tr_n(Log u) = 0, and pass to K₁(R[Ḡ]^τ, I) = GL(R[Ḡ]^τ, I)/[GL(R[Ḡ]^τ), GL(R[Ḡ]^τ, I)].
The logarithm on K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) is Oliver's finite-level one in the limit (see the gap on Oliver's book).
acceptance: Kakde notes (Remark 68) that for R = Λ̂_𝒪(Z)_{(p)} it is unclear whether log_{J_R} extends canonically to K₁(R[Ḡ]^τ); only log_{J_R} is used.

sources.match: Proposition 67 with Lemmas 65–66 (pp. 42–47), Remark 68, and the limit of finite-level logarithms (p. 47).

nodes.title: The integral logarithm on K′₁ of Iwasawa algebras
nodes.statement: Let ϕ be the endomorphism of R (Frobenius on 𝒪, p-power map on Z), extended to R[Conj Ḡ]^τ by [g] ↦ [g^p] (Definition 69). Oliver–Taylor's integral logarithm L = log − (ϕ/p)log : K′₁(𝒪[G_n]) → 𝒪[Conj G_n] sits in an exact sequence 1 → μ(𝒪) × G_n^ab → K′₁(𝒪[G_n]) → 𝒪[Conj G_n] → G_n^ab → 1 with ω(Σ a_g g) = ∏ g^{tr_{𝒪/ℤ_p}(a_g)} (Oliver, Theorem 6.6); its inverse limit is L : K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) → Λ_𝒪(Z)[Conj Ḡ]^τ with 1 → μ(𝒪) × G^ab → K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) → Λ_𝒪(Z)[Conj Ḡ]^τ → G^ab → 1 exact (Definition 70). On the completed localisation, with J = ker(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S → Λ̂_𝒪(Γ)_{(p)}) and the splitting Γ ↪ G, every x ∈ K′₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S) is x = uy with u in the image of K₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S, J) and y ∈ K′₁(Λ̂_𝒪(Γ)_{(p)}) (Lemma 71); y^p/ϕ(y) ≡ 1 mod p (Lemma 72); and L(uy) = log(u) − (ϕ/p)log(u) + (1/p)log(y^p/ϕ(y)) is a homomorphism K′₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S) → Λ̂_𝒪(Z)_{(p)}[Conj Ḡ]^τ, independent of the splitting (Definition 73, Proposition 74).
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p, or a finite direct sum of such rings.
G pro-p; 𝒪 unramified, so (p) is the maximal ideal of 𝒪.
proofSteps: Definition 70: the sequences (9) for n ≥ 0 are compatible sequences of profinite groups, so the inverse limit is exact (the finite-level sequence is Oliver's; see the gap on Oliver's book).
Lemma 71: Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S is local, so its units surject onto K′₁ and 1 + J onto K₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S, J); 1 → 1 + J → Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S^× → Λ̂_𝒪(Γ)_{(p)}^× → 1 splits by Γ ↪ G.
Lemma 72: modulo p, Λ̂_𝒪(Γ)_{(p)} is the domain 𝔽_q⟦X⟧, on which ϕ is X ↦ (1 + X)^p − 1 = X^p with Frobenius on 𝔽_q, so y^p = ϕ(y).

Integrality: L(1 − v) ≡ Σ_k (v^{pk} − ϕ(v^k))/(pk) modulo the integral elements, and pk ∣ v^{pk} − ϕ(v^k) follows from p^n ∣ v^{p^n} − ϕ(v^{p^{n−1}}), proved by grouping the monomials of v^{p^n} into orbits under cyclic permutation (legitimate because τ is symmetric) and p^t ∣ r̂^{p^t} − ϕ(r̂^{p^{t−1}}).

Independence of the splitting: the finitely many splittings agree on an open A ≤ G; L is independent on the images of K₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S, J_R) and K₁(Λ̂_𝒪(A)_S), whose product has torsion cokernel in K′₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S), and the target is torsion free.
acceptance: Kakde leaves the kernel and cokernel of L on K′₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S) open (Remark 75, citing Ritter–Weiss); only the homomorphism is planned.

nodes.title: The additive and multiplicative sides: β^G(L(x)) through θ^G(x)
nodes.statement: Define v^G_P on ∏_C F⟦Z⟧[C^ab] by v^G_P((x_C)) = Σ_{P′} ([P′ : P′^p]/[P : P′^p])ϕ(x_{P′}) over cyclic P′ with P′^p ≤ P when P is not cyclic, and Σ_{P′ ≠ P′^p = P} [P′ : P′^p]ϕ(x_{P′}) when P is cyclic (Definition 78); and u^G_P on ∏_C Λ_𝒪(U_C^ab)^× by u^G_P((x_C)) = ∏_{P′^p ≤ P} ϕ(x_{P′})^{|P′|} for noncyclic P and ∏_{P′ ≠ P′^p = P} ϕ(x_{P′}) for cyclic P, over cyclic P′ (Definition 80). Then for x ∈ K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)): β^G_P(L(x)) = (1/(p²|P|))log(α_P(θ^G_P(x))^{p|P|}/u^G_P(α(θ^G(x)))) for noncyclic P; β^G_P(L(x)) = (1/p)log(α_P(θ^G_P(x))/u^G_P(α(θ^G(x)))) for nontrivial cyclic P; and β^G_{1}(L(x)) = (1/p)log(α_{1}(θ^G_{1}(x))/(ϕ(θ^G_{1}(x))u^G_{1}(α(θ^G(x))))) (Proposition 84); the same holds on K′₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S). The logarithms are defined: α_P(θ^G_P(x))^{p|P|} ≡ u^G_P(α(θ^G(x))) mod p for noncyclic P (Lemma 82), and the cyclic quotients are ≡ 1 mod p (Remark 83).
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p, or a finite direct sum of such rings.
proofSteps: Lemma 76: log ∘ θ^G_P = t^G_P ∘ log (Oliver, Theorem 6.8); in the completed case from log(u) = lim p^{−n}(u^{p^n} − 1) and θ̂^G_P(u) = lim (1 + t^G_P(u^{p^n} − 1))^{1/p^n}.
Lemma 77: log ∘ α_P = pη_P ∘ log for nontrivial cyclic P, since ω_P commutes with log and η_P = (1/p)(p − Σ_k ω_P^k).
Lemma 79: β^G_P ∘ ϕ = v^G_P ∘ β^G for P ≠ {1}, and β^G_{1} ∘ ϕ = (ϕ + v^G_{1}) ∘ β^G, by counting cosets.
Lemma 81: log ∘ u^G_P = |P|·v^G_P ∘ log for noncyclic P and (1/p)·v^G_P ∘ log for cyclic P, by naturality of log.

Lemma 82: modulo p, α_C(θ^G_C(x)) ≡ 1 for nontrivial cyclic C and θ^G_P(x)^{|P|} ≡ θ^G_{1}(x), the latter by Schneider–Venjakob, Proposition 2.3 (on K₁(𝔽_p⟦H⟧), the norm to an open normal N followed by the inclusion is x ↦ x^{[H:N]}).

Proposition 84 by chaining Lemmas 76, 77, 79 and 81. On the completed ring write x = uy (Lemma 71): u is handled identically; for y ∈ Λ̂_𝒪(Z)_{(p)}, θ^G_P(y) = y^{[Ḡ:P]}, α_P(θ^G_P(y)) = 1 for nontrivial cyclic P and β^G_P(L(y)) = [Ḡ : P]L(y) or 0; a general y has ϕ^r(y) ∈ Λ̂_𝒪(Z)_{(p)} and y^{p^r}/ϕ^r(y) ≡ 1 mod p, and the targets are torsion free.
acceptance: At Ḡ = 1 both sides are (1/p)log(x^p/ϕ(x)).

sources.match: Proposition 84 with Lemmas 76, 77, 79, 81, 82, Definitions 78, 80 and Remark 83 (pp. 51–58).
Proposition 2.3 continues: K₁(Ω(H)) → K₁(Ω(N)) → K₁(Ω(H)), the norm followed by the canonical map, is x ↦ x^{[H:N]}, with Ω = 𝔽_p⟦−⟧. This is the input to Kakde's Lemma 82.

nodes.title: The multiplicative sequence for Φ^G
nodes.statement: θ^G(K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G))) ⊆ Φ^G and θ̂^G_S(K′₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S)) ⊆ Φ̂^G_S (Lemma 85). The map μ(𝒪) × G^ab → ∏_P Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^×, the identity on μ(𝒪) and the transfer G^ab → U_P^ab in each component, is injective and commutes with θ^G (Lemma 86). There is a surjection ω : ψ^G → G^ab, ω((a_P)) = ω(a_Ḡ), with ω ∘ β^G = ω (Lemma 87). The map ℒ = (ℒ_P) : Φ^G → ψ^G, with ℒ_P((x_C)) given by the right-hand sides of Proposition 84 with x_C in place of θ^G_C(x), sits in an exact sequence 1 → μ(𝒪) × G^ab → Φ^G → ψ^G → G^ab → 1 (Lemma 88).
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p, or a finite direct sum of such rings.
proofSteps: Lemma 85, M1: the norm to U_P equals the norm to U_{P′} followed by nr^{P′}_P after abelianising, because the bases agree. M2: the norm is conjugation-equivariant.

Lemma 85, M3: write x = Σ x_k g^k over Λ_𝒪(U_P) for g ∈ U_{P′} ∖ U_P; the norm is the determinant of the twisted circulant matrix, whose terms not fixed by σ = conjugation by g cancel modulo T_{P,P′}, and Σ_h a_h^p ∏_k σ^k(h) ≡ Σ_h ϕ(a_h)∏_k σ^k(h) = ver^{P′}_P modulo T_{P,P′}.
Lemma 85, M4: by Proposition 84 and Lemma 60, pβ^G_P(L(x)) = log(α_P(θ^G_P(x))/u^G_P(α(θ^G(x)))) ∈ pT_P, and log : 1 + pT_P ≅ pT_P.
Lemma 89: if C^p ⊆ P′ but C^p ⊄ P with [P′ : P] = p, then nr^{P′}_P(ϕ(α_C(x_C))) = 1, by Lemma 50.
ℒ lands in ψ^G: A1 by cases (P not cyclic; P cyclic and P′ not, using α_P(ϕ(α_C(x_C))) = 1 unless C^p = P; P′ cyclic by Lemma 89) from M1; A2 and A3 from M2 and M4; integrality from Proposition 64.

Exactness at Φ^G: ℒ((x_P)) = 0 gives α_P(x_P) = u^G_P(α((x_C))) for cyclic P, hence α_P(x_P) = 1 by induction from the maximal cyclic P; so x_P is torsion, hence in μ(𝒪) × U_P^ab (Higman's theorem), for noncyclic P, and x_{1} ∈ μ(𝒪) × U_{1} by Definition 70; M1 with Lemma 50 and induction extend this to all cyclic P, and M3 with induction on [Ḡ : P] puts (x_P) in the image of μ(𝒪) × G^ab.

Exactness at ψ^G: summing (1/[Ḡ : P])ℒ_P gives ℒ_Ḡ((x_C)) = (1/p)log(x_Ḡ^p/ϕ(x_Ḡ)), so ω ∘ ℒ = 1 by Definition 70; conversely lift a ∈ ker ω through the additive theorem and L to x ∈ K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)), and ℒ(θ^G(x)) = β^G(L(x)) = a.
acceptance: Higman's theorem (the torsion units of Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab) are μ(𝒪) × U_P^ab) is a cited input (see the gap on Oliver's book).

nodes.title: Kakde's congruence description of K′₁
nodes.statement: Let G be a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with G/H ≅ ℤ_p, Z ≤ G central open pro-cyclic, Ḡ = G/Z, and 𝒪 the integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p or a finite direct sum of such rings. Then θ^G induces an isomorphism K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) ≅ Φ^G (Theorem 52); θ^G_S maps K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)_S) into Φ^G_S, and Φ^G_S ∩ ∏_{P≤Ḡ} Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^× = θ^G(K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G))) (Theorem 53).
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p, or a finite direct sum of such rings.
proofSteps: Reduce to 𝒪 unramified over ℤ_p (Remark 54).

Theorem 52: the five lemma on the ladder μ(𝒪) × G^ab → K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) → Λ_𝒪(Z)[Conj Ḡ]^τ → G^ab (integral-logarithm) over μ(𝒪) × G^ab → Φ^G → ψ^G → G^ab (phi-integral-log-sequence), with θ^G, β^G (an isomorphism by additive-theorem) and the identities as vertical maps; the squares commute by Lemmas 86–87 and ℒ ∘ θ^G = β^G ∘ L (theta-beta-relation).
Theorem 53: θ^G_S lands in Φ̂^G_S ∩ ∏Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^×_S = Φ^G_S (Lemma 85 on the completed ring), and Φ^G_S ∩ ∏Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^× = Φ^G, which is θ^G(K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G))) by Theorem 52.
acceptance: Source-qualified: G pro-p of dimension one and 𝒪 unramified. The general one-dimensional G reaches this case through reduction-to-p-elementary, with 𝒪 = ℤ_p[Δ] ≅ ⊕_χ 𝒪_χ.
Checked on Ḡ = 1 and Ḡ = C₂ in congruence-group-phi's tests.

nodes.title: K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) injects into K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)_S)
nodes.statement: Let G be a compact p-adic Lie group with a quotient G/H ≅ ℤ_p, and 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p. Then the map K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) → K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)_S) is injective (Corollary 90).
hypotheses: G compact p-adic Lie with G/H ≅ ℤ_p; 𝒪 unramified.
proofSteps: G pro-p of dimension one: θ^G_S composed with K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) → K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)_S) is θ^G followed by the injection ∏Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^× ↪ ∏Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^×_S, and θ^G is injective (Theorem 52).

G of dimension one: reduction-to-qp-elementary, l-elementary-case and reduction-to-p-elementary each carry the injectivity of K′₁ → K′₁ of the localisation from their subquotients to G; they end at Δ × G_p with 𝒪[Δ] ≅ ⊕_χ 𝒪_χ unramified, which is the pro-p case.

Arbitrary dimension: if x ↦ 1 in K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)_S), then for every open U ≤ H normal in G and pro-p its image in K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G/U)_S) is 1, hence its image in K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G/U)) is 1 by the dimension-one case, and x = 1 because K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) ≅ lim_U K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G/U)) (k1-prime, Corollary 20).
acceptance: The source prints the corollary without a proof (p. 65). The route above is reconstructed and flagged. It runs the §4 reductions with 𝒪 = ℤ_p, as printed; a larger unramified 𝒪 needs the same reductions over 𝒪, which Kakde does not write out.

sources.match: Corollary 90, stated after the proofs of Theorems 52–53; no proof is printed.

nodes.title: The main conjecture as congruences between abelian zeta functions
nodes.statement: Let F_∞/F be admissible with μ = 0 and Gal(F_∞/F) = Δ × G, with Δ cyclic of order prime to p and G a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group; fix Z ≤ G central open pro-cyclic, Ḡ = G/Z. For P ≤ Ḡ put F_P = F_∞^{Δ×U_P} and K_P = F_∞^{[U_P,U_P]}, so that Gal(K_P/F_P) = Δ × U_P^ab, and let ζ_P ∈ Λ(Δ × U_P^ab)^×_S be the Deligne–Ribet (Cassou-Noguès, Barsky) p-adic zeta function of K_P/F_P (Notations 91). Then MC(F_∞/F) holds if and only if (ζ_P)_P ∈ Φ^G_S, where Φ^G_S = Φ^G_{ℤ_p[Δ],S} (Proposition 93). Every irreducible Artin representation ρ of G has a one-dimensional χ inflated from Γ with ρ ⊗ χ trivial on Z (Lemma 92).
hypotheses: F_∞/F admissible, μ = 0, p odd; Gal(F_∞/F) = Δ × G as stated.
proofSteps: Lemma 92 by induction on |G/Z|: by Clifford (Serre, Proposition 24) either ρ|_Z is isotypic, and χ = χ_i^{−1} works, or ρ = Ind_A^G η for a proper A ⊇ Z, and a χ for η on Γ^{p^r} extends to Γ.

If: take f ∈ K′₁(Λ(Δ × G)_S) with ∂f = −[C(F_∞/F)] (boundary-surjective-p-torsion). By Theorem 53, θ_S(f) = (f_P) ∈ Φ^G_S. Since ∂ζ_P = ∂f_P = −[C(K_P/F_P)] (abelian-case and base change of C), u_P = ζ_Pf_P^{−1} lies in K′₁(Λ(Δ × U_P^ab)), and (u_P) ∈ Φ^G_S ∩ ∏Λ(Δ × U_P^ab)^× = θ(K′₁(Λ(Δ × G))) (Theorem 53); with θ(u) = (u_P) (Theorem 52), ζ = uf has ∂ζ = −[C(F_∞/F)].

Interpolation: for irreducible ρ choose σ by Lemma 92, so ρ ⊗ σ factors through the p-group Ḡ and equals Ind_{U_P}^G η for some P ≤ Ḡ (Serre, Theorem 16: representations of supersolvable groups are monomial); then ρ = Ind_{U_P}^G(η ⊗ σ^{−1}) and ζ(χρκ^r) = ζ_P(χησ^{−1}κ^r_{F_P}) = L_{Σ_P}(χησ^{−1}, 1 − r) = L_Σ(χρ, 1 − r) by inductivity of Artin L-functions.
Only if (not printed): if ζ satisfies MC, the components of θ_S(ζ) interpolate the same values as the ζ_P, hence equal them, so (ζ_P) = θ_S(ζ) ∈ Φ^G_S by Theorem 53.
acceptance: The printed proof gives the 'if' direction; the converse is the standard argument and is flagged as reconstructed.
This is burns-kato-patching with Φ = Φ^G, Φ_S = Φ^G_S and the pairs (U_P, [U_P, U_P]).
Theorem 94 then reduces MC to M1–M4 for (ζ_P); M1–M2 are zeta-tuple-m1-m2, and M3–M4 (Propositions 96–99, §§6.2–6.13) are the next checkpoint.

nodes.title: The abelian zeta functions satisfy M1 and M2
nodes.statement: In the setting of main-conjecture-congruence-criterion, the tuple (ζ_P)_P satisfies M1: nr^{P′}_P(ζ_{P′}) = π^{P′}_P(ζ_P) in Λ(Δ × U_P/[U_{P′}, U_{P′}])_S whenever [P′, P′] ≤ P ≤ P′; and M2: gζ_Pg^{−1} = ζ_{gPg^{−1}} in Λ(Δ × U_{gPg^{−1}}^ab)_S for every g ∈ G (Proposition 95).
hypotheses: As in main-conjecture-congruence-criterion.
proofSteps: M1: for an irreducible Artin representation ρ of U_P/[U_{P′}, U_{P′}], a character χ of Δ and r divisible by [F_∞(μ_p) : F_∞], nr^{P′}_P(ζ_{P′})(χρκ^r) = ζ_{P′}(χ Ind_{U_P}^{U_{P′}}(ρ)κ^r) = L_{Σ_{P′}}(χ Ind ρ, 1 − r) = L_{Σ_P}(χρ, 1 − r) = π^{P′}_P(ζ_P)(χρκ^r).
Two elements of the abelian Λ(Δ × U_P/[U_{P′}, U_{P′}])_S interpolating the same values on this dense set of characters are equal.
M2: (gζ_Pg^{−1})(χρκ^r) = ζ_P(χ gρg^{−1} κ^r) = L_Σ(χ Ind_{U_P}^G(gρg^{−1}), 1 − r) and ζ_{gPg^{−1}}(χρκ^r) = L_Σ(χ Ind_{U_{gPg^{−1}}}^G ρ, 1 − r), and the two induced representations agree.
acceptance: M3 and M4 remain: Proposition 96 is M3, and Propositions 97–99 with §6.13 give M4 (next checkpoint).

nodes.title: Partial zeta values and the smoothed values Δ^u_P
nodes.statement: For j ≥ 0 and a coset x of Z^{p^j} in Δ × U_P^ab, δ(x) is its characteristic function and ζ(δ(x), s) = Σ_𝔞 δ(x)(g_𝔞)N𝔞^{−s} (Re s > 1, over integral ideals 𝔞 of F_P prime to Σ_P, g_𝔞 the Artin symbol) is the partial zeta function; by Klingen and Siegel it continues meromorphically with a simple pole at s = 1 only, and ζ(δ(x), 1 − k) ∈ ℚ for even k ≥ 2. For a locally constant ε = Σ ε(x)δ(x) with values in a ℚ-vector space V, L_{Σ_P}(ε, 1 − k) = Σ_x ε(x)ζ(δ(x), 1 − k) ∈ V (15); for a degree-one Artin character it is the Σ_P-truncated L-value. For ε locally constant ℚ_p-valued, u ∈ U_P^ab and k divisible by [F_∞(μ_p) : F_∞], Δ^u_P(ε, 1 − k) = L_{Σ_P}(ε, 1 − k) − κ(u)^k L_{Σ_P}(ε_u, 1 − k) with ε_u(g) = ε(ug) (16). These values are invariant under conjugation: Δ^u_P(δ(y), 1 − k) = Δ^u_{gPg^{−1}}(δ(gyg^{−1}), 1 − k) for u ∈ Z, g ∈ G (Lemma 103).
hypotheses: F_∞/F is admissible with μ = 0 and p odd; Gal(F_∞/F) = Δ × G with Δ cyclic of order prime to p and G a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group; Z ≤ G is central open pro-cyclic, Ḡ = G/Z, U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ, F_P = F_∞^{Δ×U_P}, d_P = [F_P : F], r_P = [F_P : ℚ], Σ_P the primes of F_P above Σ, and ζ_P the Deligne–Ribet p-adic zeta function of the abelian extension with group Δ × U_P^ab (Notations 91).
proofSteps: L_{Σ_P}(ε, 1 − k) is well defined: refining j splits δ(x) into the δ of its sub-cosets, and ζ is additive in δ.

Lemma 103: for Re s > 1, ζ(δ(gyg^{−1}), s) = Σ_𝔞 δ(y)(g_{𝔞^g})N(𝔞^g)^{−s} = ζ(δ(y), s) by reindexing 𝔞 ↦ 𝔞^g, and meromorphic continuation carries the equality to s = 1 − k; δ(y)_u = δ(u^{−1}y) and u ∈ Z is central.
acceptance: The Klingen–Siegel rationality and continuation are cited inputs, requested with the Deligne–Ribet package from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3.

nodes.title: Finite-level approximations of the abelian zeta functions
nodes.statement: Let f be such that κ^{p−1}(Z) = 1 + p^fℤ_p. For P normal in P′ let T_{P,P′,j} be the image of x ↦ Σ_{g∈P′/P} gxg^{−1} on ℤ_p[Δ × U_P^ab/Z^{p^j}]/(p^{f+j}), T_{P,j} = T_{P,N_ḠP,j} (Definition 100). Then Λ(Δ × U_P^ab) ≅ lim_j ℤ_p[Δ × U_P^ab/Z^{p^j}]/(p^{f+j}), and T_{P,P′} ≅ lim_j T_{P,P′,j} (Lemma 101). For u ∈ U_P^ab, j ≥ 0 and k divisible by [F_∞(μ_p) : F_∞], the image of (1 − u)ζ_P in ℤ_p[Δ × U_P^ab/Z^{p^j}]/(p^{f+j}) is Σ_x Δ^u_P(δ(x), 1 − k)κ(x)^{−k}x mod p^{f+j}; in particular the limit does not depend on k (Proposition 102, attributed to Ritter–Weiss).
hypotheses: F_∞/F is admissible with μ = 0 and p odd; Gal(F_∞/F) = Δ × G with Δ cyclic of order prime to p and G a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group; Z ≤ G is central open pro-cyclic, Ḡ = G/Z, U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ, F_P = F_∞^{Δ×U_P}, d_P = [F_P : F], r_P = [F_P : ℚ], Σ_P the primes of F_P above Σ, and ζ_P the Deligne–Ribet p-adic zeta function of the abelian extension with group Δ × U_P^ab (Notations 91).
proofSteps: Lemma 101: a compatible family (x_j) lifts canonically — for t ≥ j the images of x_t in ℤ_p[Δ × U^ab/Z^{p^j}]/(p^{f+t}) converge to x̃_j — and the x̃_j form an element of the limit; for T_{P,P′} pass to the limit in 0 → ker(tr_{P,P′,j}) → ℤ_p[…]/(p^{f+j}) → T_{P,P′,j} → 0, exact on the right because the groups are finite.
Step 1: the sums form an inverse system, since κ(x)^k ≡ κ(y)^k mod p^{f+j} when x ↦ y.

Step 2: independence of k is congruence (17), Δ^u_P(δ(x), 1 − k)κ(x)^{−k} ≡ Δ^u_P(δ(x), 1 − k′)κ(x)^{−k′} mod p^{f+j}; with η locally constant, η^{[F_∞(μ_p):F_∞]} ≡ κ^{[F_∞(μ_p):F_∞]} mod p^{f+j}, and ε_k = p^{−f−j}η^{−k}δ(x), the function ε_kκ^{k−1} − ε_{k′}κ^{k′−1} is ℤ_p-valued, so Deligne–Ribet Theorem 0.4 applies.

Step 3: ζ_u = lim_j(Σ_x Δ^u_P(δ(x), 1 − k)κ(x)^{−k}x) satisfies ζ_u(κ^kε) = Δ^u_P(ε, 1 − k) = (1 − u)ζ_P(κ^kε) for all locally constant ε, by the Deligne–Ribet construction of ζ_P; so (1 − u)ζ_P = ζ_u.
acceptance: The Deligne–Ribet congruences (their Theorem 0.4) and the interpolation property of ζ_P are imported from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3.

nodes.title: Reduction of the basic congruences to congruences between values
nodes.statement: The basic congruences follow from congruences between the smoothed values Δ, for all j, all cosets y of Z^{p^j}, all u ∈ Z and all k divisible by [F_∞(μ_p) : F_∞]: (10) follows from (18), Δ^{u^p}_P(δ(y), 1 − k) ≡ Δ^u_{P′}(δ(y)∘ver^{P′}_P, 1 − pk) mod pℤ_p for y fixed by P′ (Proposition 104); (11) from (22), Δ^{u^{d_P}}_P(δ(y), 1 − k) ≡ 0 mod |(W_ḠP)_y|ℤ_p for y whose image generates P (Proposition 106); (12) from (24), Δ^{u^{d_P}}_P(δ(y), 1 − k) ≡ Σ_{P′} Δ^{u^{d_P/p}}_{P′}(δ(y)∘ϕ, 1 − pk) mod |(W_ḠP)_y|ℤ_p over P′ ≠ P with P′^p = P (Proposition 107); (13) from (28), Δ^{u^{pd_{P′}}}_P(δ(y), 1 − k) ≡ Δ^{u^{d_{P′}}}_{P′}(δ(y)∘ϕ, 1 − pk) mod |(N_ḠP′/P)_y|ℤ_p (Proposition 108); and (14) from (29), Δ^{u^{p|Ḡ|}}_0(δ(y), 1 − k) ≡ Δ^{u^{|Ḡ|}}_{{1}}(δ(y)∘ϕ, 1 − pk) mod p|Ḡ|ℤ_p (Proposition 108).
hypotheses: F_∞/F is admissible with μ = 0 and p odd; Gal(F_∞/F) = Δ × G with Δ cyclic of order prime to p and G a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group; Z ≤ G is central open pro-cyclic, Ḡ = G/Z, U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ, F_P = F_∞^{Δ×U_P}, d_P = [F_P : F], r_P = [F_P : ℚ], Σ_P the primes of F_P above Σ, and ζ_P the Deligne–Ribet p-adic zeta function of the abelian extension with group Δ × U_P^ab (Notations 91).
proofSteps: Proposition 104: by Proposition 102, (1 − u^p)ζ_P and (1 − u^p)ver^{P′}_P(ζ_{P′}) have images (19) and (20) at level j; ver^{P′}_P is injective on Δ × U_{P′}^ab/V_{P,P′}Z^{p^{j−1}} with V_{P,P′} = ker ver and κ(V_{P,P′})^k = 1, and κ(y)^k = κ(x)^{pk} for y = ver(x). The difference (21) is summed over P′-orbits: a P′-fixed y contributes a multiple of py = tr(y) ∈ T_{P,P′,j} by (18), and a free orbit contributes (Δ − Δ)κ(y)^{−k}Σ_g gyg^{−1} ∈ T_{P,P′,j} by Lemma 103. Lemma 101 and the centrality of u give (10).

Remark 105: Propositions 106–108 follow the same pattern with ω^k_P, ϕ and the Weyl-group orbits: in 106 the W_ḠP-orbit of a y generating P contributes Δκ^{−k}Σ(gyg^{−1} − ω^k_P(gyg^{−1})) ∈ 𝔭T_{P,j} by (22); in 107 the orbit sum lies in T_{P,j}; in 108 the N_ḠP′/P-orbit sum lies in T_{P,N_ḠP′,j}.
acceptance: The printed proofs contain misprints recorded as E5 and E6: the placement of ∘ver in (21), and 1 − p for 1 − k in the proof of Proposition 106.

nodes.title: Hilbert Eisenstein series, restriction along the diagonal and the q-expansion principle
nodes.statement: For L totally real of degree r, Hilbert modular forms of weight k on Γ₀₀(𝔣) have standard q-expansions c(0, f) + Σ_μ c(μ, f)q^μ_L over totally positive μ ∈ 𝒪_L (§6.6). For L′ ⊇ L of degree r′, restriction along the diagonal R_{L′/L} maps M_k(Γ₀₀(𝔣𝒪_{L′})) to M_{r′k}(Γ₀₀(𝔣)) with c(μ, R_{L′/L}f) = Σ_{tr(ν)=μ} c(ν, f) (§6.7), and its constant term at the cusp of α is that of f at α^* (Lemma 109). For β ∈ 𝒪_L totally positive with 𝔣 ⊆ β𝒪_L, the Hecke operator U_β has c(μ, f|U_β) = c(μβ, f) (Lemma 110). Deligne–Ribet: for locally constant ε on Gal(L_Σ/L) and even k ≥ 2 there is G_{k,ε} ∈ M_k(Γ₀₀(𝔣)) with q-expansion 2^{−r}L(ε, 1 − k) + Σ_μ(Σ_{𝔞∋μ} ε(g_𝔞)N𝔞^{k−1})q^μ and constant term N^k((α))2^{−r}L(ε_g, 1 − k) at the cusp of α (Proposition 111); the q-expansion principle: if f ∈ M_k(Γ₀₀(𝔣), ℚ) has non-constant standard coefficients in ℤ_(p), then c(0, f) − N(α_p)^{−k}c(0, α, f) ∈ ℤ_p (§6.11); hence c(0, G_{k,ε}) − N(α_p)^{−k}c(0, α, G_{k,ε}) = 2^{−r}Δ^u(ε, 1 − k) when α has Artin symbol u (Remark 112).
hypotheses: L totally real; Σ a finite set of finite primes containing those above p; 𝔣 an integral ideal supported on Σ.
proofSteps: Lemma 109: (R_{L′/L}f)|α = R_{L′/L}(f|α^*), and constant terms are read off at τ → i∞.
Lemma 110: U_β is the double coset of diag(β, 1), f|U_β(τ) = N(β)^{k/2−1}Σ_b f|(1 b; 0 β), and the character sum Σ_b e^{2πi tr(μb/β)} is N(β) for μ ∈ β𝒪_L and 0 otherwise.
Proposition 111 and the q-expansion principle are Deligne–Ribet (Proposition 6.1, 2.22, 0.3 and 5.13–5.15); Remark 112 combines them with N((α))^kN(α_p)^{−k} = κ(u)^k.
acceptance: Deligne–Ribet's Eisenstein series, their constant terms at cusps and the q-expansion principle are requested from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3, which the atlas makes their owner.

sources.locator: §§6.6–6.11, Lemmas 109–110, Proposition 111 and Remark 112, pp. 77–81 (arXiv v3)
sources.match: The Hilbert-modular toolkit of §§6.6–6.11; Lemmas 109 and 110 are proved in the text, Proposition 111 and the q-expansion principle are cited to Deligne–Ribet.

nodes.title: The transfer into a maximal cyclic subgroup misses its generators
nodes.statement: Let P ∈ C(Ḡ) be such that no P′ ∈ C(Ḡ) has P′^p = P, and let P ⊊ N ≤ N_ḠP. Then the image of the transfer ver : N^ab → P is a proper subgroup of P (Lemma 114).
hypotheses: Ḡ a finite p-group.
proofSteps: With double coset representatives x_j of ⟨g⟩\N/P and m the order of g, ver(g) = ∏_j x_j^{−1}g^mx_j.
If g ∉ P, g^m is not a generator of P by the hypothesis on P, so neither is ver(g).
If g ∈ P, ver(g) = ∏_{x∈N/P} x^{−1}gx; N acts trivially on the order-p subgroup of P, so ver(g)^{p^{r−1}} = ∏ g^{p^{r−1}} = g^{p^{r−1}[N:P]} = 1 for #⟨g⟩ = p^r, since p divides [N : P].
acceptance: Used in Proposition 115: nontrivial stabilisers kill δ(y)(g_𝔟).

nodes.title: The value congruences via Hilbert Eisenstein series
nodes.statement: The value congruences (18), (22), (24), (28) and (29) of basic-congruence-reduction hold (Propositions 113, 115, 116 and 117). In each case an Eisenstein combination E is formed: E = R_{F_P/F_{P′}}(G_{k,δ(y)})|U_p − G_{pk,δ(y)∘ver} for (18); E = R_{F_P/F_{W_ḠP}}(G_{k,δ(y)}) for (22); E = R_{F_P/F_{W_ḠP}}(G_{k,δ(y)})|U_{d_P} − Σ_{P′}R_{F_{P′}/F_{W_ḠP}}(G_{pk,δ(y)∘ϕ})|U_{d_P/p} for (24); and similarly for (28) and (29). Its constant-term difference is 2^{−r} times the required difference of Δ-values, and its non-constant coefficients lie in the required ideal, so the q-expansion principle gives the congruence.
hypotheses: F_∞/F is admissible with μ = 0 and p odd; Gal(F_∞/F) = Δ × G with Δ cyclic of order prime to p and G a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group; Z ≤ G is central open pro-cyclic, Ḡ = G/Z, U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ, F_P = F_∞^{Δ×U_P}, d_P = [F_P : F], r_P = [F_P : ℚ], Σ_P the primes of F_P above Σ, and ζ_P the Deligne–Ribet p-adic zeta function of the abelian extension with group Δ × U_P^ab (Notations 91).
proofSteps: Proposition 113 (M3): the non-constant coefficient of E at μ is Σ_{(𝔟,η)}δ(y)(g_𝔟)N𝔟^{k−1} − Σ_𝔞 δ(y)(g_{𝔞𝒪_{F_P}})N𝔞^{pk−1}; P′/P-fixed pairs come from 𝔞 with N𝔟 = N𝔞^p, contributing δ(y)(g_𝔟)(N𝔞^{p(k−1)} − N𝔞^{pk−1}) ∈ pℤ_(p) by Fermat; free orbits contribute p times a term; and 2^{−r_P} ≡ 2^{−r_{P′}} mod p.

Proposition 115: for E = R(G_{k,δ(y)}), (W_ḠP)_y acts on the pairs (𝔟, ν); a nontrivial stabiliser V gives δ(y)(g_𝔟) = 0 by transfer-image-not-generator, and free orbits contribute |(W_ḠP)_y| times a term.
Propositions 116–117: orbits with stabiliser V contribute |(W_ḠP)_y/V|δ(y)(g_𝔟)(N𝔠^{|V|(k−1)} − N𝔠^{|V|(pk−1)/p}) ∈ |(W_ḠP)_y|ℤ_(p), since N𝔠^{|V|} ≡ N𝔠^{|V|/p} mod |V|.

The comparison of 2^{−r_P} with 2^{−r_P/p} (116) and 2^{−r_{P′}} (117) holds modulo p^{v_p(r_P)}, because r_P − r_P/p is divisible by φ(p^{v_p(r_P)}); |(W_ḠP)_y| and |(N_ḠP′/P)_y| divide d_P, hence p^{v_p(r_P)}. The printed justification, modulo r_P, is false in general (E7).
acceptance: Checked numerically in the suggested file: the Fermat step for p = 3, the |V| = 9 congruence, and the counterexample r_P = 15, p = 3 to the printed step.

sources.match: Propositions 113, 115, 116 and 117 with their proofs (the proof for (29) is said to be similar).

nodes.title: The basic congruences between abelian zeta functions
nodes.statement: The tuple (ζ_P) satisfies (10) ver^{P′}_P(ζ_{P′}) ≡ ζ_P mod T_{P,P′,S} for [P′ : P] = p, which is M3 (Proposition 96); (11) ζ_P ≡ ω^k_P(ζ_P) mod 𝔭T_{P,S} for P ∈ C(Ḡ) not properly contained in a cyclic subgroup, 𝔭 the maximal ideal of ℤ_p[μ_p] (Proposition 97); (12) ζ_P ≡ Σ_{P′}ϕ(ζ_{P′}) mod T_{P,S} over P′ ≠ P with P′^p = P, when such P′ exist (Proposition 98); (13) ζ_P ≡ ϕ(ζ_{P′}) mod T_{P,N_ḠP′,S} for P′^p = P ≠ P′, and (14) ζ_0 ≡ ϕ(ζ_{1}) mod p|Ḡ| (Proposition 99).
hypotheses: F_∞/F is admissible with μ = 0 and p odd; Gal(F_∞/F) = Δ × G with Δ cyclic of order prime to p and G a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group; Z ≤ G is central open pro-cyclic, Ḡ = G/Z, U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ, F_P = F_∞^{Δ×U_P}, d_P = [F_P : F], r_P = [F_P : ℚ], Σ_P the primes of F_P above Σ, and ζ_P the Deligne–Ribet p-adic zeta function of the abelian extension with group Δ × U_P^ab (Notations 91).
proofSteps: Each congruence reduces to a value congruence (basic-congruence-reduction), and the value congruences hold (basic-congruence-values).
acceptance: These are the additive congruences that the Deligne–Ribet method reaches; M4 is multiplicative and is assembled from them in m4-from-basic-congruences.

sources.match: Propositions 96–99 and the remark that (10) is M3.

nodes.title: The auxiliary extension F̃_∞ and the trace-ideal bound
nodes.statement: Choose a prime l ≡ 1 mod |Ḡ| with ℚ(μ_l) ∩ F_∞ = ℚ, let K ⊆ ℚ(μ_l) have degree |Ḡ| over ℚ, and put F̃ = KF, F̃_∞ = F̃F_∞. Then Gal(F̃_∞/F) = H̃ × Δ × G with H̃ cyclic of order |Ḡ|, and G̃/Z ≅ H̃ × Δ × Ḡ. For P ∈ C(G̃) let i_P = max{[P′ : P] : P ⊆ P′ ∈ C(G̃)}. If P ≠ {1} then T_P ⊆ p·i_P²·Λ(Δ × U_P), and T_{1} = |G̃|Λ(Δ × Z); the same holds for T_{P,S} and T̂_P (Lemma 118). The main conjecture for F̃_∞/F implies it for F_∞/F.
hypotheses: F_∞/F is admissible with μ = 0 and p odd; Gal(F_∞/F) = Δ × G with Δ cyclic of order prime to p and G a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group; Z ≤ G is central open pro-cyclic, Ḡ = G/Z, U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ, F_P = F_∞^{Δ×U_P}, d_P = [F_P : F], r_P = [F_P : ℚ], Σ_P the primes of F_P above Σ, and ζ_P the Deligne–Ribet p-adic zeta function of the abelian extension with group Δ × U_P^ab (Notations 91).
proofSteps: Case P ⊆ H̃: i_P = [H̃ : P] and N_{G̃}P = G̃ acts trivially on Λ(Δ × U_P), so T_P = [G̃ : P]Λ = |Ḡ|[H̃ : P]Λ ⊆ p·i_P²Λ since |Ḡ| ≥ p·i_P.
Case P ⊄ H̃: P = ⟨(h̃, h)⟩ with h ≠ 1; for P′ = ⟨(h̃₀, h₀)⟩ realising i_P, H̃ × ⟨h₀⟩ ⊆ N_{G̃}P acts trivially, so T_P ⊆ (|H̃||⟨h₀⟩|/|P|)Λ = |H̃|i_PΛ ⊆ p·i_P²Λ as |H̃| ≥ p·i_P.

Admissibility and μ = 0 for F̃_∞, which the source asserts without argument (E10): K is totally real because |Ḡ| is odd and divides (l − 1)/2, and μ = 0 passes from F_∞ to the finite p-extension F̃_∞ (the vanishing of μ is inherited by finite p-extensions, a theorem of Iwasawa, cited here).
Descent: MC for F̃_∞/F gives MC for its quotient F_∞/F by the compatibility of ∂, C and interpolation with the quotient map (as in reduction-to-dimension-one).
acceptance: The descent along G̃ → G uses Fukaya–Kato's base change for C, recorded in the gap on Fukaya–Kato.

sources.match: The trick of §6.13, the field F̃_∞ and Lemma 118 with its proof.

nodes.title: M4 from the basic congruences
nodes.statement: For the enlarged extension F̃_∞/F: for every P ∈ C(G̃) and 0 ≤ k ≤ p − 1, ζ_P − ω^k_P(ζ_P) ∈ 𝔭T_{P,S}/i_P, hence ζ_P^p/∏_kω^k_P(ζ_P) ∈ 1 + pT_{P,S}/i_P (Lemma 119); and the tuple (ζ_P) satisfies M4: ∏_{P′}ϕ(α_{P′}(ζ_{P′}))·(ζ_P^p/∏_kω^k_P(ζ_P))^{−1} ∈ 1 + pT_{P,S} for nontrivial P, and ∏_{P′}ϕ(α_{P′}(ζ_{P′}))·(ζ_{1}^p/ϕ(ζ_{1}))^{−1} ∈ 1 + pT_{{1},S} (§6.13.3).
hypotheses: F_∞/F is admissible with μ = 0 and p odd; Gal(F_∞/F) = Δ × G with Δ cyclic of order prime to p and G a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group; Z ≤ G is central open pro-cyclic, Ḡ = G/Z, U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ, F_P = F_∞^{Δ×U_P}, d_P = [F_P : F], r_P = [F_P : ℚ], Σ_P the primes of F_P above Σ, and ζ_P the Deligne–Ribet p-adic zeta function of the abelian extension with group Δ × U_P^ab (Notations 91).
Applied to F̃_∞/F (enlarged-extension).
proofSteps: Lemma 119 by reverse induction on |P|: for maximal cyclic P, i_P = 1 and (11) applies; otherwise (12) gives ζ_P − ω^k_P(ζ_P) ≡ Σ_{P′}ϕ(ζ_{P′} − ω^k_{P′}(ζ_{P′})) mod 𝔭T_{P,S} (34), the induction hypothesis puts each term in ϕ(𝔭T_{P′,S}/i_{P′}), and ϕ(Σ_x xT_{P′,S}x^{−1}) ⊆ T_{P,S}/p with i_P = p·i_{P′}; Galois invariance over ℚ_p(μ_p)/ℚ_p upgrades 𝔭 to p.
log(ω^k_P(ζ_P)/ζ_P) ≡ 1 − ω^k_P(ζ_P)/ζ_P mod (pT̂_P/i_P)², so log(∏_kω^k_P(ζ_P)/ζ_P^p) ≡ (pζ_P − Σ_kω^k_P(ζ_P))/ζ_P, and (pT̂_P/i_P)² ⊆ pT̂_P by Lemma 118.

Using (34), log(∏ϕ(α_{P′}(ζ_{P′}))/(ζ_P^p/∏ω^k_P(ζ_P))) ≡ Σ_{P′}(pϕ(ζ_{P′}) − Σ_kω^k_P(ϕ(ζ_{P′})))(ζ_P − ϕ(ζ_{P′}))/(ζ_Pϕ(ζ_{P′})) mod pT̂_P; the first factor lies in pϕ(T̂_{P′}/i_{P′}) by Lemma 119 and the second in T̂_{P,N_{G̃}P′} by (13), so the sum lies in pT̂_P.
log : 1 + pT̂_P ≅ pT̂_P, and (1 + pT̂_P) ∩ (1 + pT_{P,S}/i_P) = 1 + pT_{P,S}.
For P = {1}: ∏_kω^k_{1}(ζ_{1}) = ζ_0 (Lemma 50 or interpolation), and (14) with T_{{1},S} = |G̃|Λ(Δ × Z)_S replaces ζ_0 by ϕ(ζ_{1}).
acceptance: The printed computation has a misprint recorded as E9 (ω^k_P(ζ_{P′}) for ω^k_P(ϕ(ζ_{P′})) in the second line on p. 89).

nodes.title: The abelian zeta functions satisfy M1–M4
nodes.statement: For the enlarged extension F̃_∞/F, the tuple (ζ_P)_{P≤G̃/Z} lies in Φ^{G̃}_S: it satisfies M1 and M2 (Proposition 95), M3 (Proposition 96) and M4 (§6.13) — Theorem 94 for F̃_∞/F. Hence MC(F̃_∞/F) holds by the congruence criterion (Proposition 93).
hypotheses: F_∞/F is admissible with μ = 0 and p odd; Gal(F_∞/F) = Δ × G with Δ cyclic of order prime to p and G a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group; Z ≤ G is central open pro-cyclic, Ḡ = G/Z, U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ, F_P = F_∞^{Δ×U_P}, d_P = [F_P : F], r_P = [F_P : ℚ], Σ_P the primes of F_P above Σ, and ζ_P the Deligne–Ribet p-adic zeta function of the abelian extension with group Δ × U_P^ab (Notations 91).
proofSteps: M1 and M2: zeta-tuple-m1-m2. M3: basic-congruences (10). M4: m4-from-basic-congruences.
Proposition 93 (main-conjecture-congruence-criterion) turns (ζ_P) ∈ Φ^{G̃}_S into MC(F̃_∞/F).
acceptance: Theorem 94 is stated for F_∞/F but proved for F̃_∞/F; F_∞/F is reached by descent (enlarged-extension).

sources.match: Theorem 94 (M1–M4, whose M4 display is a quotient, as the page image shows) and its proof assembled in §§6.2–6.13.

nodes.title: The main conjecture for totally real fields (Kakde)
nodes.statement: Let p be odd and F_∞/F an admissible p-adic Lie extension satisfying μ = 0, with G = Gal(F_∞/F). There is a unique ζ(F_∞/F) ∈ K′₁(Λ(G)_S) with ∂(ζ(F_∞/F)) = −[C(F_∞/F)] and ζ(F_∞/F)(ρκ^r_F) = L_Σ(ρ, 1 − r) for every Artin character ρ of G and every r ≥ 1 divisible by [F_∞(μ_p) : F_∞] (Theorem 11). That is, MC(F_∞/F) of NE.5/totally-real-main-conjecture holds.
hypotheses: p odd; F_∞/F admissible; μ = 0 (Definition 8, known when F_∞ is abelian over ℚ by Ferrero–Washington).
proofSteps: Reduce to dimension one (reduction-to-dimension-one), then to ℚ_p-elementary groups (reduction-to-qp-elementary).
The l-ℚ_p-elementary case for l ≠ p is l-elementary-case; the p-ℚ_p-elementary case reduces to Δ × G_p with G_p one-dimensional pro-p (reduction-to-p-elementary).

For Δ × G_p: MC holds for the enlarged extension (zeta-tuple-in-phi), hence for F_∞/F (enlarged-extension). The K′₁-injectivity hypotheses of the reductions are k1-injects-localisation, and the ℚ_p[Δ]-coefficients are handled by main-algebraic-theorems with 𝒪 = ℤ_p[Δ].
Uniqueness: two solutions differ by an element of K′₁(Λ(G)) (∂ = 0 and Corollary 90) with trivial evaluations, which is 1 by the diagram chases of the reductions.
acceptance: This completes the Kakde route: every intermediate congruence and descent lemma of Kakde §§2–6 is a node, with Oliver's book, Fukaya–Kato §1, Deligne–Ribet and Wiles as cited inputs (gaps and requests). This meets NE.6's acceptance clause for one completed theorem.
Ritter–Weiss's independent route and the source-by-source coverage table remain.

nodes.title: Determinant functors on perfect complexes
nodes.statement: For any ring R there is a Picard category 𝒞_R and a determinant functor d_R : (C^p(R), quasi-isomorphisms) → 𝒞_R with the properties d)–i) of Burns–Venjakob: d_R(C) ≅ d_R(C′)d_R(C″) for short exact sequences (taken as identifications); a canonical 1_R → d_R(C) for acyclic C; d_R(C[r]) = d_R(C)^{(−1)^r}; factorisation through, and unique extension to, (D^p(R), isomorphisms); d_R(C) ≅ d_R(H(C)) ≅ ∏_i d_R(H^i(C))^{(−1)^i} when C is cohomologically perfect (Knudsen's description); and base change along bimodules Y finitely generated projective over R′. Aut_{𝒞_R}(1_R) = K_1(R). For regular R property d) does not extend to arbitrary triangles unless R is regular (Remark 2.1).
hypotheses: R an associative unital ring; C^p(R) bounded complexes of finitely generated projective left R-modules.
proofSteps: 𝒞_R is Deligne's category of virtual objects (the fundamental groupoid of the K-theory space of P(R)), and d_R sends a complex to the alternating product of its terms; Fukaya–Kato §1.2 and Knudsen give the construction.
Remark 2.3: for C = [P --φ--> P] the identification by the identity and the acyclicity isomorphism differ by d_R(φ)^{−1} ∈ K_1(R).
Remark 2.4: for a finite 𝒪-module A with a trivialisation from 0 → 𝒪^n → 𝒪^n → A → 0, the induced c ∈ L^× has ord_L(c) = length_𝒪(A), by elementary divisors.
acceptance: The construction is requested from GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.4, which owns C^p(R) and its K-theory; this node fixes the property list and conventions the Iwasawa-theoretic nodes use.

nodes.title: The localized K₁ of Fukaya and Kato
nodes.statement: For a full subcategory Σ of C^p(R) containing 0 and closed under quasi-isomorphism, shifts and direct sums ((i)–(iii), (iv′)), K_1(R, Σ) is the abelian group generated by symbols [C, a] with C ∈ Σ and a : 1_R → d_R(C), subject to [0, id] = 1, [C′, d_R(f)∘a] = [C, a] for quasi-isomorphisms f, [C, a] = [C′, a′][C″, a″] for short exact sequences in Σ, and [C[1], a^{−1}] = [C, a]^{−1} (Definition 2.5, after Fukaya–Kato). For a left denominator set S and Σ_S the complexes with R_S ⊗ C acyclic, [C, a] ↦ θ_{C,a} (the composite 1 → d(R_S ⊗ C) → 1) is an isomorphism ch_{R,Σ_S} : K_1(R, Σ_S) ≅ K_1(R_S) (Fukaya–Kato Proposition 1.3.7), and any Σ ⊆ Σ_S gives ch_{R,Σ} : K_1(R, Σ) → K_1(R_S).
hypotheses: R a ring; S a left denominator set; Σ as stated. When Σ satisfies (iv) (closure under extensions) the definition is Fukaya–Kato's.
proofSteps: Relation (3) follows from (0)–(2) (Remark 2.6).
ch_{R,Σ_S} is well defined because each relation is respected by base change to R_S and acyclicity; it is bijective by Fukaya–Kato Proposition 1.3.7 (see the gap on Fukaya–Kato).
acceptance: This supplies the NE.2 remaining item "the Fukaya–Kato localized K_1(R, Σ_S) ≅ K_1(R_S)"; the proof of bijectivity is cited to Fukaya–Kato.
For Σ_{A·} use the smallest subcategory with (i)–(iii) and (iv′) containing A·: the extension-closed version need not lie in Σ^{ss} (finding E11).

nodes.title: Bockstein homomorphisms
nodes.statement: Let θ ∈ H^1(G, ℤ_p) = Hom_cont(G, ℤ_p) be G ↠ Γ → ℤ_p with γ ↦ 1; it corresponds to the extension 0 → ℤ_p → E_θ → ℤ_p → 0 with E_θ = ℤ_p² and G acting by (1 θ; 0 1), which gives θ : A· → A·[1] in D^b(Λ(G)). The Bockstein morphism in degree i is B_i = H^{−i}(θ_*) : Tor_i^{Λ(G)}(T_ρ, A·) → Tor_{i−1}^{Λ(G)}(T_ρ, A·), with T_ρ = 𝒪^n a right module through ρ^t. For G = Γ, the triangle A· --T--> A· → ℤ_p ⊗^L A· gives 0 → H^i(A·)_Γ … exact sequences (3), and B_i is the composite H_i(Γ, A·) → H^{−i+1}(A·)^Γ --κ--> H^{−i+1}(A·)_Γ → H_{i−1}(Γ, A·), with κ induced by the identity (Lemma 3.1); so (H_·(Γ, A·), B_·) is a complex (4).
hypotheses: G is a compact p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H and Γ = G/H ≅ ℤ_p, with a fixed generator γ and T = γ − 1; ρ : G → GL_n(𝒪) is continuous, 𝒪 = 𝒪_L for L/ℚ_p finite.
proofSteps: E_θ ∈ Ext^1_{Λ(G)}(ℤ_p, ℤ_p) ≅ H^1(G, ℤ_p) (NSW 5.2.14); tensoring A· with it gives the triangle defining θ.

Lemma 3.1: with cone(A·) = cone(T) and the quasi-isomorphism π : cone(A·) → A·_0, θ is (a, b) ↦ (b, 0) (Schneider); for a cycle ā lift to (a, b) with b = −T^{−1}d(a), and the class maps to −T^{−1}d(a), which is the stated composite.
acceptance: The mapping-cone sign convention is BV's: d_cone = (d_B f; 0 −d_A).

sources.match: §3.1, the definition of θ and B_i; §3.2, the cone, the sequences (3) and Lemma 3.1.

nodes.title: Semisimple complexes and the order r(ρ)
nodes.statement: A· ∈ C^p(Λ(Γ)) is semisimple if the Bockstein complex (H_·(Γ, A·), B_·) has ℤ_p-torsion (hence finite) cohomology; Σ^{ss} is the full subcategory of such complexes, and r_Γ(A·) = Σ_i (−1)^{i+1} dim_{ℚ_p}(H^i(A·)^Γ ⊗ ℚ_p) (Definition 3.2). Semisimple complexes have Λ(Γ)-torsion cohomology, and A· ∈ Σ^{ss} iff κ_i ⊗ ℚ_p is bijective in every degree, in which case r_Γ(A·) = Σ(−1)^{i+1} dim H^i(A·)_Γ ⊗ ℚ_p (Remark 3.3). For general G: A· is semisimple at ρ if (H_·(G, A·(ρ^*)), B_·) has ℤ_p-torsion cohomology (Definition 3.11), finite at ρ if H_·(G, A·(ρ^*)) is ℤ_p-torsion (Definition 3.12, so Σ^{fin−ρ} ⊆ Σ^{ss−ρ}), and r_G(A·)(ρ) = Σ(−1)^{i+1} dim_L(H^i(H, A·(ρ^*))^Γ ⊗ L). A· is semisimple at ρ iff A·_ρ = (Λ_𝒪(Γ) ⊗ 𝒪^n) ⊗^L A· is semisimple, with the same Bockstein maps and r_G(A·)(ρ) = r_Γ(A·_ρ) (Lemma 3.13). Over a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer T, a semisimple complex is a finite direct sum of [R --1--> R] and [R --T--> R] (Lemma 3.9).
hypotheses: G is a compact p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H and Γ = G/H ≅ ℤ_p, with a fixed generator γ and T = γ − 1; ρ : G → GL_n(𝒪) is continuous, 𝒪 = 𝒪_L for L/ℚ_p finite.
proofSteps: Remark 3.3(ii): Lemma 3.1 gives 0 → cok(κ_{−i}) → ker B_i/im B_{i+1} → ker(κ_{−i+1}) → 0.
Lemma 3.9: T kills H^·(A·); split off [R^d --H--> R^d] with H diagonal in {1, T} from the top degree and induct on length.
Lemma 3.13: 𝒪^n ⊗^L_{Λ(G)} A· ≅ 𝒪 ⊗^L_{Λ_𝒪(Γ)} A·_ρ, and Λ_𝒪(Γ) ⊗^L_{Λ(G)} A· ≅ 𝒪 ⊗^L_{Λ(H)} A·; the Bockstein map is functorial.
acceptance: Σ^{ss} and Σ^{ss−ρ} satisfy (i)–(iii) and (iv′) but not (iv): they are not closed under extensions (finding E11).

nodes.title: The Bockstein trivialisation t(A·)
nodes.statement: For A· ∈ Σ^{ss}, t(A·) : d_{ℤ_p}(ℤ_p ⊗^L_{Λ(Γ)} A·)_{ℚ_p} ≅ d((H_·(Γ, A·), 0))_{ℚ_p} = d((H_·(Γ, A·), B_·))_{ℚ_p} ≅ 1_{ℚ_p}, using property h) and then e) for the acyclic rational Bockstein complex (Definition 3.4, (5)). If ℚ_p ⊗^L A· is already acyclic, t(A·) is the acyclicity trivialisation (Remark 3.5). For an exact triangle A· → B· → C· of semisimple complexes, r_Γ(B·) = r_Γ(A·) + r_Γ(C·) and t(B·) = t(A·)t(C·) (Lemma 3.6). For general G, t(A·(ρ^*)) is the same composite (7) for 𝒪 ⊗^L_{Λ_𝒪(G)} A·(ρ^*), equal to t(A·_ρ) (Lemma 3.13).
hypotheses: G is a compact p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H and Γ = G/H ≅ ℤ_p, with a fixed generator γ and T = γ − 1; ρ : G → GL_n(𝒪) is continuous, 𝒪 = 𝒪_L for L/ℚ_p finite.
proofSteps: Definition: the rational Bockstein complex is acyclic by semisimplicity, so e) trivialises it; h) identifies ℤ_p ⊗^L A· with its cohomology complex.
Lemma 3.6 ("easy and left to the reader" in the source): the long exact sequence of the triangle is compatible with the Bockstein maps, so the alternating determinants multiply; ranks add.
Lemma 3.13(iii) transports Lemma 3.6 along A· ↦ A·_ρ.
acceptance: Lemma 3.6 is stated without proof in the source; the proof step above is a sketch to be completed.

nodes.title: The leading term at a representation
nodes.statement: For A· ∈ Σ^{ss−ρ} and a : 1_{Λ(G)} → d_{Λ(G)}(A·), the leading term (A·, a)^*(ρ) ∈ L^× is (−1)^{r_G(A·)(ρ)} times the element of L^× ≅ K_1(L) ≅ Aut(1_L) given by 1_L --L^n ⊗ a--> d_L(L^n ⊗^L_{Λ(G)} A·) --t(A·(ρ^*))--> 1_L (Definition 3.14; for G = Γ and ρ = ρ_triv, Definition 3.7). It gives a homomorphism (−)^*(ρ) : K_1(Λ(G), Σ) → L^× on subcategories Σ ⊆ Σ^{ss−ρ} with (i)–(iii), (iv′). If A· ∈ Σ^{fin−ρ}, the leading term is the value [A·, a](ρ) in the sense of Fukaya–Kato 4.1.5 (Remark 3.15).
hypotheses: G is a compact p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H and Γ = G/H ≅ ℤ_p, with a fixed generator γ and T = γ − 1; ρ : G → GL_n(𝒪) is continuous, 𝒪 = 𝒪_L for L/ℚ_p finite.
proofSteps: Well defined on K_1(Λ(G), Σ): relations (1) and (2) are respected by Lemma 3.13(iii) and Lemma 3.6, relation (0) trivially.
Compatibility of Definitions 3.7 and 3.14 for G = Γ, ρ = ρ_triv is immediate.
acceptance: The acceptance case: A· = [R --T--> R] with a_ε from ε ∈ R^× has leading term ε(0) and order r = −1; its shift [R --T--> R][1] has order +1 and leading term ε(0)^{−1} (a vanishing case with its Bockstein determinant); [R --f--> R] with f(0) ≠ 0 is finite at ρ_triv with value f(0)^{±1} (a nonvanishing scalar specialisation).
BV define (−)^*(ρ) on K_1(Λ(G), Σ_{A·}) and claim Σ_{A·} ⊆ Σ^{ss−ρ}; that inclusion fails for the extension-closed Σ_{A·} (E11), so the domain is taken with (iv′).

nodes.title: Leading terms as leading coefficients of characteristic series
nodes.statement: Let L = [A·, a] with A· ∈ Σ^{ss} for G = Γ, and ch_Γ : K_1(Λ(Γ), Σ^{ss}) → K_1(Q(Γ)) = Q(Γ)^×. Writing F = T^rG(T) with G(0) ∈ L^× (6), (i) r(ch_Γ(L)) = r_Γ(A·), and (ii) (−)^*(ρ_triv) = (−)^*(0) ∘ ch_Γ, where F^*(0) = G(0) (Proposition 3.8). The same holds with 𝒪, L, Λ_𝒪(Γ) and Q_𝒪(Γ) (Remark 3.10).
hypotheses: G is a compact p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H and Γ = G/H ≅ ℤ_p, with a fixed generator γ and T = γ − 1; ρ : G → GL_n(𝒪) is continuous, 𝒪 = 𝒪_L for L/ℚ_p finite.
proofSteps: Both maps factor through the localisation R = Λ(Γ)_𝔭 at the augmentation ideal, a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer T and residue field ℚ_p, and K_1(R, Ξ) for the semisimple complexes Ξ over R.
Lemma 3.9 reduces to A· = [R --a--> R] with a = 1 or T; the acyclic case is trivial.

For a = T and the trivialisation a_ε (ε ∈ R^×): ch_Γ(L_ε) = T^{−1}ε, so ch_Γ(L_ε)^*(0) = ε(0). The Bockstein B_1 is ℤ_p --(−1)--> ℤ_p, so the composite in the definition is ℚ_p --ε(0)--> ℚ_p --(B_1)^{−1} = −1--> ℚ_p, of determinant −ε(0); with r_Γ(A·) = −1 = r(ch_Γ(L_ε)) the sign (−1)^{−1} gives L_ε^*(ρ_triv) = ε(0).
acceptance: This is the acceptance example: order −1 with leading term ε(0).

sources.match: Proposition 3.8 with its proof via Lemma 3.9, and Remark 3.10.

nodes.title: Leading terms on the canonical localisation
nodes.statement: For A· ∈ Σ_{S*} ∩ Σ^{ss−ρ} and ch_{G,A·} : K_1(Λ(G), Σ_{A·}) → K_1(Λ(G)_{S*}), let ρ_* : K_1(Λ(G)_{S*}) → K_1(M_n(Q_𝒪(Γ))) ≅ Q_𝒪(Γ)^× be induced by g ↦ ρ(g)ḡ. Then (i) r_G(A·)(ρ) = r_Γ(A·_ρ) = r(ρ_*(ch_{G,A·}(A·))), and (ii) (−)^*(ρ) = (ρ_*(−))^*(0) ∘ ch_{G,A·} (Proposition 3.16). Accordingly F^*(ρ) := ρ_*(F)^*(0) for F ∈ K_1(Λ(G)_{S*}), and F(ρ) := F^*(ρ) when r(ρ_*(F)) = 0.
hypotheses: G is a compact p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H and Γ = G/H ≅ ℤ_p, with a fixed generator γ and T = γ − 1; ρ : G → GL_n(𝒪) is continuous, 𝒪 = 𝒪_L for L/ℚ_p finite.
S, S* the canonical Ore sets of CFKSV.
proofSteps: (i) from Lemma 3.13(i), H_i(H, A·(ρ^*)) = H^{−i}(A·_ρ), and Proposition 3.8.
(ii) by composing the square (Λ_𝒪(Γ) ⊗ 𝒪^n) ⊗ − over ch with the square of Proposition 3.8, as in Fukaya–Kato Lemma 4.3.10.
acceptance: F(ρ) agrees with CFKSV's evaluation at ρ (NE.3/artin-evaluation) when r = 0.
The domain K_1(Λ(G), Σ_{A·}) is taken with (iv′), as in leading-term (E11).

sources.match: The canonical Ore sets, ch_{G,A·}, ρ_* and Proposition 3.16 with its proof.

nodes.title: Leading terms as derivatives in the cyclotomic direction
nodes.statement: Fix χ : G ↠ Γ → ℤ_p^× of infinite order, c_{χ,γ} = log_p(χ(γ)) ∈ ℚ_p^×, L = [A·, a] with A· ∈ Σ_{S*}, f_ρ(T) = ρ_*(ch_{G,A·}(L)) ∈ Q_𝒪(Γ)^×, and f_L(ρχ^s) = f_ρ(χ(γ)^s − 1), a p-adic meromorphic function of s ∈ ℤ_p. With r = r_G(A·)(ρ): (i) near 0, L^*(ρχ^s) = L(ρχ^s) = f_L(ρχ^s) for s ≠ 0; (ii) c_{χ,γ}^r L^*(ρ) is the leading coefficient at s = 0 of f_L(ρχ^s); (iii) if r ≥ 0, c_{χ,γ}^r L^*(ρ) = (1/r!)(d^r/ds^r) f_L(ρχ^s)|_{s=0} (Lemma 3.17). For χ = χ_cyc this is partial derivation in the cyclotomic direction (Remark 3.18).
hypotheses: G is a compact p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H and Γ = G/H ≅ ℤ_p, with a fixed generator γ and T = γ − 1; ρ : G → GL_n(𝒪) is continuous, 𝒪 = 𝒪_L for L/ℚ_p finite.
proofSteps: Near 0, f_{ρχ^s}(0) ∈ L^× for s ≠ 0 and f_{ρχ^s}(T) = f_ρ(χ(γ)^s(T + 1) − 1), so Proposition 3.16 gives (i).
Factor f_ρ = T^rG_ρ with G_ρ(0) = f_ρ^*(0); then f_ρ(χ(γ)^s − 1)/s^r = ((χ(γ)^s − 1)/s)^rG_ρ(χ(γ)^s − 1) → log_p(χ(γ))^rG_ρ(0).
acceptance: For r < 0 only the leading-coefficient statement (ii) holds.

sources.match: Lemma 3.17 with its proof and Remark 3.18.

nodes.title: Generalized Euler–Poincaré characteristics
nodes.statement: For A· ∈ Σ^{ss−ρ}, put H^i_B(G, −) = H^i((H_{−·}(G, −), B_{−·})), χ_add(G, A·(ρ^*)) = Σ_i (−1)^i length_𝒪 H^i_B(G, A·(ρ^*)) and χ_mult = (#κ_L)^{χ_add}. For any trivialisation a and L = [A·, a]: χ_add(G, A·(ρ^*)) = ord_L(L^*(ρ)) and χ_mult(G, A·(ρ^*)) = |L^*(ρ)|_p^{−[L:ℚ_p]} (Proposition 3.19). The Pontryagin dual of the Hochschild–Serre differentials used by Coates–Schneider–Sujatha and others is the Bockstein map, and when A·(ρ^*) ⊗ ℚ_p is acyclic this recovers CFKSV Theorem 3.6, Venjakob Proposition 6.3 and Fukaya–Kato Remark 4.1.13 (Remark 3.20).
hypotheses: G is a compact p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H and Γ = G/H ≅ ℤ_p, with a fixed generator γ and T = γ − 1; ρ : G → GL_n(𝒪) is continuous, 𝒪 = 𝒪_L for L/ℚ_p finite.
proofSteps: Lemma 3.13, property h) and regularity of 𝒪 give 1_𝒪 → d_𝒪(𝒪^n ⊗^L A·) ≅ ∏_i d_𝒪(H^i_B(G, A·(ρ^*)))^{(−1)^i}.
After ⊗L and acyclicity, the leading term is, modulo 𝒪^×, the product of the elements attached to the finite modules H^i_B, whose valuations are their lengths (Remark 2.4).
acceptance: This is the "nonvanishing scalar specialisation" of the acceptance when A· is finite at ρ: the value's valuation is the Euler characteristic.

nodes.title: The Fukaya–Kato global zeta isomorphism (as a proposition)
nodes.statement: For p odd, U = Spec ℤ[1/S] with S ⊇ {p, ∞}, a motive M over ℚ with a G_ℚ-stable lattice T_p of M_p, F_∞/ℚ a p-adic Lie extension with G = Gal(F_∞/ℚ), and 𝕋 = Λ(G) ⊗ T_p with the diagonal action g(x ⊗ y) = xḡ^{−1} ⊗ gy: the conjecture (Fukaya–Kato 2.3.2) asserts a unique isomorphism ζ_Λ(M) : 1_Λ → d_Λ(RΓ_c(U, 𝕋))^{−1} in 𝒞_Λ whose base change along every motivic ρ : G → GL_n(𝒪_λ) is the composite of ζ_K(M(ρ^*))_{K_λ} : 1 → Δ_K(M(ρ^*))_{K_λ} with the p-adic period-regulator ϑ_λ, where ζ_K(M(ρ^*)) is the isomorphism matching L^*_K(M(ρ^*)) through the period-regulator ϑ_∞ on the fundamental line Δ_K(M) = d(H^0_f(M))^{−1}d(H^1_f(M))d(H^0_f(M^*(1))^*)d(H^1_f(M^*(1))^*)^{−1}d(M_B^+)d(t_M)^{−1} (Conjecture 4.1). It implies the equivariant Tamagawa number conjecture of Burns–Flach. This is a proposition; no node assumes it.
hypotheses: p odd; the finiteness of motivic cohomology, ϑ_∞ and ϑ_λ are themselves conjectural inputs (standard conjectures).
proofSteps: Definitions only: RΓ_c(U, 𝕋) is perfect over Λ(G) (Fukaya–Kato; NE.4), and the base change is property i) of the determinant functor.
acceptance: Stated as a proposition with explicit conjectural inputs, like NE.5's conjectures; BV §§5–6 prove interpolation formulas for its leading terms (next checkpoint).

sources.match: §§4.1–4.3: compactly supported cohomology, the fundamental line, the period-regulators, and Conjecture 4.1 (Fukaya–Kato 2.3.2).

nodes.title: Descent for the Tate motive at ρ under Leopoldt (BV Lemma 5.1)
nodes.statement: Fix ρ ∈ R_{ℂ_p}(Ḡ) with Leopoldt's conjecture valid at ρ, i.e. (ℚ_p ⊗ ker λ_p)^ρ = 0 for λ_p : O_E[1/p]^× ⊗ ℤ_p → ∏_{w|p}E_w^× ⊗̂ ℤ_p. (i) (H^i_c(U, 𝕋_E) ⊗ ℚ_p)^ρ is (cok λ_p ⊗ ℚ_p)^ρ for i = 2, (ℚ_p)^ρ for i = 3, and 0 otherwise. (ii) RΓ_c(U, 𝕋) ∈ Σ_{ss−ρ} and r_G(RΓ_c(U, 𝕋))(ρ) = ⟨ρ, 1⟩ = dim_{ℂ_p}(ℚ_p)^ρ. (iii) Under (i), the Bockstein morphism (B²)^ρ : H²_c → H³_c is induced by log_{p,γ,E} : ∏_{w|p}E_w^× ⊗̂ ℤ_p → ℤ_p, (e_w) ↦ −Σ_w c_γ^{−1}log_p(N_{E_w/ℚ_p}(e_w)).
hypotheses: p odd; F_∞/ℚ totally real Galois, containing ℚ_cyc, unramified outside a finite set S ∋ p, with G = Gal(F_∞/ℚ) a compact p-adic Lie group, H = Gal(F_∞/ℚ_cyc), Γ = G/H; E ⊆ F_∞ finite over ℚ with E ∩ ℚ_cyc = ℚ and E_w ∩ ℚ_{p,cyc} = ℚ_p for w | p (condition (15)); Ḡ = Gal(E/ℚ); 𝕋 = Λ(G) with σ acting by multiplication by χ_cyc(σ̄)σ̄^{−1}; U = Spec ℤ[1/S]; c_γ = c_{χ_cyc,γ}.
proofSteps: (i): the triangle RΓ_c(U, 𝕋_E) → RΓ(U, 𝕋_E) → ⊕_{ℓ∈S}RΓ(ℚ_ℓ, 𝕋_E) with H^i(O_E[1/S], ℤ_p(1)) and H^i(E_w, ℤ_p(1)); H²_c ⊗ ℚ_p ≅ cok λ_p ⊗ ℚ_p always, and (H¹_c ⊗ ℚ_p)^ρ = 0 iff (ker λ_p ⊗ ℚ_p)^ρ = 0 since E is totally real.
(ii): (15) gives Gal(E_cyc/ℚ) ≅ Γ × Ḡ; RΓ_c(U, 𝕋)_ρ ≅ O^n ⊗ RΓ_c(U, 𝕋_{E_cyc}) (18), and Lemma 3.13 with the semisimplicity criterion of Remark 3.3(ii).
(iii): compare the global Bockstein with the local ones B¹_w through the triangle, then with B¹_p on RΓ(ℚ_{p,cyc}, ℤ_p(1)), which is c_γ^{−1}·log_p.
acceptance: Check the trivial character ρ = 1 with E = ℚ: ⟨1, 1⟩ = 1, cok λ_p = (ℚ_p^× ⊗̂ ℤ_p)/⟨p⟩ ≅ 1 + pℤ_p, so cok λ_p ⊗ ℚ_p ≅ ℚ_p via log_p, and the Bockstein is −c_γ^{−1}log_p.

sources.match: Leopoldt's conjecture as injectivity of λ_p, and Lemma 5.1.

nodes.title: The p-adic Stark conjecture at s = 1 (Serre; BV Conjecture 5.2)
nodes.statement: For ρ ∈ R_{ℂ_p}(Ḡ), let L_{p,S}(s, ρ) be Greenberg's S-truncated p-adic Artin L-function (L_{p,S}(n, ρ) = L_S(n, ρω^{n−1}) for n < 0) and L^*_{p,S}(1, ρ) := lim_{s→1}(s − 1)^{⟨ρ,1⟩}L_{p,S}(s, ρ). Let μ_∞ : ℂ ⊗ log_∞(O_E^×) ≅ ℂ ⊗ E₀ (E₀ the trace-zero part of E) and μ_p : ℚ_p ⊗ log_∞(O_E^×) ≅ ℚ_p ⊗ E₀ the maps induced by exp_∞ followed by λ_p and log_p (19). The conjecture P-Stark(ρ) asserts that L^*_{p,S}(1, ρ) is the leading term of L_{p,S}(s, ρ) at s = 1 and, for every ℚ[Ḡ]-isomorphism g : E₀ → O_E^× ⊗ ℚ, L^*_{p,S}(1, ρ)/det_{ℂ_p}((ℂ_p ⊗ μ_p) ∘ (ℂ_p ⊗ g))^ρ = L^*_S(1, ρ)/det_ℂ(μ_∞ ∘ (ℂ ⊗ g))^ρ, the two sides compared through a fixed j : ℂ_p ≅ ℂ.
hypotheses: p odd; F_∞/ℚ totally real Galois, containing ℚ_cyc, unramified outside a finite set S ∋ p, with G = Gal(F_∞/ℚ) a compact p-adic Lie group, H = Gal(F_∞/ℚ_cyc), Γ = G/H; E ⊆ F_∞ finite over ℚ with E ∩ ℚ_cyc = ℚ and E_w ∩ ℚ_{p,cyc} = ℚ_p for w | p (condition (15)); Ḡ = Gal(E/ℚ); 𝕋 = Λ(G) with σ acting by multiplication by χ_cyc(σ̄)σ̄^{−1}; U = Spec ℤ[1/S]; c_γ = c_{χ_cyc,γ}.
A fixed isomorphism j : ℂ_p ≅ ℂ.
proofSteps: Well-definedness: log_∞(O_E^×) is a lattice in ℝ ⊗ E₀ (Dirichlet), so μ_∞ is an isomorphism; (19) factors through ℚ_p ⊗ E₀, so μ_p is an isomorphism under Leopoldt.
Independence of g: changing g multiplies both determinants by the same algebraic number det(ℚ ⊗ h)^ρ.
acceptance: Check that Remark 5.3's point is recorded: Tate's formulation (Chapter VI §5) is imprecise about "log U" and μ_p, and BV's statement is the clarification.

sources.match: Greenberg's L_{p,S}, the maps μ_∞, μ_p and Conjecture 5.2.

nodes.title: The p-adic Stark conjecture for permutation characters (BV Remark 5.4, after Colmez)
nodes.statement: For a subgroup J ⊆ Ḡ and ρ = Ind_J^{Ḡ}1_J, P-Stark(ρ) holds iff the residue at s = 1 of the p-adic zeta function of E^J is nonzero and equal to 2^{[E^J:ℚ]−1}hR_p e_p/√|d|, with e_p = ∏_{v|p}(1 − Nv^{−1}); by Colmez this holds iff Leopoldt's conjecture holds for E^J. Leopoldt for E implies it for every E^J.
hypotheses: p odd; F_∞/ℚ totally real Galois, containing ℚ_cyc, unramified outside a finite set S ∋ p, with G = Gal(F_∞/ℚ) a compact p-adic Lie group, H = Gal(F_∞/ℚ_cyc), Γ = G/H; E ⊆ F_∞ finite over ℚ with E ∩ ℚ_cyc = ℚ and E_w ∩ ℚ_{p,cyc} = ℚ_p for w | p (condition (15)); Ḡ = Gal(E/ℚ); 𝕋 = Λ(G) with σ acting by multiplication by χ_cyc(σ̄)σ̄^{−1}; U = Spec ℤ[1/S]; c_γ = c_{χ_cyc,γ}.
proofSteps: Inductivity of L-functions reduces ρ = Ind 1_J to the Dedekind and p-adic zeta functions of E^J; the complex side is the analytic class number formula (AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4).
Colmez 1988 (the p-adic class number formula for totally real fields; cited, requested from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3).
acceptance: Check E^J = ℚ: the formula reduces to Res_{s=1}ζ_p(s) = 1 − 1/p (Kubota–Leopoldt).

sources.match: Remark 5.4 (with Tate's remark p. 138 and Colmez).

nodes.title: Interpolation formula for the Tate motive (BV Theorem 5.5)
nodes.statement: If P-Stark(ρ) holds for all ρ ∈ R_{ℂ_p}(Ḡ), then for each ρ: RΓ_c(U, 𝕋) ∈ Σ_{ss−ρ}, r_G(RΓ_c(U, 𝕋))(ρ) = ⟨ρ, 1⟩, and c_γ^{⟨ρ,1⟩}·ζ_{Λ(G)}(𝕋)^*(ρ) = L^*_{p,S}(1, ρ) (20), where ζ_{Λ(G)}(𝕋) is the Fukaya–Kato zeta isomorphism for M = h⁰(Spec E)(1). By Lemma 3.17 the left side is the leading term at s = 0 of s ↦ f_𝓛(ρχ_cyc^s) for 𝓛 = [RΓ_c(U, 𝕋), ζ_{Λ(G)}(𝕋)].
hypotheses: p odd; F_∞/ℚ totally real Galois, containing ℚ_cyc, unramified outside a finite set S ∋ p, with G = Gal(F_∞/ℚ) a compact p-adic Lie group, H = Gal(F_∞/ℚ_cyc), Γ = G/H; E ⊆ F_∞ finite over ℚ with E ∩ ℚ_cyc = ℚ and E_w ∩ ℚ_{p,cyc} = ℚ_p for w | p (condition (15)); Ḡ = Gal(E/ℚ); 𝕋 = Λ(G) with σ acting by multiplication by χ_cyc(σ̄)σ̄^{−1}; U = Spec ℤ[1/S]; c_γ = c_{χ_cyc,γ}.
The Fukaya–Kato isomorphism ζ_{Λ(G)}(𝕋) (Conjecture 4.1) is assumed to exist.
proofSteps: P-Stark implies Leopoldt for E (padic-stark-permutation-case), so Lemma 5.1(ii) gives the semisimplicity and the rank.

For M = h⁰(Spec E)(1): H¹_f(M) = O_E^× ⊗ ℚ, H⁰_f(M^*(1)) = ℚ, t_M = E and the other terms vanish; ζ_K(M([ρ]^*))_{K_λ} is the composite (21) (multiplication by L^*_S(1, ρ), the regulator sequence (22), Lemma 5.1(i) with the p-adic logarithm (23)).
t(RΓ_c(U, 𝕋)(ρ^*)) is the composite (24) with −c_γ^{−1}log_{p,γ,E} (Lemma 5.1(iii)); the sign (−1)^{⟨ρ,1⟩} of Definition 3.14 cancels the −1 of the trace diagram, giving (25).
The correction factor ξ equals det(μ_p ∘ g)^ρ/det(μ_∞ ∘ g)^ρ (26), and P-Stark turns (25) into (20).
acceptance: Check the trivial character: (20) says c_γ·ζ_{Λ(G)}(𝕋)^*(1) is the residue of ζ_{p,S} at s = 1, the Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic class number formula for ℚ.
Check the leading-term interpretation (Remark 5.6): both sides are leading terms of p-adic meromorphic functions, at s = 1 and s = 0 respectively.

nodes.title: The interpolation formula for ℚ-rational characters under Leopoldt (BV Corollary 5.7, corrected scope)
nodes.statement: If Leopoldt's conjecture holds for E at p, then for every ℚ-valued character ρ of Ḡ there is n_ρ ≥ 1 with (c_γ^{⟨ρ,1⟩}·ζ_{Λ(G)}(𝕋)^*(ρ))^{n_ρ} = L^*_{p,S}(1, ρ)^{n_ρ}; for a permutation character one can take n_ρ = 1. (BV state this for "ℚ_p-rational" characters; the proof covers ℚ-valued ones, see NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa/E12.)
hypotheses: p odd; F_∞/ℚ totally real Galois, containing ℚ_cyc, unramified outside a finite set S ∋ p, with G = Gal(F_∞/ℚ) a compact p-adic Lie group, H = Gal(F_∞/ℚ_cyc), Γ = G/H; E ⊆ F_∞ finite over ℚ with E ∩ ℚ_cyc = ℚ and E_w ∩ ℚ_{p,cyc} = ℚ_p for w | p (condition (15)); Ḡ = Gal(E/ℚ); 𝕋 = Λ(G) with σ acting by multiplication by χ_cyc(σ̄)σ̄^{−1}; U = Spec ℤ[1/S]; c_γ = c_{χ_cyc,γ}.
Leopoldt's conjecture for E at p; the Fukaya–Kato isomorphism exists.
proofSteps: Artin's induction theorem: for ℚ-valued ρ, n_ρ·ρ = Σ_H n_H·Ind_H^{Ḡ}1_H with integers n_H (Tate, Chapitre II, Théorème 1.2).
Both sides of (20) are additive and inductive in ρ; padic-stark-permutation-case (via Colmez) gives (20) for each Ind_H 1_H under Leopoldt.
acceptance: Check the scope: the permutation characters Ind_H 1_H are ℚ-valued, so only ℚ-valued n_ρ·ρ are ℤ-combinations of them; a ℚ_p-valued cubic character (p ≡ 1 mod 3) is not.

sources.match: Corollary 5.7 and its proof by Artin induction.

nodes.title: The local ε-isomorphism ε_{p,L}(V) and Fukaya–Kato's local conjecture (BV §6.1, Conjecture 6.1)
nodes.statement: Fix t = (t_n) a generator of ℤ_p(1) and ψ_p : ℚ_p → Q̄_p^× with kernel ℤ_p, 1/p^n ↦ t_n. For a de Rham L-representation V of G_{ℚ_p}, with L̃ = Q̂_p^nr ⊗ L, Γ^*(j) = Γ(j) = (j − 1)! for j > 0 and Res_{s=j}Γ(s) = (−1)^j((−j)!)^{−1} for j ≤ 0, h(j) = dim_L gr^jD_dR(V) and Γ_L(V) = ∏_j Γ^*(j)^{−h(−j)}, ε_{p,L}(V) : 1_{L̃} → (d_L(RΓ(ℚ_p, V))d_L(V))_{L̃} is the product of Γ_L(V), η_l(V)·η_l(V^*(1))^* and Fukaya–Kato's ε_dR(V) : 1 → d(V)d(D_dR(V))^{−1} (which involves Deligne's ε(D_pst(V))). Conjecture 6.1 (Fukaya–Kato 3.4.3): for 𝕋 = Λ ⊗ T there is a unique ε_{p,Λ}(𝕋) : 1_{Λ̃} → (d_Λ(RΓ(ℚ_p, 𝕋))d_Λ(𝕋))_{Λ̃} (Λ̃ = W(F̄_p)⟦G⟧) whose base change along each ρ : G → GL_n(O) is ε_{p,L}(T(ρ^*)).
hypotheses: L/ℚ_p finite; V de Rham; the Haar measure and t are fixed and suppressed.
proofSteps: Definitions; ε_dR(V) exists by Fukaya–Kato Proposition 3.3.5 (cited, source not freely available).

nodes.title: Dabrowski–Panchishkin representations and their Selmer complexes (BV §6.2, Lemma 6.2)
nodes.statement: A representation W of G_ℚ satisfies (DP) if it is de Rham and has a G_{ℚ_p}-subrepresentation Ŵ with D⁰_dR(Ŵ) = t_p(W) := D_dR(W)/D⁰_dR(W); then 0 → Ŵ → W → W̃ → 0 with D⁰_dR(Ŵ) = t_p(W̃) = 0, and Z = W^*(1) satisfies (DP) with Ẑ = W̃^*(1). The Selmer complexes SC_U(Ŵ, W) and SC(Ŵ, W) are the mapping fibres of RΓ(U, W) → RΓ(ℚ_p, W/Ŵ) ⊕ ⊕_{ℓ∈S_f∖S_p}RΓ(ℚ_ℓ, W) (resp. RΓ_{/f}(ℚ_ℓ, W) with RΓ_{/f} = cone(RΓ_f → RΓ)). Conditions: (A1) P_ℓ(W, 1)P_ℓ(Z, 1) ≠ 0 for ℓ ∈ S_f ∖ S_p; (B1) P_p(W, 1)P_p(Z, 1) ≠ 0; (C1) P_p(W̃, 1)P_p(Z̃, 1) ≠ 0 (each with equivalent forms). Lemma 6.2: under (A1) the complexes at ℓ ≠ p are acyclic; under (C1), RΓ_{/f}(ℚ_p, X) ≅ RΓ(ℚ_p, X̃) and RΓ_f(ℚ_p, X) ≅ RΓ(ℚ_p, X̂); under both, SC_U(Ŵ, W) ≅ RΓ_f(ℚ, W).
hypotheses: W a finite-dimensional L-representation of G_{ℚ,S}; P_ℓ(V, u) = det(1 − φ_ℓu | V^{I_ℓ}) (ℓ ≠ p), det(1 − φ_pu | D_cris(V)) (ℓ = p), φ geometric Frobenius.
proofSteps: (A1): local duality and the Euler characteristic formula make RΓ(ℚ_ℓ, X) acyclic.
(C1): complexes of vector spaces are quasi-isomorphic to their cohomology, and RΓ(ℚ_p, X̂) ≅ RΓ_f(ℚ_p, X̂) ≅ RΓ_f(ℚ_p, X) (Fukaya–Kato 4.1.7); compare the two triangles.
(iii) from (i), (ii) and the definitions.
acceptance: Check Example 6.3: for an abelian variety A/ℚ with good ordinary reduction at p, W = V_p(A)(ρ^*) satisfies (DP), (A1), (B1), (C1); with split multiplicative reduction (B1) fails.

nodes.title: Nekovář's p-adic height as a Bockstein map; semisimplicity iff non-degenerate (BV §6.2, Propositions 6.4, 6.6)
nodes.statement: Nekovář's height h_p(W) : H¹_f(ℚ, W) × H¹_f(ℚ, Z) → L (his h̃_{π,1,1}, agreeing up to sign with Schneider, Perrin-Riou, Mazur–Tate and Zarhin) has adjoint equal to H¹_f(ℚ, W) ≅ H¹(SC_U) →^B H²(SC_U) ≅ H²_f(ℚ, W) ≅ H¹_f(ℚ, Z)^* with B the Bockstein of SC_U(𝕋̂_{cyc,ρ}, 𝕋_{cyc,ρ}) (32)–(33). Descent (Proposition 6.4, Fukaya–Kato 1.6.5): L_n ⊗_{Λ,ρ} commutes with RΓ(U, ·), RΓ_c(U, ·), RΓ(ℚ_ℓ, ·) and SC_U, and with RΓ_f(ℚ_ℓ, ·) for ℓ ∉ Υ ∪ S_p, while SC descends only up to the triangle (34) over ℓ ∈ Υ. Proposition 6.6: under (A1), (C1) and (D2), SC_U(𝕋̂_{cyc,ρ}, 𝕋_{cyc,ρ}) ∈ Σ_ss iff h_p(W) is non-degenerate (F), and then r_Γ = dim_L H¹_f(ℚ, W).
hypotheses: W = N_λ = V ⊗ [ρ]^*_λ for a motive M satisfying (DP) and a critical twist; (D2): H⁰_f(ℚ, W) = H⁰_f(ℚ, Z) = 0; Υ the primes ℓ ≠ p of infinite ramification in F_∞.
proofSteps: (32)–(33): Nekovář, Selmer Complexes, the sentence after (11.1.3.2) and Theorem 11.3.9 (cited, gap).
Proposition 6.6: under (D2), H^i(SC_U(Ŵ, W)) = 0 for i ≠ 1, 2, and semisimplicity is the invertibility of the Bockstein in degree 1, which is (F).
acceptance: Check Example 6.5: for an abelian variety over ℚ, (D1) and (D2) hold, but non-degeneracy (F) is open except Bertrand's CM result.

sources.match: The Bockstein description of the height, descent, and Proposition 6.6.

nodes.title: Interpolation formula for critical motives (BV Theorem 6.7)
nodes.statement: Assume W satisfies (A1), (B1), (C1), (D1) and (F), and that ζ_Λ(M) (Conjecture 4.1) and ε_{p,Λ}(𝕋̂) (Conjecture 6.1) exist. Then SC_U(𝕋̂, 𝕋) and SC(𝕋̂, 𝕋) belong to Σ_ss, r = r_G(SC_U)(ρ) = r_G(SC)(ρ) = dim_L H¹_f(ℚ, W), and the leading term 𝓛^*(ρ) (resp. 𝓛_U^*(ρ)) of the Fukaya–Kato p-adic L-function equals (−1)^r·L^*_{K,B}(M(ρ^*))/(Ω_∞(M(ρ^*))R_∞(M(ρ^*)))·Ω_p(M(ρ^*))R_p(M(ρ^*))·Γ(V̂)^{−1}·P_{L,p}(Ŵ^*(1), 1)/P_{L,p}(Ŵ, 1) (38), with L^*_{K,B} truncated at B = Υ ∪ S_p (resp. B = S ∖ S_∞), Ω_∞, R_∞ the archimedean period and regulator (42)–(43), Ω_p the p-adic period (46) and R_p = det h_p(W) (50).
hypotheses: The hypotheses of height-pairing-bockstein and of Fukaya–Kato's Conjectures 4.1 and 6.1.
proofSteps: Model: Fukaya–Kato Theorem 4.2.26 (as amplified by Venjakob, proof of Theorem 6.4). Choose good bases γ, δ of M_B^+ and t_M and bases P^∨, P of H¹_f(N), H¹_f(N^*(1)); can = can_{γ′,δ′}·can_{P^∨,P} identifies ζ_K(N) with L^*_K(M)/(Ω_∞R_∞)·can.

𝓛_U^*(ρ) is the product of the factors (44)–(50): the complex leading term over Ω_∞R_∞; Γ_L(Ŵ)^{−1}; the p-adic period Ω_p; the Euler factors at ℓ ≠ p; {P_{L,p}(W, u)P_{L,p}(Ŵ, u)^{−1}}_{u=1}; P_{L,p}(Ŵ^*(1), 1); and the p-adic regulator R_p = det h_p(W), which is t(SC_U(ρ^*)) by height-pairing-bockstein.

requests.need: The completed group algebras Λ(G) = ℤ_p⟦G⟧ = lim ℤ_p[G/U] and Ω(G) = F_p⟦G⟧ for arbitrary (nonabelian) profinite G as compact topological rings, with the quotient maps φ_J : Λ(G) → Λ(G/J), ψ_J : Λ(G) → Ω(G/J), the augmentation, the maps Λ(H) → Λ(G) for closed subgroups H (restriction/induction), O-coefficients, and the universal property for compact modules with a continuous G-action. RS-16 assigns this construction to L1.
The power-series coordinate Λ(Γ) ≅ ℤ_p⟦T⟧ (γ ↦ 1 + T) for Γ ≅ ℤ_p, and Ω(Γ) ≅ F_p⟦T⟧, from Tau Ceti's completedGroupAlgebra (ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 9).

The category C^p(R) of bounded complexes of finitely generated projective modules over a (noncommutative) ring R with quasi-isomorphisms and degreewise split cofibrations, as K.4 states for the Gillet–Waldhausen comparison; NE.1 defines the subcategory Σ_S of it.

Quillen's localisation sequence for a (noncommutative) Ore localisation A → S⁻¹A by nonzero divisors: K₁(A) → K₁(S⁻¹A) → K₀(S-torsion modules of projective dimension ≤ 1) → K₀(A) → K₀(S⁻¹A), with the connecting map ∂[s] = [A/As] for s ∈ S (Swan, Grayson).

The resolution theorem: for a noetherian ring of finite global dimension, K₀ of finitely generated projectives equals G₀ of finitely generated modules, and the corresponding statement for Serre subcategories; lifting of idempotents modulo a complete ideal.

Characteristic power series/ideals of finitely generated torsion Λ(Γ)-modules with the structure theorem up to pseudo-isomorphism. Also the norm of characteristic series under Λ_𝒪(Γ) → Λ(Γ) (Bourbaki VII §4.8, Prop. 18).
Morita invariance K_i(M_n(A)) ≅ K_i(A) (i = 0, 1), compatible with the connecting maps of the localisation sequence, and K₁(F) = F^× via the determinant for a field F.

For a finitely generated torsion Λ_𝒪(Γ)-module N with characteristic series f_N: N has finite Γ-Euler characteristic iff f_N(0) ≠ 0, and then χ(Γ, N) = |f_N(0)|_p^{−[L:ℚ_p]}; for G with G/H = Γ, the Hochschild–Serre formula χ(G, W) = ∏_i χ(Γ, H_i(H, W))^{(−1)^i} (CFKSV (44), after Coates–Schneider–Sujatha).

Selmer groups of an elliptic curve over algebraic extensions L/ℚ, 𝒮(E/L) = ker(H¹(L, E_{p^∞}) → Π_w H¹(L_w, E)), their Pontryagin duals X(E/L) with the Λ(Gal(L/F))-action, and the restriction maps between layers (CFKSV §5); later, the Poitou–Tate duality behind equivariant Selmer complexes (NE.4). Also: the cohomological dimension and weak Leopoldt inputs for H²(Gal(F_Σ/F_∞), ℚ_p/ℤ_p) = 0 in the complex C(F_∞/F) (cohomological-dimension-bound is cited).

The Deligne–Ribet (Cassou-Noguès, Barsky) p-adic L-functions G_ψ ∈ 𝒪_ψ⟦T⟧ of a totally real field and the pseudomeasure ζ ∈ Q(Λ(H × Γ)) for H finite abelian, with the interpolation G_ψ(u^n − 1) = L_Σ(ψ, 1 − n) and G₁(u^n − 1)/(u^n − 1) = L_Σ(1, 1 − n) (Kakde §3).
Wiles's main conjecture for totally real fields at odd p (Annals 1990, Theorems 1.3–1.4): h_ψ(T) and G*_ψ(T) generate the same ideal, and μ_ψ = 0 when p ∤ #Gal(F_ψ/F).
Brauer's induction theorem, for the p-adic L-functions of nonabelian Artin characters and for interpolation in the reductions (Kakde §§3–4).

Clifford's dichotomy for a normal subgroup A (Serre, Linear representations of finite groups, Proposition 24: an irreducible ρ either restricts to an isotypic representation of A or is induced from a proper subgroup containing A), and its consequence that irreducible representations of supersolvable, in particular finite p-, groups are monomial (Serre, Theorem 16). Kakde's Lemma 92 and Proposition 93 use both.

Inductivity of Σ-truncated Artin L-functions, L_{Σ_K}(Ind_K^F ρ, s) = L_{Σ_F}(ρ, s) for Σ_K the primes of K above Σ, at the negative integers s = 1 − r, for the interpolation in Kakde §6.1 (Propositions 93 and 95).

The Deligne–Ribet toolkit behind Kakde §6: rationality and continuation of partial zeta values ζ(δ(x), 1 − k) (Klingen, Siegel); the Hilbert Eisenstein series G_{k,ε} with its standard q-expansion and constant terms at the cusps (Deligne–Ribet Proposition 6.1 and 2.22); the q-expansion principle (Deligne–Ribet 0.3, 5.13–5.15); and the congruences of Deligne–Ribet Theorem 0.4.

Greenberg's S-truncated p-adic Artin L-functions L_{p,S}(s, ρ) for totally real fields (Brauer induction from the Deligne–Ribet and Cassou-Noguès p-adic L-functions), with the interpolation L_{p,S}(n, ρ) = L_S(n, ρω^{n−1}) for n < 0; and Colmez's p-adic class number formula for the residue at s = 1 of the p-adic zeta function of a totally real field. Used for BV Conjecture 5.2 and Remark 5.4.

Nekovář's Selmer complexes as mapping fibres RΓ(U, W) → ⊕_v RΓ(ℚ_v, W)/U_v^+ with explicit local conditions (Greenberg-type at p), their base change along Λ → O^n and Nekovář's p-adic height pairing (Selmer Complexes §11) with its Bockstein description; used for BV §6.

Wall, Norms of units in group rings (Proc. London Math. Soc. 1974).

sourceIssues.printed: Σ is equal to smallest full subcategory Σ_{A·} of Cp(R) that contains A· and also satisﬁes the conditions (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) that are described above. (With this deﬁnition, it is easily seen that Σ_{A·} ⊂ Σ^{ss}).
sourceIssues.correction: Take Σ_{A·} to be the smallest full subcategory containing A· that satisfies (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv′) (closure under direct sums, not extensions). It lies in Σ^{ss−ρ} whenever A· does, and Definition 3.14 and Propositions 3.16–3.19 go through with this domain.
sourceIssues.reason: Σ^{ss} is not closed under extensions (the source itself notes it fails (iv), Remark 3.5). For R = Λ(Γ) and A· = [R --T--> R] (semisimple, the example in the proof of Proposition 3.8), B· = [R² --M--> R²] with M = ((T, 1), (0, T)) is an extension 0 → A· → B· → A· → 0, so B· ∈ Σ_{A·}; but H^0(B·) ≅ R/T², κ_0 : (R/T²)^Γ → (R/T²)_Γ is zero, and the Bockstein complex of B· is ℤ_p in degrees 0 and 1 with zero differential, so B· ∉ Σ^{ss}.
